The prophets had foretold that the Messiah would be most poor: A shoot will come out of the stump of Jesse, and a branch from its roots (Isa. 11:1); He shall grow up before Jehovah like a sapling, and like a root out of dry ground; he has no form or beauty, we saw him, and there was no appearance that we should desire him; he was despised, a man of sorrows, etc. (Isa. 53:2, 3). Jesus, looking to this and teaching the scribe about his poverty and his despised state, plainly likes to call himself the Son of man: The foxes, he said, have holes, and the birds of heaven have nests, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head (Matt. 8:20). When Christ himself performed the miracles by which the Messiah was to be made famous, as Isaiah had prophesied (Isa. 35:4–6), and when the disciples of John asked whether he was to come, he addressed the crowd under the title Son of man and so adorned himself (Matt. 11:5, 19). The prophets had foretold the sufferings of the Messiah, the kind and circumstances of his death (Ps. 22:17–19; Isa. 53:4–9). Jesus, foretelling his death on the cross, plainly calls himself the Son of man (Matt. 26:2; John 3:14). The prophets had prophesied that the Messiah would rise from the dead (Ps. 16:9–11; Isa. 53:10). Jesus, foretelling his own resurrection from the dead, marks himself with the title Son of man (Matt. 17:9). The prophets had foretold the burial of the Messiah (Isa. 53:9). Jesus, foretelling his burial, rejoices in the title Son of man: As Jonah was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights, so the Son of man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights (Matt. 12:40). The prophets foretold that the Messiah would ascend into heaven with triumphal pomp (Ps. 68:19). Jesus, when he speaks of his future ascension, again rejoices in the title Son of man: What then if you see the Son of man ascending where he was before? (John 6:62). The prophets had promised that the Messiah would sit at the right hand of God (Ps. 110:1). Jesus, when he forewarns of his future session at the right hand of God, commends himself by the title Son of man: Moreover I tell you, hereafter you will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of Majesty and coming on the clouds of heaven (Matt. 26:64; Mark 14:62; Luke 22:69). Hence it is most evident that Jesus constantly calls himself the Son of man wherever he teaches that whatever the prophets had foretold of Christ as momentous would be fulfilled in him; so one may rightly say that Christ and Son of man are truly synonymous names. Hence there is no cause for surprise that in the New Testament the name Son of man sometimes appears joined to Christ's sufferings and humble and despised state, and sometimes to his glory and majesty; for the holy prophets had foretold that the Son of man, or Christ, would of necessity come under a twofold state, namely of contempt and of glory, in alternating turns. Therefore those most learned men have strayed no less from the path of truth who have thought that the title Son of man aims solely at the humility and despised lot of Christ, than those who, falling into the opposite hyperbole, have thought it looks to the commending of the personal greatness and glory of Christ. Third, the foundation of our view is found in John 12:34, where the crowd of Jews, hearing that the Son of man was to be lifted up on the cross, replies in amazement: We have heard from the law that Christ remains for ever; how then do you say that the Son of man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of man? From which it is as easy to conclude as it is to see rain when it is raining that both Jesus and the crowd of Jews used Christ and Son of man for one and the same thing.

units.la: Tot illustribus testimoniis quibus efficitur filium hominis & Christum unum plane significare, unus obstare locus videtur, Mat. 16:13. τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι, τὸν υἱὸν τῦ ἀνθρώπου; quemnam me dicunt esse homines, filium hominis? discipulis vero respondentibus. Alii Iohannem Baptistam, alii vero Eliam, alii vero Ieremiam, aut unum ex Prophetis, pergit Iesus, vos autem quemnam me dicitis esse? Ad quem Simeon Petrus os Apostolorum, ut loquitur Chrysostomus σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τῦ θεῦ ζῶντος, tu es Christus, filius Dei viventis. Hinc colligi posse videtur, τὸν υἱὸν τῦ ἀνθρώπου non significare Christum, frustra enim videretur Iesus ab iis percunctatus, quemnam vos me dicitis esse? cum hac sua insigni appellatione filii hominis, se esse Christum eos docuisse, supponeretur. Respondemus, locum hunc nihil sententiæ nostræ incommodare, sed eam magis magisque roborare. Observare igitur licet ac lubet, sermonem Christi esse interrogativum, & in primo interrogationis commate, Iesum de sententia & opinione hominum de sese, duo rogare, generale alterum his verbis, quemnam me dicunt esse homines? id est, quam habent de me homines opinionem? qualem me esse existimant? particulare alterum his verbis τὸν υἱὸν τῦ ἀνθρώπου; filium hominis? id est, opinanturne me esse filium hominis? cum à discipulis propositis ambabus quæstionibus hocce tulisset responsum, alii Iohannem Baptistam, scilicet è mortuis excitaexcitatum : alii Eliam è cœlo delapsum; alii Ieremiam, aut unum ex Prophetis redivivum, dum Iesus repetita interrogatione, sententiam propriam rogat discipulos suos; Et vos qualem me dicitis esse? non repetit τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου; ut ostendat se non quaerere ab iis num credant se esse filium hominis, seu Christum, (hoc enim discipuli antea saepè confessi fuerant) credidimus & cognovimus te esse Christum filium Dei viventis, Ioh. 6:69. Quid ni enim confessi fuissent testes ἀποτόπῳ miraculosæ multiplicationis panum, cum vel ipsa Iudæorum multitudo, tanto perculsa miraculo, in hanc confessionem erupisset, iste est verè Propheta venturus in mundum, Ioh. 6:14. Conscius igitur Christus, persuasos discipulos suos se esse Christum, seu filium hominis, rogat quid sentiant de origine sua, vel de modo quo ipse esset Christus, an scilicet opinarentur se Messiam è vivis, an è mortuis duxisse originem, Iudæi enim persuasi de Messia venturo, penduli ambigebant de origine ac modo adventus ejus, num scilicet è vivis, num è mortuis oriundus foret, quaerit igitur Iesus, num ipsi conscii, & saepe saepius hactenus confessi, eum esse Messiam, de origine & modo adventus ejus, sicut & caeteri Iudæi, ambigerent. Reponunt igitur Discipuli ore Petri sui, se non modo persuasos, eum esse filium hominis, seu Christum, sed & sine ulla cunctatione de ejus origine modoque adventus persuasos, quod absque ambage hisce suæ confessionis ultimis verbis, ore rotundo pronunciant, tu es filius Dei viventis. Non credimus modo, te esse filium hominis, seu Christum, te verò aliquem esse è mortuis redivivum, ut sentiamus, absit, plane persuasi sumus te esse è vivente, vivum scilicet & æternum Dei viventis filium.
units.tr: Since so many clear testimonies show that "son of man" and "Christ" plainly mean one and the same thing, there seems to be one passage in the way, Matt. 16:13: Whom do men say that I, the Son of man, am? [τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι, τὸν υἱὸν τῦ ἀνθρώπου;] "Whom do men say that I am, the Son of man?" The disciples answered: Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, others Jeremiah or one of the prophets, and Jesus went on: But whom do you say that I am? Simon Peter, the mouth of the Apostles, as Chrysostom puts it, replied: You are Christ, the Son of the living God [σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τῦ θεῦ ζῶντος]. From this it seems we may conclude that the Son of man does not mean Christ. For Jesus would have asked the disciples in vain, "Whom do you say that I am?", if he had already taught them, by this distinctive title Son of man, that he himself was Christ. We reply that this passage does nothing to harm our view but rather strengthens it more and more. We may therefore observe, and it is worth observing, that Christ's speech is interrogative, and that in the first clause of the question Jesus asks two things about the opinion and judgment of men concerning himself: the first, general, in these words, "Whom do men say that I am?", that is, what opinion do men have of me, what do they think I am? The second, particular, in these words, the Son of man?, that is, do they think I am the Son of man? When the disciples had answered both questions, some saying John the Baptist, that is, raised from the dead, others Elijah come down from heaven, others Jeremiah or one of the prophets returned to life, Jesus, repeating the question, asks his disciples for their own judgment: But you, what do you say that I am? He does not repeat "the Son of man", thereby showing that he is not asking them whether they believe he is the Son of man, or Christ (for the disciples had often confessed this before): We have believed and know that you are Christ, the Son of the living God, John 6:69. Why should they not have confessed it, when they were witnesses of the astonishing [ἀποτόπῳ] miraculous multiplication of the loaves, and when the very multitude of the Jews, struck with so great a miracle, had burst out in this confession: This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world, John 6:14? Christ, therefore, knowing that his disciples were persuaded that he was Christ, or the Son of man, asks what they think about his origin, or about the manner in which he himself is Christ: whether, that is, they judged that the Messiah derived his origin from the living or from the dead. For the Jews, though persuaded of the Messiah who was to come, were uncertain and wavering about the origin and manner of his coming, whether he would be born of the living or would arise from the dead. Jesus therefore asks whether they too, who were aware and had so often confessed that he was the Messiah, were uncertain, as the other Jews were, about his origin and the manner of his coming. The disciples, therefore, through the mouth of their Peter, reply that they are not only persuaded that he is the Son of man, or Christ, but are also persuaded without any hesitation about his origin and the manner of his coming. They declare this plainly, without ambiguity, in the final words of their confession, with full voice: You are the Son of the living God. "We do not merely believe that you are the Son of man, or Christ, and that you are one who has risen from the dead (far be it from us to think so); we are fully persuaded that you are from the living, that is, the living and eternal Son of the living God."

units.la: USUS.
units.tr: USUS.

units.la: 1. Solemnis hæc Filii hominis nomenclatio, & Iesum verum fuisse hominem, & ex homine oriundum, juxta institutam de ipso Euangelistarum genealogiam, luculenter nos docet adversus Valentinum, ejusque asseclas Valentinianos, Marcionem ac Marcionitas, Appellem & Appellianos, novitiosque Anabaptistas. Marcionitæ autem veram Christi humanam naturam, dum negarunt. In phantasmate putative carnis, ut loquitur Tertullianus contra Marcionem, apparuisse in mundo, docere non erubuerunt. Unde δοκηταί dicti. Valentinus verò, Christum ex substantia beatæ virginis, verum corpus negabat assumpsisse: sed cœleste, seu spirituale corpus, per Mariam, veluti per canalem, seu fistulam percolatum, in mundum hunc visibilem produxisse docebat, unde Iesum non ex Maria, sed per Mariam natum afferebat. At Jesus fuit, estque etiamnum Filius hominis: est igitur & verus homo, factus ex muliere, nobis in omnibus similimus excepto peccato, & vere ex homine oriundus, particeps carnis & sanguinis, sicut pueri, ut per mortem aboleret eum qui imperium mortis obtinebat, id est, Diabolum, Hebr. 2:14.
units.tr: 1. This solemn designation, Son of man, clearly teaches us that Jesus was a true man, descended from a man according to the genealogy of him set out by the Evangelists. It refutes Valentinus and his followers, the Valentinians, Marcion and the Marcionites, Apelles and the Appellians, and the newer Anabaptists. The Marcionites, while they denied Christ's true human nature, did not hesitate to teach that he appeared in the world in a phantom of putative flesh, as Tertullian puts it against Marcion. Hence they were called Docetae [δοκηταί]. Valentinus taught that Christ did not assume a true body from the substance of the blessed virgin. He taught instead that a heavenly or spiritual body was brought through Mary, as through a channel or pipe, into this visible world. So he asserted that Jesus was born not of Mary but through Mary. But Jesus was, and still is, the Son of man. He is therefore a true man, made of a woman, in all things most like us except sin, and truly descended from a man: a partaker of flesh and blood, as the children are, so that through death he might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil, Heb. 2:14.

units.la: 2. Cum filius hominis homo sit necessario, idemque pariter & Christus, Propheta, Pontifex, Rexque orbis universi ac Ecclesiae, hic & hominis gloriam, & Dei φιλανθρωπίαν mirari subit: non Angelus, non Archangelus, hac eximia gaudet praerogativa: sed unus homo, quia Deus non fuit φιλάγγελος, sed φιλάνθρωπος esse voluit, ut hominem Deo rebellem & inimicum, amoris ac delitiarum vinculis alliceret in sui amorem. O stupendam Dei charitatem, quae vel ipsos Angelos in stuporem dat! anne adorandum Numen tua illa in hominem effusa bonitas, qua caeteris animantibus longe praestabat? anne tua providentia in eo sarto tectoque, ut ut rebelli conservando? anne coelestes pluviae tuae, tempestatesque fertiles, cibus ac gaudium, quibus corculum ejus recurrentibus indefessis vicissitudinibus exhilarasti? anne solis syderumque serenae luces, vividique influxus, cumulataque bonorum omne genus supellex, tuum illum rebellem in tui lucis vivificae amorem pellicere potuere, ni eum ad Christi tui gloriam eveheres, & vinculo aeternum haud dissolubili cum tuo Immanuele consociares? Plaudite mortalium genus, manibus date lilia plenis, Psallite, cantate exultantes, Deus est charitas. Vae ingrato homini! siquis Deum ter Opt. Max. φιλάνθρωπον, Charitatem, toto corde non dilexerit, anathema sit.
units.tr: 2. Since the Son of man is necessarily a man, and at the same time Christ, Prophet, High Priest, and King of the whole world and of the Church, here we are led to marvel both at the glory of man and at the loving-kindness [φιλανθρωπία] of God. Not an angel, not an archangel, enjoys this outstanding privilege, but one man. For God was not a lover of angels [φιλάγγελος] but a lover of man [φιλάνθρωπος], and wished to draw man, his rebel and enemy, into love for himself by the bonds of love and delight. O stupendous charity of God, which astonishes even the angels themselves! Was it not your goodness, poured out upon man, that made him far superior to the other living creatures, O adorable Deity? Was it not your providence that clothed and sheltered him, though he rebelled, and preserved him? Were it not for your heavenly rains and fruitful seasons, food and joy, with which you cheered his little heart through unfailing changes, and for the serene light of the sun and stars and their lifegiving influence, and the heaped-up store of every kind of good, could they have won your rebel to love of your life-giving light? Unless you had raised him to the glory of your Christ and joined him eternally to your Immanuel by a bond that cannot be dissolved? Applaud, race of mortals, give lilies with full hands, sing psalms, sing exultantly: God is love. Woe to ungrateful man! If anyone has not loved God, the best and greatest, the lover of man [φιλάνθρωπος], the Charity, with his whole heart, let him be anathema.

units.la: 3. Filium hominis, Deus gloria & honore coronavit, omnia pedibus ejus subjecit, Pf. 8:7. O eximiam humanae naturae sortem, O gloriosam hominis in Christo conditionem, heu quantum mutatus ab illo homine, cui datum & mox ereptum artibus diaboli in omnes creaturas infimas dominium! primus equidem homo ad imaginem Dei conditus fuit, sed mutabilem: verum filius hominis Christus; imago est Dei invisibilis, splendor gloriae Patris, & character impressus aeternae ὑποστάσεως Dei immutabilis. Primus homo dominium obtinuit in universum terrarum orbem: sed filius hominis Christus in omnes, nulla excepta, creaturas, infimas, medioxumas, supernas, Angelos ipsos dominatur, ἐξουσίαν & authoritatem ἀνεύθυνον exercet, in omnem carnem, ac mundum praesentem: sed & in mundum futurum. Ad gloriam Christi throno insidentis ipsi Seraphim obstupescunt, & facies alis ambabus obnubunt. Ponite tamen metum homines, quid fugis Petre, perculsus gloria Christi? quid clamas? discede à me Domine, sum enim homo peccator. Christus & homo est & filius hominis, sicut & nos homines & filii hominis. In Christo optimè conveniunt & in una sede morantur Majestas & amor. Christus majestatem, filius hominis spirat charitatem: at idemmet Christus est & filius hominis, filius hominis idemmet & Christus, hic majestas charitas est, hic charitas est majestas. Oportunum sanè in filio hominis Christo, fidei objectum, spei ac fiduciæ fulcrum. Hinc quia Christus homo est, quia filius hominis est, non Dæmonas, non Angelos; sed homines ac filios hominum ad sese vocat, ad vos viri clamo, & vox mea ad filios hominis, Prov.8:4. Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis & onerati estis, & ego vos reficiam, discite ex me quia mitis sum & corde humilis, & requiem invenietis animabus vestris, Matth. 11: 28. 29. Christus Propheta est, Pontifex, ac Rex, sed potens compati infirmitatibus nostris, tentatus per omnia ad similitudinem nostri absque peccato; est enim homo, est filius hominis sicut & nos. Adeamus ergo cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus, Hebr. 4:15. 16. O vos ignari viæ salutis & felicitatis homines, adite Christum, Prophetam, hominem, filiumque hominis, eum audite docentem arcana felicitatis, viamque Dei in veritate monstrantem sequimini. O vos reatu peccati, sordibusque impliciti homines, adite Christum Pontificem, filium hominis, factumque pro nobis peccatum, fecit enim per se ipsum peccatorum purgationem, purissimus ac preciosissimus ipsius sanguis, vestras eluet maculas, & vos ab omni labe peccati mundabit. O vos miseri, afflictionibus impetuque hostium imminentium conflictati, perculsi, prostrati, ad Christum Regem confugite; est enim filius hominis, tentatus malis omne genus ad similitudinem vestri: sed potens & volens, quia optimus juxta eo & maximus, vos ab omni malo liberare. Si quis ad gloriosum Christi nomen in genua non procubuerit: si quis filium hominis Christum non dilexerit; si quis fidem, fiduciam, spemque suam in eo non posuerit, anathema maranatha sit.
units.tr: 3. "God has crowned the Son of man with glory and honour, and put all things under his feet," Ps. 8:7. O the outstanding lot of human nature, O the glorious condition of man in Christ! Alas, how much changed from that man to whom dominion over all the lowest creatures was given, and soon taken away by the arts of the devil. The first man indeed was made in the image of God, but a changeable one. But Christ the Son of man is the invisible image of God, the brightness of the Father's glory, and the impressed character of the unchangeable substance [ὑποστάσεως] of God. The first man obtained dominion over the whole orb of the earth. But Christ the Son of man rules over all creatures without exception, lowest, middle, and highest, even the angels themselves. He exercises power [ἐξουσίαν] and an authority [ἀνεύθυνον] accountable to none, over all flesh and the present world, and also over the world to come. Before the glory of Christ seated on the throne, the Seraphim themselves are astounded and cover their faces with both wings. Yet do not be afraid, men. Why do you flee, Peter, struck by the glory of Christ? Why do you cry out, "Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man"? Christ is man and the Son of man, just as we are men and sons of men. In Christ majesty and love agree well and dwell in one seat. Christ breathes majesty; the Son of man breathes charity. And yet the same Christ is also the Son of man, and the same Son of man is also Christ. Here majesty is charity, and here charity is majesty. Surely in Christ, the Son of man, there is a most fitting object of faith and a support of hope and trust. Hence, because Christ is man, because he is the Son of man, he calls to himself not demons or angels, but men and sons of men: To you, O men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of men, Prov. 8:4. Come to me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you. Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart, and you will find rest for your souls, Matt. 11:28, 29. Christ is Prophet, Priest, and King, but he is able to sympathize with our infirmities, tempted in all things like us, without sin. For he is man, the Son of man, just as we are. Let us therefore draw near with confidence to the throne of his grace, Heb. 4:15, 16. O you men ignorant of the way of salvation and happiness, come to Christ, the Prophet, the man, and the Son of man. Hear him teaching the secrets of happiness, and follow him as he shows the way of God in truth. O you men entangled in the guilt of sin and its filth, come to Christ the High Priest, the Son of man, who was made sin for us. For by himself he made purification of sins, and his most pure and precious blood will wash away your stains and cleanse you from every stain of sin. O you wretched men, afflicted and struck down, prostrated by the attacks of the enemies that threaten you, flee to Christ the King. For he is the Son of man, tempted in every kind of evil like you, but powerful and willing, since he is the best and greatest, to free you from every evil. If anyone has not bowed his knees at the glorious name of Christ; if anyone has not loved Christ the Son of man; if anyone has not placed his faith, trust, and hope in him, let him be anathema maranatha.

units.la: 4. Cum filius hominis sit Christus, quanto in pretio homo sit habendus, luculenter docemur. Quid hominem spernis, homo superciliose, quem Deus tanto habuit in pretio, ut dilecto filio suo unione non solubili; super omnem principatum & potestatem, & omne nomen: quod & in hoc & in futuro nominatur sæculo, æternum consociare dignatus est? Quid hominem flocci facis, quem Deus fecit Dominum atque Christum? Non diffluit divitiis, non cingitur diademate, non pompa regali ad magnificentiam vestitur; lacera veste mendicus, retrimentum & opprobrium præ forma vili ac despicabili habetur. Esto. Quid vero tu ζόωον, quin potius ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὁ Υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου respicis? quin Deum tuum imitaris? qui hominem & filium hominis voluit esse Christum, non Prophetam eximium, non Pontificem lamina aurea gloriosum, non Regem splendida corona redimitum: sed hominem, filiumque hominis Christum, fecit Prophetam, Pontificem, ac Regem supremum.
units.tr: 4. Since the Son of man is Christ, we are taught clearly how highly man should be esteemed. Why do you despise man, arrogant man, whom God has so valued that he deigned to join him eternally to his beloved Son in an indissoluble union, above every principality and power and every name that is named, both in this age and in the age to come? Why do you think so little of man, whom God has made Lord and Christ? He does not overflow with riches, he is not girded with a diadem, he is not clothed in royal pomp and magnificence. A beggar in a torn garment, he is regarded as refuse and a reproach, in a cheap and contemptible form. Be it so. But why do you look to the animal [ζῷον], or rather to the man, the Son of man [ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου], and not imitate your God? He who wished Christ to be man and the Son of man, made him not an outstanding Prophet, not a High Priest glorious with a golden plate, not a King crowned with splendid diadem, but the supreme Prophet, Priest, and King, the man and Son of man, Christ.

units.la: 5. Cum filius hominis, homo scilicet ex homine oriundus, sit Christus, ad sanctificationem seu studium sanctitatis perpetuò invigilare, argumento omni exceptione majore docemur: in Christo enim, homo & filius hominis est Deo sanctificatus perpetua divinitatis praesentia, quae vero sua praesentia Deus dignari voluit, sancta fuere ac inviolabilia. Hinc sancta Bethel, porta coeli, ac domus Dei; hinc sanctus mons, ubi numen è rubo ardenti Mosem alloquitur: hinc sancta Hiericuntina terra, ubi Iosue praesentem oculis usurpat, principem exercituum Jehova: hinc sanctum tabernaculum ac templum: hinc vasa tabernaculi sancta: hinc populus Israel gens sancta. Quanto magis sanctus homo; quanto sanctior natura humana, quam in Christo praesenti divinitatis plenitudine, aeternum implevit numen sanctum? Quid tu peccator spurcissime, naturam humanam in Christo sanctissimam, mortuis peccati operibus, avaritia, quae idololatria est, luxuria, libidine, scortatione, adulterio, blasphemia, ac flagitiis omne genus violare, profanare, conspurcare non erubescis? si quis Dei templum violaverit, destruet eum Deus, Pharaonis filiam, dilectam uxorem suam, in aedibus Davidis Regis, non finit habitare Salomon, ne loca Sancta praesentia scilicet Numinis in arca, uxore Aegyptiaca, vel quavis alia muliebri spurcitie conspurcarentur, Uxor mea non habitabit in domo Davidis Regis Israel, quia ipsa Sancta quam ingressa est arca Iehova, 2. Chron. 8: 11. Quam Sanctior est humana natura, in quam ingressa divinitatis plenitudo in Christo filio hominis? Absit igitur ut caro vitiis mundi Aegypti spiritualis scatens ac praegnans, una habitet cum Sancto Dei filio in humana nostra natura, Deo Sacra, ac Sanctificata in Christo. Age igitur fidelis Schelomo, imitare consilium ac alloquium Sapientis Salomonis, dilectae carni tuae peccatrici, hunc mitte repudii libellum; non habitabit in corpore meo peccatum in quo habitat Sanctitas Christi; non supercilium, ubi humilitas: non odium, ubi charitas: non ingluvies & compotatio, ubi temperantia: non mendacium, ubi veritas; non fraus & fallacia, ubi intemerata sinceritas: non blasphemia, non impietas, ubi zeli fervor, & consummata pietas in Christo meo stabulatur. A page mundum, carnis, oculorum concupiscentiam, totam Aegyptum apage, arca & Dagon, lux & tenebrae, Christus & Belial non in una sede morantur. 6.
units.tr: 5. That the Son of man, a man born of man, is Christ, teaches us beyond any exception that we must be constantly vigilant for sanctification, that is, for the pursuit of holiness. For in Christ the man and Son of man is sanctified by God through the continual presence of the divinity, and those things in which God deigned to be present by his presence were holy and inviolable. Hence Bethel was holy, the gate of heaven and the house of God. Hence the mount was holy, where the Deity spoke to Moses from the burning bush. Hence the holy land of Jericho, where Joshua saw before his eyes Jehovah, the prince of the army. Hence the holy tabernacle and temple, hence the holy vessels of the tabernacle, hence the people of Israel, a holy nation. How much more holy is the holy man, and how much holier is human nature, which the holy Deity has eternally filled in Christ by the present fullness of divinity? Why, you most filthy sinner, are you not ashamed to violate, profane, and defile the human nature most holy in Christ, with the dead works of sin, with avarice, which is idolatry, with luxury, lust, fornication, adultery, blasphemy, and every kind of shameful deed? If anyone violates the temple of God, God will destroy him. Solomon did not allow Pharaoh's daughter, his beloved wife, to dwell in the house of King David, lest the holy places, namely the presence of the Deity in the ark, be defiled by an Egyptian wife or any other woman's filth. My wife shall not dwell in the house of David, King of Israel, because the places into which the ark of the Lord has entered are holy, 2 Chron. 8:11. How much holier is human nature, into which the fullness of divinity has entered in Christ the Son of man? Far be it, then, that the flesh, teeming and pregnant with the spiritual vices of the world of Egypt, should dwell together with the holy Son of God in our human nature, which is sacred and sanctified to God in Christ. Come then, faithful Solomon, imitate the counsel and speech of the wise Solomon. To your beloved, sinful flesh, send this bill of divorce: sin shall not dwell in my body, in which the holiness of Christ dwells. Pride does not dwell where humility is, hatred where charity is, gluttony and drunkenness where temperance is, lying where truth is, fraud and deceit where unspoiled sincerity is, blasphemy and impiety where the fervour of zeal and perfect piety abide in my Christ. Away with the world, the flesh, the lust of the eyes, away with all Egypt. The ark and Dagon, light and darkness, Christ and Belial do not dwell in one seat. 6.

units.la: 6. Quid miraris, filium hominis, modò cœli volucribus, vulpeculisque soli pauperiorem? modò cœli Angelis splendidiorem? orbis Regibus cunctis magnificentiorem? Quid miraris, filium hominis, modò e ligno maledicto crucis inter latrones pendulum? modò sedentem in throno excelso ad dexteram æternæ Majestatis, duobus Seraphim gloriæ stipatum ac collaudatum? deformem modò, & quovis mancipio vilissimo viliorem, servientem & accinctum ad probrosum ac ignominiosum usque obsequium crucis? modò pulcherrimum filiorum hominum multiplici diademate cinctum? Leges summis imperatoribus ac orbi universo sub isthoc glorioso lemmate Rex Regum, Dominusque dominantium, ferentem? Memento, filium hominis esse Christum, & Christum à Deo unctum in mediatorem, inter Deum & homines, ministrum circumcisionis, Prophetam, Pontificem ac Regem mundi redimendi. Quâ Mediator hominum apud Deum, vilis est ac despicabilis, quia vas & sponsor est probrosorum hominum: quâ Dei mediator apud homines, hominum pulcherrimus est, imago Dei invisibilis, & splendor gloriæ Patris: Qua Pontifex atque victima, morti maledictæ addicta, vile caput est, peccatum atque maledictio pro nobis: sed quatenus Rex judexque supremus orbis universi, gloriâ, honore, & majestate ἀνευθυνῶ coronatus. Cum filium hominis paupertate, miseriis, maledictione & morte probrosa conflictatum vides, sortem tuam reputa miselle peccator: At cum eundem conspicis, divitiis, potentiâ, ac majestate suprema conspicuum, inexhaustas puta, misericordiæ æternæ divitias, quibus te in Christo, Numen benignissimum mactare dignatum est, canito animitus: benedicito anima mea Domino, & quicquid in me est, benedicat nomini sanctitatis ejus: magnificat anima mea Dominum, & latatur in Deo servatore meo spiritus meus.
units.tr: 6. Why do you wonder that the Son of Man, who a moment ago was poorer than the birds of the air and the foxes, is now more splendid than the angels of heaven, and more magnificent than all the kings of the world? Why do you wonder that the Son of Man, who a moment ago hung on the cursed wood of the cross between thieves, is now seated on the lofty throne at the right hand of eternal Majesty, surrounded and praised by two Seraphim of glory? He was once disfigured and viler than any most worthless slave, serving and girded for the shameful and humiliating obedience of the cross, but now he is the most beautiful of the sons of men, crowned with many diadems. He rules the highest emperors and the whole world under this glorious title: King of kings and Lord of lords. Remember that the Son of Man is Christ, anointed by God as Mediator between God and men, minister of the circumcision, Prophet, Priest and King for the redemption of the world. As Mediator of men before God he is lowly and despised, because he is the vessel and surety of wretched men. As Mediator of God before men he is the most beautiful of men, the invisible image of God and the brightness of the Father's glory. As Priest and victim, given over to the cursed death, he is a base head, sin and a curse for us. But as the supreme King and Judge of the whole universe, he is crowned with glory, honour and majesty, [ἀνευθυνῶ, unaccountable]. When you see the Son of Man wrestling with poverty, miseries, curse and shameful death, consider your own lot, you wretched sinner. But when you see the same one shining with riches, power and supreme majesty, think of the inexhaustible riches of eternal mercy with which the most benevolent Godhead has deigned to bless you in Christ, and sing from your heart: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and let all that is in me bless his holy name. My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Saviour.

units.la: 7. Verum enim vero, filius hominis non foret Christus, ni idemmet pariter foret filius Dei: nec enim mundum, arcana salutis, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis unquam ascenderunt ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, homo merus, potis erat docere qua Propheta. Nec mundum Deo reconciliare, nec divinam justitiam placare, nec peccata in Majestatem infinitam expiare, λύζῳ sufficientissimo, Christus merus homo potuit: nec orbem universum regere, nec Ecclesiam efficaciter vocare e potestate tenebrarum in admirabilem Dei lucem, nec corda lapidea in carnea commutare, nec leges Dei, non atramento, sed spiritu Dei viventis, inscribere cordibus, nec mortuos in vitam denuò revocare, nec orbem universum sistere ad gloriosum suum tribunal, ac judicare, Christus merus homo potuit. Est igitur filius hominis Christus, quia & filius Dei est, in sæcula benedictus. Et tu quoque Ecclesia, fidelis cœtus, Christus es, 1. Cor. 12:12. Homines filios hominum Christum esse quipote? Quia sunt & filii Dei. Agedum quicunque gaudes Christi nomine, esto & filius Dei, ductum patere spiritu Dei; quotquot enim spiritu Dei ducuntur, filii Dei sunt, Rom.8: 14. sequere ducentem, audi loquentem, præbe te imperanti obsequiosum, imitare Dei Patris charitatem, misericordiam, justitiam, benignitatem, veracitatem, fidelitatem, patientiam, sanctitatem, & filius eris patris tui, qui est in cœlis, filius hominis, filius Dei, Christus, sicut & Christus tuus.
units.tr: 7. Indeed, the Son of Man would not be Christ unless he were also, at the same time, the Son of God. A mere man, homo merus [ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος], could not teach the mysteries of salvation, which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have they entered into the heart of man, as a prophet teaches them. A mere man could not reconcile the world to God, nor appease divine justice, nor expiate sins against infinite Majesty by a ransom [λύζῳ] fully sufficient. A mere man could not govern the whole world, nor effectually call the Church out of the power of darkness into the marvellous light of God, nor change hearts of stone into hearts of flesh, nor write the laws of God on hearts, not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, nor raise the dead to life again, nor bring the whole world before his glorious judgment seat and judge it. Therefore Christ is the Son of Man because he is also the Son of God, blessed for ever. And you too, Church, faithful assembly, are Christ, 1 Cor. 12:12. How could men, sons of men, be Christ? Because they are also sons of God. Come then, whoever rejoices in the name of Christ, be also a son of God by letting yourself be led by the Spirit of God, for as many as are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God, Rom. 8:14. Follow the one who leads you, hear the one who speaks, make yourself obedient to his commands, imitate the love, mercy, justice, kindness, truthfulness, faithfulness, patience and holiness of God the Father, and you will be a son of your Father who is in heaven, a son of man, a son of God, a Christ, just as your Christ is.

units.la: 8. Eò te ducit exemplum Christi, ipse enim in sæcula filius Dei benedictus, factus est in sæculorum consummatione filius hominis, Deus in carne manifestatus, factus ex muliere, ut foret tibi Christus, tibi nascitur-us, tibi moriturus, tibi è mortuis resurrecturus, tibi in cœlum ascensurus, tibi author ac consummator salutis futuræ. Eccur verò? Ipse tibi respondet, te dilexi amore æterno: & Paulus, Christus dilexit Ecclesiam. Dilectio æternum est vinculum, quod unione, vel ipsa morte crudelissima insolubili, filium Dei filio hominis copulavit. Hic verus est ille amor, quem penes est amantem in rem amatam transformare. Hic stupendus est vel ipsis Angelis amor, qui filium Dei in filium hominis meruit transformare. Tu verò peccator, miselle fili hominis, amorem imitare filii Dei, esto in omnibus similis filio Dei Christo tuo, sicut ille factus filius hominis, ductu amoris sui, in omnibus tibi fuit quam simillimus, & sicut unum non novit tuum, Christi similitudo, scilicet peccatum, unum est tantum, quod tua Christi imago imitari nescia est, infinitudo scilicet & independentia æterna naturæ ipsius. De cætero, transformator ad imaginem Christi tui de gloria in gloriam, perpetuus esto æmulus fidei, pietatis, fiduciæ, charitatis, humilitatis, patientiæ, castitatis, temperantiæ, fidelitatis, justitiæ, sanctitatis Christi tui, ad hoc vocati estis, quotquot de candido Christi nomine verè fideles censemini, quia Christus pro nobis passus est, vobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia ejus, 1. Pet. 2: 21. O Terque quaterque beatos, æmulos filii Dei fideles! Vos in conformitatem filii Dei, ut sit primogenitus inter multos fratres, prædestinatos, sors manet quam simillima sorti Christi, filii hominis ac filii Dei: nunc equidem filii Dei estis, sicut & filius hominis erat & filius Dei, dum versaretur in terris: sed nondum apparuit quicquid futuri estis, miseriis ac morti obnoxii; sed futuri mortis victores uti & Christus. Sperate fore, ut plenè declaremini filii Dei per resurrectionem è mortuis, futuri ipsi similes, quia ipsum videbitis sicuti est. Sperate, fore vos cœli compotes & currus splendidæ nubis in cœleste domicilium micilium evehendos, numeroso stipante Angelorum satellitio, gratulantibus vobis illustrem victoriam, palmas & coronas amaranthinas, omnibus coelicolis, applausu & jubilatione secunda, sicut & filio hominis Christo vestro, cui sit laus, honor & gloria, imperium, ac magnificentia, in seculorum saecula. Amen.
units.tr: 8. The example of Christ leads you there. For he who is blessed for ever as the Son of God was made, at the consummation of the ages, the Son of Man, God manifested in the flesh, made of a woman, so that he might be Christ for you: born for you, to die for you, to rise from the dead for you, to ascend into heaven for you, and to be for you the author and perfecter of future salvation. But why? He himself answers you: I have loved you with an everlasting love; and Paul: Christ loved the Church. Love is an eternal bond, which, by a union that not even the most cruel death could dissolve, joined the Son of God to the son of man. This is the true love, which has the power to transform the lover into the beloved. This is a love wonderful even to the angels, which deserved to transform the Son of God into a son of man. But you, sinner, wretched son of man, imitate the love of the Son of God, be in all things like the Son of God your Christ, just as he, by the impulse of his love, became the son of man and was in all things as like to you as possible. Only one thing does the likeness of your Christ not know: sin, which alone your Christ's image is unable to imitate, namely the infinity and eternal independence of his nature. For the rest, be transformed into the image of your Christ from glory to glory, and be an ever-zealous imitator of the faith, piety, trust, love, humility, patience, chastity, temperance, faithfulness, justice and holiness of your Christ. For to this you were called, all of you who are truly counted faithful in the honoured name of Christ, because Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow in his steps, 1 Pet. 2:21. O thrice and four times blessed, faithful imitators of the Son of God! You are being conformed to the image of the Son of God, so that he may be the firstborn among many brothers, and the lot that remains for you is most like the lot of Christ, Son of Man and Son of God. Now indeed you are sons of God, just as the Son of Man was also the Son of God while he lived on earth; but it has not yet appeared what you will be, subject to miseries and death, but you will be victors over death, as Christ also is. Hope that you will be fully declared sons of God by the resurrection from the dead, becoming like him, because you will see him as he is. Hope that you will be made partakers of heaven, and be carried in a chariot of splendid cloud into the heavenly dwelling, with a numerous retinue of angels attending, while all the inhabitants of heaven rejoice with you at your illustrious victory, with palms and amaranth crowns, with applause and joyful acclamation, as to your Christ, the Son of Man, to whom be praise, honour and glory, dominion and majesty, for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: QUÆSTIO II.
units.tr: QUESTION II.

units.la: Cur Jesus in Novo Instrumento se titulo Filii hominis passim insignire voluerit, ut eo se esse Messiam, seu Christum significaret?
units.tr: Why did Jesus so often wish to designate himself by the title Son of Man in the New Testament, signifying thereby that he is the Messiah, or Christ?

units.la: QUis temperet à lachrymis ruinam contuitus lamentabilem, quam mundo intulit Adam, Princeps generis humani? Abstergite lachrymas, facessat luctus, valeat moeror, exultate miserorum mortalium genus: Filius hominis est Christus, adorandus generis humani reparator, unctus in Regem & οἰκουμένης μελλόντης, mundi futuri, cujus sors tantò felicior, quantò Adam è coelo, Adamo è terra creto, dignitate, potentia, felicitate autecellit. O felix Adami culpa, quae tantum nobis meruit redemptorem! Homo nos perdidit: Filius hominis nos servavit: homo nobis amisit supremum, in omnes creaturas inferiores, pisces sali, volucres coeli, animantia soli, dominium. Filius hominis comparavit nobis regnum coelorum, dominiumque supremum in omnes creaturas, visibiles ac invisibiles, fecitque nos sedere cum ipso in excelsis, super omnem principatum & potestatem, & omne nomen, quod & in hoc saeculo & in futuro nominatur. Homo nos è paradiso terreno expulit, luctuosum in modum exules errantesque in terra maledicta, spinis armata, infertilibusque tribulis hispida ac horrida. Filius hominis nos in coelestem Paradisum intulit, fluvio deliciarum irriguum, arbore vitae amoenum, floribus immortalibus variegatum ac coronatum. Homo peccato, maledictione, miseriisque commeritis plenus, è lamentabili sua plenitudine peccatum, reatum, maledictionem ac mortem, miseriarum culmen, uti lethalis scaturigo in nos omnes derivavit. Filius hominis gratia plenus, & veritate, sapientiam, justitiam, sanctificationem, & redemptionem, benedictiones omne genus coelestes, vitae ac felicitatis fons perennans, nobis omniomnibus jugiter affundit, ac largitur, hausimus enim explenitudine ejus omnes, gratiam pro gratia, Joh. 1 : 16. Est enim filius hominis. Christus, unctus oleo laetitiae, ut ex pretioso illo, sibi, aliisque sufficientissimo capite unctio laetifica ad barbam, infimasque vestis fimbrias defluat ac corrivetur. Eccur vero haec filii hominis Nomenclatura, ad Christum nostrum indigetandum adhibita fuerit ab ipso sapientissimo Christo? Quaestio est ad perstringendum difficilis, nodusque vero vindice dignus.
units.tr: Who could refrain from tears at the lamentable ruin that Adam, the prince of the human race, brought upon the world? Wipe away your tears, let grief cease, let sorrow depart, rejoice, race of wretched mortals: the Son of Man is Christ, the adored restorer of the human race, anointed as King and [οἰκουμένης μελλόντης] of the world to come, whose lot is as much happier as he surpasses Adam in dignity, power and blessedness, Adam having been created from the earth and Christ from heaven. O happy fault of Adam, which earned us so great a Redeemer! Man ruined us; the Son of Man saved us. Man lost for us the supreme dominion over all lower creatures, the fish of the sea, the birds of the air, and the beasts of the field. The Son of Man has won for us the kingdom of heaven and supreme dominion over all creatures, visible and invisible, and has made us sit with him in the heavenly places, above every principality and power and every name that is named, both in this age and in the age to come. Man expelled us from the earthly paradise, so that we wandered as sorrowful exiles over a cursed land, armed with thorns and bristling with barren thistles. The Son of Man has brought us into the heavenly paradise, watered by a river of delights, pleasant with the tree of life, and adorned and crowned with immortal flowers. Man, full of sin, curse and deserved miseries, from his own wretched fullness poured out upon us all, as a deadly spring, sin, guilt, curse and death, the very height of misery. The Son of Man, full of grace and truth, pours out upon us all, and bestows without end, wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption, every kind of heavenly blessing, a fountain of life and happiness that never fails; for of his fullness we have all received, grace for grace, John 1:16. For he is the Son of Man, Christ, anointed with the oil of gladness, so that the joyful anointing flows down from that precious head, which is sufficient for himself and for others, upon the beard and to the lowest fringe of his garment. But why was this name Son of Man used by our most wise Christ himself to designate himself? The question is difficult to unravel, and the knot is truly worthy of a solution.

units.la: Proposita tamen quaestio cuivis ad solvendum quam facillima obtutu primo videtur, si cum viris doctis dixerit, se Jesum ea commendasse nomenclatura, quia Daniel Messiam hoc nomine insignierat, Dan. 7 : 13. ואריו עם ענני שמיא כבר אנוש אתה הוא Et ecce cum nubibus coeli tanquam filius hominis veniebat. Judaei fere omnes, iisque Rabbinorum doctissimi hunc locum de Messia interpretantur. Rabbi Ieschugnha referente Aben Esra in hunc locum Danielis ואמר רבי ישועה כי זה כבר אנש הוא המשיח Et dixit Rabbi Ieschugnha quod iste filius hominis est Messias. Rabbenou Sagnhadias illustris, quo titulo Judaei eximios & magni nominis Rabbinos insigniunt, in hunc locum Danielis, filium hominis interpretatur Messiam, non vilem illum & afflictum, quem vocant filium Josephi, sed illustrem alterum Messiam, quem vocant filium Davidis his verbis והו משיח צדקינו והלא כתוב על משיח עני ורוכב על חמור אלא יבוא בענוה כי לא יבוא על סוסים בגאות ואשר כתוב עם ענני שמיא והנה עם השמים הם מלאכי צבא השמים וו היא רוב הגדולה שיתן חבורא למשיח Hic est Messias justitia nostra, sed hoc non est scriptum de Messia afflicto & vehente super asino, quia venturus est in humilitate, quoniam non venturus est in pompa vehens super equis: sed scripsit cum nubibus coeli, & ecce cum nubibus coelorum, ipsi angeli exercitus coelorum intelliguntur, id est abundantia magnitudinis, quam creator daturus est Messiae, Rabbi Schelomo Jarki, in hunc locum Danielis כבר אנוש אתה sic commentatur הוא מלך משיח, hic est Rex Messias. Rabbi Joseph Jacchiades hunc locum Danielis sic interpretatur והוא משיח צדקני אשר ינין לפני ה׳. Hic est Messias justitia nostra qui perveniet in Dei conspectum. Hinc vero factum, ut Christus optime conscius, & Danielem vocasse Messiam Filium hominis, & Judaeos per Filium hominis Messiam intellexisse apud Danielem, hac se Filii hominis insignire nomenclatura voluerit. Verum animo veritatem inquirenti, & mysteria Evangelica indaganti paulo penficulatius, hac virorum undiquaque Doctorum responsione, non plene fit satis, ulterius enim scisscitari licet, 1°. Cur Daniel Messiam post debellatos hostes suos, orcum, Satana, peccatum, mortem, sepulchrum & mundum, pompa triumphali in coelum regnum suum venientem, בר אנש filium hominis aegritudine tudine laborantis nuncupare voluerit, quod prima fronte cum pompa regali ac triumphali Messiae parum convenire videtur. 2o. Cur Jesus rarum istum titulum & hac sua raritate (extat enim apud unum Danielem alterumve Prophetam ־ Ps.8:5.& 80:18.) paucis Judaeorum obvium, spretis aliis longe frequentioribus, longeque illustrioribus, tam crebro, tam sedulo, usurpare voluerit, sibique tribuere; cum solemne sit omnibus qui aliquid cognitum impendio cupiunt, ad id significandum non rara & fere inusitata sua raritate nomina: sed omnibus obvia, adhibere: quod cum sapientissimum Dominum nostrum haud fugeret: si quis Jesum absque deliberato consilio, tam constanter alios Messiae claros, obvios, neglexisse titulos, ut unum hunc ־ vel ־ rarum atque μονογεν in Veteri Instrumento, tam crebro tam constanter adhiberet; ut se esse Christum, seu Messiam, Judaeis significaret, illi sane, sanum esse syncipiut, non facile dixerim. Equidem si raro apud Prophetas Jesus titulo gaudebat, rara non ignorabat haec Messiae nomina אִישׁ יהוה Vir Iehova, Gen.4:1. אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה Vir bellator, seu illustris bellator, Ex.15:3. הַשָּׁרוֹן, Rosa, seu Lilium Saron, Cant.2:1. enim & Rosam & Lilium significat, a nomine שֵׁשׁ sex, quod ex sex foliis efflorescat. Mirum sane, quod singularem hunc titulum הַשָּׁרוֹן rosim, seu Lilium Saron non elegerit, eo enim significasset & locum nativitatis suae, spinis durarum afflictionum consitum, quia Saron regio est inter Caesaream Palestinae, & montem Tabor, lacumque Genezareth. Nazareth vero, ubi Christus, & in virgine conceptus, & multos annos fuit educatus, pars est tractus seu regionis Saron. Si vero Christus illustres amabat Messiae nomenclaturas: obvias sibi & aliis habebat פלא vel פלא Jud.13:18. Ef.9:6. שר צבא יהוה Principem exercitus Domini, Jof.5:14.15. שר שלום Principem pacis, Ef.9:6. דויד Davidem, Jer.30:9. Ezech.34:23.24. & cap.37:24.25. Hof.3:5. יהוה צדקנו Iehova justitiam nostram, Jer.23:6.& 33:16. Si vero nomina filiationem prae se ferentia, Christo erant in deliciis, cur non selegit eximia haec magisque obvia quam בן אדם vel בר אנוש, quibus Messiam Prophetae insignierant, nimirum semen Abrahami, Gen.22:18. semen Isaaci, Gen.26:4. semen Jacobi, Gen.28:14. semen Davidis 2 Sam.7:12. 1.Chron.17:11.12.13.14. Pf.132:11. Jer.23:5. filium Dei, Pf.2:6.7. Pf.89:27.28.29.30. Gemina haec Messiae nomenclatura filii nempe Davidis & filii Dei, ita erat Judaeis tempore Christi obvia, ut non pauci Messiam fore filium Davidis & filium Dei persuasi, Jesum hoc nomine compellaverint. Ita caeci, fili David, miserere nostri: Mat.9:27.& 20:30.31. Ita Judaeorum multitudo tudo ad Iesum venientem ingeminavit Hosanna Filio David: Math. 21: 9. & 22: 42. Et multi ex Iudaeis, Nonne scriptura dicit, Christum venturum ex semine David? Ioh. 7: 42. Ita Pharisaei Iesu quaerenti, cuiusnam Christus est filius? reponunt, David: Luc. 20: 41. Nec minus filium Dei Messiam nuncupant, ita Nathanael, tu es filius Dei, tu es Rex Israel; Ioh. 1: 49. ita qui erant in navigio venientes adoraverunt, dicentes, vere tu es filius Dei; Math. 14: 33. Ita summus pontifex, adjuro te per Deum viventem, ut dicas nobis, an tu sis Christus filius Dei: Mat. 26: 63. Mar. 14: 61. Mirum sane ac quaesitu dignissimum, cur Iesus verus ille Messias, neglectis fere illustribus illis filii Davidis, & filii Dei elogiis, quibus Numen ipsum, ac Prophetae, non semel Messiam ornaverant, & universa Iudaeorum natio etiamnum condecorabat, unum filii hominis elogium, quo unus Daniel semel, Dan. 7: 13. vel bis in totum Dan. 10: 16. Et Psalmographus Ps. 8: 5. & 80: 28. Messiam insignierant, tam sedulo, tam constanter sibi tribuere, habuerit in deliciis, ut nec se ipsum filium Davidis, nec filium Dei dixerit, nisi dum responderet Iudaeis inquirentibus, num esset Christus, filius Dei? Agedum rationem admirandae istius dispensationis, allucente nobis scriptura sacra, investigemus.
units.tr: Yet the question, once put, seems at first sight very easy to answer, if one says with learned men that Jesus commended this name because Daniel had designated the Messiah by it, Dan. 7:13: "Behold, one like the Son of Man came with the clouds of heaven." [ואריו עם ענני שמיא כבר אנוש אתה הוא]. Almost all the Jews, and the most learned of the rabbis, interpret this passage of the Messiah. Rabbi Ieschugnha, as reported by Aben Ezra on this passage of Daniel, says: "Rabbi Ieschugnha said that this Son of Man is the Messiah." [ואמר רבי ישועה כי זה כבר אנש הוא המשיח]. Rabbenu Sagnhadias, the illustrious one, by which title the Jews honour their eminent rabbis of great name, on this passage of Daniel interprets the Son of Man as the Messiah, not that lowly and afflicted one whom they call the son of Joseph, but the other, illustrious Messiah whom they call the son of David, in these words: [והו משיח צדקינו והלא כתוב על משיח עני ורוכב על חמור אלא יבוא בענוה כי לא יבוא על סוסים בגאות ואשר כתוב עם ענני שמיא והנה עם השמים הם מלאכי צבא השמים וו היא רוב הגדולה שיתן חבורא למשיח]. "This is the Messiah our righteousness; but it is not written of the afflicted Messiah, riding upon an ass, that he will come in humility, for he will not come in pomp riding upon horses. But it is written 'with the clouds of heaven'; and 'behold, with the clouds of heaven' are understood to be the angels of the host of heaven, that is, the abundance of greatness which the Creator will give to the Messiah." Rabbi Shelomo Yarchi comments on this passage of Daniel, "Behold, one like the Son of Man," thus: [הוא מלך משיח], "this is the King Messiah." Rabbi Joseph Jacchiades interprets this passage of Daniel thus: [והוא משיח צדקני אשר ינין לפני ה׳]. "This is the Messiah our righteousness, who shall come before the presence of God." Hence it came about that Christ, being fully aware both that Daniel called the Messiah the Son of Man and that the Jews understood by the Son of Man the Messiah in Daniel, wished to designate himself by this name. But to one who seeks the truth with a sound mind and investigates the Gospel mysteries somewhat more carefully, this answer of learned men on every side does not wholly suffice. For one may further ask: (1) why Daniel, wishing to name the Messiah, who after subduing his enemies, hell, Satan, sin, death, the grave and the world, was to come into heaven in a triumphal procession to his kingdom, by the title [בר אנש] Son of Man, which is a name of one suffering affliction, a name which at first sight seems little suited to the royal and triumphal pomp of the Messiah. (2) Why Jesus should have so frequently, so earnestly, and so constantly used and claimed for himself this rare title, rare as it is (for it occurs only in Daniel and perhaps one other prophet, Ps. 8:5 and 80:18), and seldom met with among the Jews, passing over other titles far more frequent and far more illustrious. For it is customary for all who desire to make known something that is very important to use not rare names, scarcely used because of their rarity, to signify it, but names familiar to all. Since our most wise Lord was not unaware of this, one could hardly say, I think, that a man in his right mind would suppose that Jesus, without deliberate purpose, had so consistently neglected the other famous and familiar titles of the Messiah, and had so constantly used this one, which is rare and unique [μονογενής] in the Old Testament, in order to signify to the Jews that he is Christ, or the Messiah. For if Jesus had a fondness for a title that was rare among the Prophets, he was not unaware of these other names of the Messiah: [אִישׁ יהוה] Man of Jehovah, Gen. 4:1; [אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה] a man of war, or illustrious warrior, Ex. 15:3; [הַשָּׁרוֹן] the Rose, or Lily of Sharon, Song 2:1, for it signifies both rose and lily, from the word [שֵׁשׁ] six, because it blossoms with six petals. It is indeed strange that he did not choose this singular title, the rose or lily of Sharon, for by it he would also have signified the place of his birth, planted with the thorns of harsh afflictions; for Sharon is a region between Caesarea of Palestine and Mount Tabor and the Lake of Gennesaret, and Nazareth, where Christ was both conceived of a virgin and brought up for many years, is part of the district or region of Sharon. But if Christ loved the illustrious names of the Messiah, he had at hand and could apply to himself and others [פלא] or [פלא], Judg. 13:18; Isa. 9:6; [שר צבא יהוה] Prince of the army of the Lord, Josh. 5:14-15; [שר שלום] Prince of peace, Isa. 9:6; [דויד] David, Jer. 30:9; Ezek. 34:23-24 and 37:24-25; Hos. 3:5; [יהוה צדקנו] Jehovah our righteousness, Jer. 23:6 and 33:16. And if names expressing sonship were dear to Christ, why did he not choose these outstanding and more familiar titles, rather than [בן אדם] or [בר אנוש], by which the Prophets designated the Messiah, namely the seed of Abraham, Gen. 22:18; the seed of Isaac, Gen. 26:4; the seed of Jacob, Gen. 28:14; the seed of David, 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Chron. 17:11-14; Ps. 132:11; Jer. 23:5; the Son of God, Ps. 2:6-7; Ps. 89:27-30? This twofold name of the Messiah, namely Son of David and Son of God, was so familiar to the Jews at the time of Christ that not a few, persuaded that the Messiah would be the Son of David and the Son of God, addressed Jesus by this name: "Have mercy on us, Son of David," Matt. 9:27 and 20:30-31. So the multitude of Jews, as Jesus came, repeated again and again, "Hosanna to the Son of David," Matt. 21:9; and 22:42. And many of the Jews said, "Does not the Scripture say that Christ comes from the seed of David?" John 7:42. So the Pharisees, when Jesus asked them, "Whose son is Christ?" answered, "David," Luke 20:41. Nor do they name the Messiah the Son of God less often: thus Nathanael said, "You are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel," John 1:49; and those who were in the boat, coming, worshipped him, saying, "Truly you are the Son of God," Matt. 14:33. So also the high priest said, "I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God," Matt. 26:63; Mark 14:61. It is indeed strange and most worthy of inquiry why Jesus, the true Messiah, having neglected almost those illustrious titles, Son of David and Son of God, with which God himself and the Prophets had more than once adorned the Messiah, and which the whole Jewish nation still honoured, should have held in such favour the one title Son of Man, which only Daniel applied to the Messiah once, Dan. 7:13, or twice in all, Dan. 10:16, and which the Psalmist, Ps. 8:5 and 80:28, had used to designate him; so that he claimed it so earnestly and so constantly for himself, and called himself the Son of David or the Son of God only when he answered the Jews who asked whether he was Christ, the Son of God. Come now, let us, with holy Scripture shedding its light upon us, investigate the reason for this admirable arrangement.

units.la: Verum enim vero, mentem ac scopum Christi assecuturis si pote, nonnullas praemittere observationes operae pretium erit.
units.tr: Indeed, if we are to grasp the mind and aim of Christ, it will be worth setting out some preliminary observations.

units.la: Observa igitur 1o. filium hominis & hominem esse, & ex homine oriundum, unde Adam, homo quidem fuit ex terra rubra in animam viventem cretus: sed filius hominis nunquam ac nusquam perhibetur, quia non erat ex homine oriundus.
units.tr: Observe, then, first, that the Son of man is a man and was born of a man, as Adam was a man, made from red earth into a living soul. But the Son of man is never and nowhere called so, because he was not descended from a man.

units.la: Observa 2o. Hebraeis םדא utrumque sexum significare: ut, Gen. 5: 1. 2. Ps. 22: 7. & 39: 6. nec minus ἀνθρωπος, Graecis vero ὁ ἀνθρωπος utrumque pariter sexum significat: Ps. 9: 20. 21. Dan. 2: 43. & 4: 14.
units.tr: Observe, second, that the Hebrew word for man [אדם] signifies both sexes, as in Gen. 5:1, 2; Ps. 22:7 and 39:6. So too the Greek ἄνθρωπος, and ὁ ἄνθρωπος likewise signifies both sexes: Ps. 9:20, 21; Dan. 2:43; 4:14.

units.la: Observa 3o. Iesum se non quidem υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου; sed ὁ υἱὸς ὁ ἀνθρώπου, illum filium illius hominis, constanter κατ' ἐξοχὴν appellasse, si unum locum exceperis; Ioh. 5: 27. nec mirum, nam 1o. ὅτι, eo quod. 2o. Christi sermo de suprema authoritate judicandi orbem universum, quae mortalium nemini competere potest, abunde significant, quod aliis in locis per articulos characteristicos ac emphaticos ὁ υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, significatur. At si quando Iesus, neglectis articulis υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου dicitur, ut: Hebr. 2: 6. & Apoc. 1: 13. & 14: 14. Hoc fit 1o. non ab ipso Christo: sed ab Apostolis spectantibus vel ad Psalmum 8: 5. ubi in Hebraeo non exstat emphaticum ן ut Heb. 2: 6. vel ad caput Danielis, ut in ambobus locis apocalypseos; norunt vero, qui norunt quantum distent aera lupinis,
units.tr: Observe, third, that Jesus never called himself υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου ("a son of man"), but consistently, and κατ' ἐξοχήν (pre-eminently), ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ("the Son of that Man"), with one exception, if you count John 5:27. This is not surprising, for first, ὅτι means "because"; and second, Christ's words about the supreme authority to judge the whole world, which can belong to no mortal, plainly show that in other passages this is signified by the characteristic and emphatic articles ὁ υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. But if at any time Jesus is called υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου with the articles omitted, as in Heb. 2:6, Rev. 1:13 and 14:14, this happens, first, not by Christ himself but by the Apostles, who had in view either Ps. 8:5, where the Hebrew has no emphatic ן as in Heb. 2:6, or the chapter of Daniel, as in both places of the Apocalypse. Those who know how far apart bronze coins and lupin beans are, know what I mean.

units.la: Johannem in hocce libro prophetico Prophetarum phrases, ac imprimis Danielis perpetuò imitari: hinc sapienter dixit ὁμοίων υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου, ut exprimeret τὸ בר אנש Danielis. 2o. Cum Paulus Heb. 2: 6. & in Apocalypsi Johannes, Jesum vocant υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, nihil opus erat praefixis articulis characteristicis, ut significarent, eum esse excellentem illum filium singularis primi hominis, tunc enim eventus comprobaverat, per victricem è mortuis resurrectionem, ascensionem in cœlum, sessionem ad dextram Dei, Spiritus sancti missionem, Euangelii praedicationem, gentium vocationem, idolorum & regni Satanæ abolitionem, Jesum esse illum singularem filium Adami, qui caput serpentis contriverat, prostratis Satana, peccato, morte atque sepulchro. Longè diversa ratio erat, dum Jesus diebus carnis infirmitatis suæ, se ἐκ υἱοῦ ἀνθρώπου signanter appellabat, nondum enim pugnam decretoriam cum diabolo pugnaverat, nec ignominiosissimam mortem, nec tritum calcaneum passus fuerat, nec de Diabolo, peccato, morte ac sepulchro, triumphum egerat in nube. Si quis è Grammaticorum cavea, vel è doctorum Orchestra nobis properantibus ad Christi scopum, manu injecta, hic reponat, articulos praefixos non semper excellentiam adsignificare. Hoc nostrum ferat responsum. 1o. Vix exemplum in contrarium proferri posse, cum nomina communia generi, vel speciei, praefixos gerunt ejusmodi articulos; tunc enim insignia sunt characteristica, quibus è genere vel specie, designandum aliquod singulare eximitur. 2o. Ut ut rarum aliquod exemplum supeteret, non rarum est ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου elogium: sed frequens, ne dixerim perpetuum. Vident, qui oculos habent, Euangelistas, qua erant divina ac infallibili sapientia, hanc ab ore Christi Syram, vel Syro-chaldaicam appellationem filii hominis, non tam sedulo, tam constanter Græcam fecisse, praefixis utrique appellativo Nomini articulis, absque deliberato consilio: tum Jesum discernendi: 1o. ab Angelis sub humana specie visis, 2o. ab Adamo. 3o. ab omnibus aliis hominum filiis: tum denique singularem hominem, Adamum puta & Evam, beatamque virginem indigetandi. Reapse enim Angeli vero ac reali corpore humano vestiti, (Angeli enim lucis ac veritatis, nec fucum faciunt sensibus, nec illudunt homines, uti pater mendacii dum se transformat in Angelum lucis) & perhibentur, & se gerunt homines, nemo tamen Angelorum, filius fuit hominis: quippe nec via generationis naturali, nec supernaturali, corporis humani substantiam ab ullo traxerat homine. Adam pariter homo erat, non verò filius hominis, utpote parens omnium filiorum hominis, & à nullo terrenorum hominum secundus. Cæteri omnes, quotquot ab Adamo duxere originem homines, filii quidem sunt hominis, sed Christus χάτ' ἐξοχὴν, omnibus hominibus prorsus incommunicabilem, est ὁ Υἱὸς τ̃ ἀνθρώπου, singularis ac excellentissimus hominis filius: seu modum generationis ipsius spectaveris, non enim fuit e terra cretus sicut Adamus, sed ex humana substantia, non generatione naturali, non ope virili: sed supernaturali plane generatione, & Spiritus sancti inumbratione, ex virgine a viro: sed non a partu: seu puritatem ac humanae naturae sanctitatem in eo spectaveris: fuit enim unus inter omnes filios hominis, purus, sanctus, & a labe peccati prorsus immunis, non mutabili in horas sanctitate, sicut Adam: sed immutabili & intemerabili sicut ipse Deus: seu humanae naturae cum persona filii Dei ineffabilem in eo unionem adverteris: est enim inter omnes Adami filios unus Immanuel Θεάνθρωπος Deus & homo: seu munus mediatorium: est enim inter omnes hominum filios, non typicus & umbratilis sicut Moses: sed realis Mediator: seu tria ex quibus effloresc it munus mediatorium, munera, propheticum, sacerdotale, regium, quibus sustinendis nemo ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος par erat: seu vim & efficaciam ejusmodi munerum ad Deum, ad diabolum & homines attenderis: nam & divinam unus placavit justitiam, Diabolum prostravit, imperium ejus, mortem, caeteraque illius opera abolevit, & spiritum sanctificationis ac vitam spiritualem & immortalem in homines derivavit: unde Apostolus dum Christum contendit cum primo Adamo, in animam viventem creto; caelestem Adamum factum in Spiritum vivificum, sapienter nuncupavit 1. Cor. 15: 45. Nolito igitur mirari, cum Jesum, praefixis articulis emphaticis, ὁ υἱὸς τ̃ ἀνθρώπου, audis perpetuo nuncupatum.
units.tr: John, in this prophetic book, constantly imitates the phrases of the prophets, and especially of Daniel; hence he wisely wrote ὅμοιον υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου ("like a son of man") to express the בר אנש of Daniel. Second, since Paul in Heb. 2:6 and John in the Apocalypse call Jesus υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, there was no need for prefixed characteristic articles to signify that he is that excellent son of the singular first man. By then the event had confirmed it: through his victorious resurrection from the dead, his ascension into heaven, his session at the right hand of God, the sending of the Holy Spirit, the preaching of the gospel, the calling of the Gentiles, and the abolition of idols and of the kingdom of Satan, Jesus was shown to be that unique son of Adam who had crushed the serpent's head, laying low Satan, sin, death and the grave. The case was quite different when Jesus, in the days of his weak flesh, called himself expressly ἐκ υἱοῦ ἀνθρώπου, that is, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. For he had not yet fought the decisive battle with the devil, nor suffered the most shameful death and the bruised heel, nor celebrated his triumph over the devil, sin, death and the grave in the cloud. If someone from the cage of the grammarians, or from the orchestra of the learned, laying hands on us as we hasten towards Christ's aim, should object here that prefixed articles do not always signify excellence, let our answer be this. First, an example to the contrary can scarcely be produced, since common nouns of a genus or species carry such articles prefixed; for then they are characteristic marks by which something singular is picked out from the genus or species. Second, however rare some such example might be, the designation ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου is not rare but frequent, not to say perpetual. Those who have eyes can see that the Evangelists, with divine and infallible wisdom, did not so carefully and constantly make this Syriac or Syro-Chaldaic title "son of man" into Greek, from Christ's lips, by prefixing articles to both nouns without deliberate purpose. They did so, first, to distinguish Jesus from the angels seen in human form; second, from Adam; third, from all other sons of men; and finally, to pick out a singular man, namely Adam, and Eve, and the blessed Virgin. For in truth, angels clothed with a real human body (since angels of light and truth neither deceive the senses nor mock men, unlike the father of lies who transforms himself into an angel of light) are both called men and act as men. Yet none of the angels was a son of man, since neither by natural nor by supernatural generation had any of them derived the substance of a human body from any man. Adam likewise was a man, but not a son of man, being the parent of all sons of men and second to no earthly man. All the others, as many as derive their origin from Adam, are indeed sons of man. But Christ, pre-eminently (κατ' ἐξοχήν), is ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, the Son of man, wholly incommunicable to all men, the singular and most excellent Son of man. You may see this in the mode of his generation: he was not made from earth as Adam was, but from human substance, not by natural generation, not by male agency, but by a wholly supernatural generation, by the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, from a virgin without a man, yet not by childbirth. Or you may see it in the purity and holiness of his human nature: he was one among all the sons of men, pure, holy, and wholly free from the stain of sin, with a holiness not changeable from hour to hour as Adam's was, but unchangeable and inviolable like God himself. Or you may note the ineffable union in him of human nature with the person of the Son of God: among all the sons of Adam he is the one Immanuel, God and man, Θεάνθρωπος [God-man]. Or you may see his mediatorial office: among all the sons of men he is not a typical and shadowy mediator like Moses, but a real Mediator. Or you may see the three offices from which his mediatorial office flourishes, the prophetic, the priestly and the kingly, which no mere man (ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος) was equal to sustaining. Or you may consider the power and efficacy of these offices towards God, the devil and men: for he alone appeased divine justice, overthrew the devil, abolished his dominion, death and his other works, and conveyed into men the Spirit of sanctification and a spiritual and immortal life. Whence the Apostle, when he sets Christ against the first Adam, made a living soul, wisely called him the heavenly Adam, made a life-giving Spirit (1 Cor. 15:45). Do not wonder, therefore, that you hear Jesus perpetually named with the emphatic prefixed articles, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

units.la: Observa 4°. Messiam a lapsu, Adamo fuisse promissum, sicut semen mulieris, contriturum caput serpentis, & vicissim in talo a serpente conterendum, Gen. 3: 15. Hoc nos docet Paulus, cum venit plenitudo temporis, emisit Deus filium suum factum ex muliere: Gal. 4: 4. Hoc Judaeorum Magistri, velut per obscuram inspexere nebulam: unde Targum Hierosolymitanum ejusmodi promissionis complementum refert ad ultima tempora, ad dies Regis Messiae, & Rabbi Menachem in Lev. 25. quamdiu, inquit, impuritatis Spiritus non fuit ex mundo exterminatus, oportuit animas venientes in mundum mori, quia erumpebat potentia corrumpens impuritatis mundi, & consumebat eas, & illud omne propter decretum quod fuerat decretum propter corruptionem & spurcitiem, quam serpens intulerat in Evam. Et quando res ita habebat, omnes animae, quae erant creatae, & veniebant impurae per hanc corruptionem, necesse erat, ut morerentur ante adventum Messiae, &c. sed ad advenadventum Messiæ, exhinc omnes animæ erunt consummatæ. Hic vero tria notanda occurrunt. 1°. Messiam fore semen, hoc est juxta phrasiologiam Hebræorum, Filium mulieris: sed mulieris ægritudine ac infirmitatibus peccati laborantis: Deus enim promisit Messiam oriundum ex homine, post invectam in genus humanum peccati ægritudinem. 2°. Messiam filium ægri peccato hominis, bellaturum adversus serpentem diabolum, & caput illius, hoc est robur ac regnum contriturum. 3°. Messiam in pugna illa memorabili, quam cum Diabolo ac regno ipsius erat pugnaturus, passurum calcanei sui contritionem, hoc est mortem in infima natura sua, quam ex muliere ducturus erat, quæque in habitudine ad divinam ipsius naturam, calcanei ad instar sese ad caput habebat.
units.tr: Observe, fourth, that the Messiah was promised from the fall, through Adam, as the seed of the woman who would crush the serpent's head, and in turn would be bruised in the heel by the serpent (Gen. 3:15). Paul teaches us this: when the fullness of time came, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman (Gal. 4:4). The masters of the Jews saw this as if through a dim cloud. Hence the Jerusalem Targum refers the fulfilment of such a promise to the last times, to the days of the Messianic King, and Rabbi Menachem, on Lev. 25, says: As long as the impurity of the Spirit had not been exterminated from the world, it was necessary that souls coming into the world should die, because a destructive power of the world's impurity broke forth and consumed them; and all this was decreed on account of the corruption and filthiness which the serpent had brought into Eve. And while things were so, all souls which were created and came impure through this corruption had to die before the coming of the Messiah, etc. But from the coming of the Messiah onwards, all souls will be made complete. Three things here call for notice. First, the Messiah would be the seed, that is, in Hebrew phraseology, the son of the woman; but of a woman labouring under the sickness and infirmities of sin, for God promised that the Messiah would be born of a man after the sickness of sin had been brought into the human race. Second, the Messiah, a son of man sick with sin, would wage war against the serpent, the devil, and would crush his head, that is, his strength and kingdom. Third, in that memorable battle which he was to fight with the devil and his kingdom, he would suffer the bruising of his heel, that is, death in his lowest nature, which he was to take from a woman, and which, in relation to his divine nature, stood to the head as the heel does to the head.

units.la: Observa 5°. Solemnem hanc Messiæ, sicut seminis mulieris promissionem, Evam in exspectationem promissi in consolationem, illius filii, ita erexisse; ut quam primum peperit, se nactam spectatum illum filium consolatorem rata, in hæc verba eruperit acquisivi virum Jehova, את enim cum nota sit accusativi, non vero dativi, non significat virum Jehova, sed virum Jehova. Intellexerat enim promissum filium mulieris, futurum Satanæ invictum debellatorem, non fore φίλον ἀνθρωπον, merum hominem: merus enim homo victus, & diaboli imperio subditus, vel dum pleno robore gloriosæ creationis lætabatur, jam æger, & diaboli imperio mancipatus, impar erat ad victorem diabolum debellandum, conterendum & imperio suo expoliandum. Hinc lætabunda ista exclamatio, acquisivi virum Iehova, id est, Immanuelem, Deum atque hominem: sed ut ut voto suo frustrata fuerit Eva, non minus in spem concipiendi ac enitendi Messiam cæteræ mulieres Evæ filiæ erectæ fuerunt. Hinc Lemech primogenitum suum vocavit לנוח levamen, seu requiem, quia dixit, iste consolabitur nos ab opere nostro: Gen. 5: 29. Nec plane voto suo excidit: etsi enim Noach non fuit Messias, fuit tamen illustris ipsius typus. Hinc probro & infamiæ, universa Israëlitarum natio, sterilitatem mulieribus vertit. Hinc illæ sterilium mulierum lachrymæ, quod iis spes omnis pariendi Messiam decollasset. Hinc filia Jephthe duos menses impensè a parente efflagitat, non ut vitam: sed ut virginitatem suam lamentaretur, pluris enim faciebat spem enitendi Messiam, quâ voto paterno plane excidebat, quam vitam ipsam. Non spem modo mulierum: sed & universorum Abrahamitarum, ex quo Deus Abrahamo receperat fore, ut in semine ipsius, quod semen Christus est, Gal. 3: 16. omnes terræ gentes benedicerentur: sed imprimis tribus Judæ, ac tandem familiæ Davidis, ex quo Numen Messiam ex lumbis ejus nasciturum promiserat, solemni jurejurando, illustris hæc promissio feminis mulieris nasciturî, luculentum in modum fovebat, & universam nationem, quæ de illustri Judæ nomine, gens Judæa censebatur, in tantam exspectationem sollicitabat, ut regius vates Esaías, ubi Judæorum gentem voti ream ac compotem pervidet, in hæc verba exclamabundus erumpat, puer nobis natus est, filius nobis datus, & imperium ejus humero impositum, & vocabitur admirabilis consiliarius, Deus fortis, pater æternitatis, princeps pacis, Esa. 9: 5. Quasi diceret, afflicta Judæorum natio: sed in spem nasciturî promissi filii mulieris divinitus erecta, abstergite lachrymas, plaudite, exultate, ecce puer, longis retro sæculis exspectatus, Filius promissus à lapsu Adami, nobis tandem natus est, nobis divinitus datus. Nulli dubitate, amabo: erit enim admirabilis, modo nativitatis ex virgine à viro, & naturarum divinæ ac humanæ, admiranda personali unione: sed & erit Deus fortis, ut conterat serpentis caput, nosque liberet è dura servitute diaboli, peccati, ac mortis: sed ex victoria memorabili tantaque liberatione, regnum reportabit æternum: nam imperium fuit humero ejus impositum: regnabit, sed ut subditis suis sit consiliarius intemeratæ obedientiæ ac illibatæ ad mortem usq; fidelitatis, princeps, & author vitæ immortalis, ac æternæ felicitatis: credite mihi, nam ideo vocabitur consiliarius, pater æternitatis, ac princeps pacis.
units.tr: Observe, fifthly, that this solemn promise of the Messiah, as the seed of the woman, raised Eve to expect that promised son as her consolation. As soon as she bore a child, she supposed she had gained that expected son who would console them, and burst out with these words: I have gotten a man, the LORD. The particle את, since it marks the accusative and not the dative, does not mean a man for the LORD but the man, the LORD [את]. For she understood that the promised son of the woman would be the unconquered conqueror of Satan, and would not be a mere man [φίλον ἀνθρωπον]. A mere man, once conquered and subject to the power of the devil, even while rejoicing in the full strength of his glorious creation, would already be weak and enslaved to the devil's power, and so unequal to defeating, crushing, and stripping of his power the conquering devil. Hence her joyful cry, I have gotten the man, the LORD, that is, Immanuel, God and man. But although Eve was disappointed in her hope, the other women, daughters of Eve, were no less raised to hope of conceiving and bringing forth the Messiah. Hence Lamech called his firstborn Noah [לנוח], that is, rest or comfort, because he said, this one will comfort us in our work (Gen. 5:29). Nor did he altogether fail in his hope: for although Noah was not the Messiah, he was nevertheless a distinguished type of him. Hence the whole nation of the Israelites turned barrenness into a reproach and a disgrace for women. Hence the tears of barren women, because every hope of bearing the Messiah had been cut off from them. Hence Jephthah's daughter asked her father for two months, not to lament her life, but her virginity, for she valued the hope of bringing forth the Messiah more than life itself, of which she was plainly deprived by her father's vow. Not only the hope of the women, but also of all the sons of Abraham, was kindled, since God had promised Abraham that in his seed, which is Christ (Gal. 3:16), all the nations of the earth would be blessed. Above all, the tribe of Judah and finally the family of David, from whose loins God by solemn oath had promised the Messiah would be born, were greatly nourished by this illustrious promise of one to be born of the woman's seed, and it stirred the whole nation, which was counted as the Jewish people from the famous name of Judah, into such expectation that the royal prophet Isaiah, seeing the Jewish nation guilty of hope and granted it, breaks out exclaiming: A child is born to us, a son is given to us, and the government will be upon his shoulder, and his name will be called Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace (Isa. 9:5).
