Nor should you reply that God put forth his almighty power in the Son of Man, in a singular manner, so that he might win so great a victory over the Devil, sin, curse, the world and death. We have already advanced far, and you have spoken truly, if in a sound sense. God indeed put forth his almighty power in the Son of Man, a famous warrior, in a singular manner, because the Son of Man himself, while fighting his victorious battle, was God blessed for ever. But you, companion of Socinus, deny this with a smooth mouth. Tell me, then, please, what is that singular reason by which God put forth his almighty power in the Son of Man so that he might win so great a victory? Did the most powerful Deity, by a singular reasoning, put forth his almighty power in the prophets through many amazing miracles of infinite power? Did he likewise put forth the same power in the apostles of the Son of Man, bearing witness everywhere with signs, wonders, various powers and distributions of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will, that the salvation whose heralds they were is true, Heb. 2:4. How then does it happen that no prophet and no apostle is said to have crushed the head of the serpent or conquered the world? Why does the Holy Spirit credit so great a work to the one Son of Man alone? How is it that no prophet and no apostle has claimed for himself the crushing of the serpent's head and the victory over the world? Who, I ask, among the Son of Man's own people has dared to ascribe to the one Son of Man this extraordinary work without robbery and blasphemy? Either God, most closely united with the Son of Man in a personal union, conquered the Devil and the world, or God the Father, separated from Christ as far as the Creator is from the creature, brought this work about through the Son of Man, as through a finite instrument. If you admit the first, you have lost your cause, and truth has conquered. If the second, you hold up your shield for your error. Therefore it was not the Son of Man who crushed the head of the serpent, but God, through the Son of Man, as through a finite instrument. But you boldly contradict the Son of Man himself, who cries out joyfully: I have trodden the winepress alone [levadi], and of the peoples there was no man with me; and I have trodden them in my anger, and trampled them in my fury; for the day of vengeance is in my heart, and the year of my redeemed has come; and I looked, and there was no helper, and I was astonished; because there was none to uphold; but my own arm saved me, and my fury upheld me, Isa. 63:3, 4, 5. Be of good cheer, I have conquered the world, John 16:33. You also contradict Paul, who ascribes the whole of so great a victory to Christ alone: He stripped the principalities and powers, made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in himself, Col. 2:15. How does it happen at last that this great victory, for which all the powers of finite creatures were unequal, is never ascribed to God the Father, the author and cause, if your opinion were to stand, but is always and everywhere ascribed to Christ the Son of Man, merely a finite instrument? 2. We must weigh a little more carefully the manner and method by which the Son of Man crushed the head of the serpent and of the world. He entered the battle with the serpent and the world, and in it he suffered the crushing of his heel, that is, the bloody and accursed death of the cross: You shall bruise his heel, serpent. Therefore the death of the Son of Man crushed the head of the serpent and of the world; or, if you prefer, the Son of Man, dying on the cross, conquered and abolished the strength and kingdom of the Devil and the world. Paul taught us this: He himself, namely the Son of Man, partook of flesh and blood, that through death he might destroy him who had the power and dominion of death, that is, the Devil, Heb. 2:14. Here your cause gets no help, even if you fly, as is your habit, to martyrdom and example; for the death of Christ abolished the Devil, the lord of death, neither as a martyrdom nor as an example. Martyrdom and example concern men, not the Devil. Indeed the death of Christ is valuable as martyrdom and example, as a moral cause for persuading men of the truth of Christ's doctrine and for infusing its holiness into their minds, by the power of example and the sweet and voluntary allurement of love. But for crushing Satan and stripping him of his dominion over death, it is worth nothing under the aspect of martyrdom and example; for Satan is not persuaded by these to give up his rule willingly and gladly, and the head of the serpent had to be crushed, and the Devil's dominion abolished, by external and opposing force, not by moral persuasion. 3. The heel of the woman's seed, bruised, in view of its opposition to the head of the serpent, draws you, Socinian, whether you like it or not, into the confession of the divine nature really existing in the Son of Man, whether we consider his heel as suffering its bruising. For just as the serpent, so also the head of the serpent is understood allegorically; thus the exact opposition of the Son of Man's heel demands, and even against your will forces you, to understand the heel allegorically. For in truth the heel of Christ, properly so called, was neither bruised by the serpent and the world in the crucifixion and death of the Son of Man, nor is it recorded to have been; rather the whole human nature of Christ was bruised and extinguished by death. This crucified nature, therefore, was the heel of the Son of Man. Now, Socinian, tell me please, what was the head of this bruised heel? Will you say it was the human head? But first, the exact reasoning of the divine allegory forbids it: for just as we have shown by solid arguments that the heel is to be understood not literally but allegorically, so the head of this heel in the Son of Man must necessarily be allegorical too. Second, because when Christ died, the human head of the Son of Man was bruised, or extinguished, by the deadly weapon of the Serpent. But the seed of the woman, as the Deity itself attests, was to suffer bruising not in the head, as the Serpent did, but in the heel. What then was there in the Son of Man, the head of his bruised heel, unharmed and untouched by the venomous assaults of the Serpent? Tell me, please, Socinian: perhaps the soul of Christ? Away with that godsent [theelaton] error! The most holy soul of the Son of Man felt the deadly darts of the Serpent: My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death, Matt. 26:38. Hence drops of blood falling to the ground; hence the sad laments, the repeated prayers and supplications of the Son of Man; hence that fear, not indeed of death, for he gladly faced it and was not terrified by it, but of the most savage temptation and of the impending curse of God, under whose weight he greatly feared that his soul would at last succumb: but he was heard, because he was delivered from that fear, Heb. 5:7. It remains, therefore, that the head of the Son of Man, corresponding to his bruised heel, was unharmed and untouched by the assaults of Satan, so that the divine nature of the Son of Man must, Socinian, be acknowledged, whether you like it or not. Learn then the mystery of the title Son of Man, who suffered the bruising of his heel in the cursed and ignominious death of the cross, and you will learn to your eternal salvation that there are two natures in the Son of Man, human and divine, and you will confess it with a better mouth. 5. The Papists...

units.la: 5°. Pontificii in contrariam delapsi ὑπερβολὴν, utut humanam filii hominis naturam ore confiteantur, eam tamen novitia sua, & melioribus orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ Christianæ seculis, incognitā transsubstantiationis doctrinā, filio hominis reapse detractum eunt. Cur enim amabo, Christus est ac perhibetur filius hominis, nisi quia semen est mulieris, verus homo, ex substantia beatæ virginis, Spiritus sancti, virtute supernaturali cretus? Sed Christum ex substantia panis & vini Sacramentalis, semen esse mulieris, verum ac realem filium hominis, nobis per omnia simillimum, excepto peccato, qui pote? Christum hominem, filium hominis coactæ adeò brevitatis, ut in punctum Eucharisticum, ubi nulla comparet organorum corporeorum distinctio, cui nec caput, nec pes uni redditur formæ, quæ mens, vel angelica capere potest? Proh Dei hominumque fidem! si Christus est filius hominis, quia à sexdecim retrò seculis, ex substantia beatæ virginis, humanam duxit naturam & originem; quî pro libitu & intensione sacrificuli, ex substantia panis & vini exanimi, ubivis nunc & in posterum ad seculorum consummationem novam duxerit originem? Christum sanè hujuscemodi non filium hominis: sed panis ac vini filium, jure merito dixeris, conversâ scilicet, & ut barbarè loquuntur Barbari, totâ substantiâ panis & vini, in substantiam corporis & sanguinis Christi, transsubstantiatâ.
units.tr: 5. The Papists, having lapsed into the opposite extreme, although they confess the human nature of the Son of Man with their mouths, nonetheless, by their novelty and by the doctrine of transubstantiation, which was unknown in the better centuries of the orthodox Christian Church, they in fact strip the Son of Man of it. For why, pray, is Christ called and declared to be the Son of Man, unless because he is the seed of the woman, a true man, formed from the substance of the blessed Virgin by the supernatural power of the Holy Spirit? But how can Christ, who is formed from the substance of the sacramental bread and wine, be the seed of a woman, a true and real Son of Man, most like us in all things except sin? How can Christ be a man, a Son of Man, shrunk to such a tiny size that he is reduced to a Eucharistic point, where no distinction of bodily organs appears, where neither head nor foot is given to a single form, which mind, even an angelic one, can grasp? Good God, and good faith of men! If Christ is the Son of Man because, sixteen centuries ago, he took his human nature and origin from the substance of the blessed Virgin, how is it that, at the will and intention of a little priest, he now takes a new origin from the substance of lifeless bread and wine, wherever he is, and will do so henceforth until the consummation of the ages? Such a Christ is surely not the Son of Man, but rightly you would call him the son of bread and wine, the whole substance of bread and wine having been converted, or, as the barbarians put it in their barbarous speech, transubstantiated, into the substance of the body and blood of Christ.

units.la: 6°. Miratus est ac obstupuit orbis Christianus, obtinentibus pessimorum seculorum tenebris, & eriamnum reddita Euangelii luce, miratur, reducta Christianis Judæorum somnia ac deliria, super Christo filio hominis. Redditum miratur incerta origine Christum: fictum obstupescit Messiam geminum. Christi regnum planè spirituale in secularem monarchiam apud Pontificios commutatum, ingemiscit. Eò quidem lamentabilius, quod in plena Euangelii luce, nullos Judæorum prætextus, ullo possunt jure prætexere Christiani. Nec quicquam Pontificiis, malè nos affingere, Deus ipse testis est. Incerti fluctuant sicut Judæi, de origine Christi sui, oriundi scilicet ex substantia panis & vini, num actione adductiva, num actione productiva, sub speciebus panis & vini, præsens existat, integræ Franciscanorum ac Thomistarum familiæ miserè digladiantur. Sopita verò, nondum tamen extincta lite, concilii Tridentini librato altu in utramque partem decreto, incerti, animiqúe adhuc penduli hærent, hærebuntque, dum misericors Deus mentem meliorem dederit, num cretus ille ex panis ac vini substantia suus Christus, sit corpore præsens Sacramento, quia corporea ipsius præsentia, in totum pendet ex consecrantis sacrificuli intensione, uni Deo cognitâ.
units.tr: 6. The Christian world has been astonished and amazed, while the darkness of the worst centuries still prevails and the light of the Gospel has only just been restored, to see revived among Christians the dreams and delusions of the Jews about Christ the Son of Man. It marvels that Christ has a revived uncertain origin; it is stunned that a Messiah has been invented who is twofold. It groans that the plainly spiritual kingdom of Christ has among the Papists been changed into a worldly monarchy. This is the more lamentable because, in the full light of the Gospel, Christians can have no pretext, by any right, for the excuses of the Jews. God himself is witness that we do not falsely charge the Papists with anything. Like the Jews, they waver uncertainly about the origin of their Christ, namely whether, born from the substance of bread and wine, he is present under the species of bread and wine by an attractive action or by a productive action; the whole families of the Franciscans and the Thomists wrangle wretchedly over this. The dispute has been lulled but not yet extinguished by the decree of the Council of Trent, which was balanced so as to favour both sides; and uncertain and still wavering in mind, they cling, and will go on clinging, to the question of whether that Christ born from the substance of bread and wine is present in the Sacrament in his body, since his bodily presence depends wholly on the intention of the consecrating priest, which is known to God alone. Until merciful God gives them a better mind.

units.la: O stupendam Christianorum ἀξελψίαν! Prophetiarum obscuritatem cau-sentur Judæi, ac suæ fluctuationi de Messiæ origine, modoque adventus prætexant. Ecquid verò causæ est, in hac nostra Euangelii luce aper-tissima, cur Christiani dubitent de origine adventus filii hominis? quandoquidem sancta virgo peperit semen mulieris Christum, morte sua victorem, resurrectione, & in cœlum ascensione ad dexteram Majestatis Dei sedentem, quem cœlum oportet capere, in tempus restaurationis omnium, & seculorum consummationem. Miratur & stupescit Christianus orbis, ubi duos Christos, sicut apud somniantes Judæos, apud Pontificios etiamnum contemplatur. Unum equidem, fatebor enim, ore confitentur Christum: sed ambos reapse habent, gemino Judæorum Messiæ quam simillimos, afflictum & inglorium alterum: illustrem alterum ac gloriosum: alterum ex substantia panis & vini, intentione presbyteri, & vi verborum sacramentalium plane stupendâ, cretum: alterum ex substantia beatæ virginis, ineffabili Spiritus sancti potentia, à sexdecim, & quod excurrit, seculis, in hominum salutem genitum: alterum afflictum, & immolatum in sacrificium propitiatorium verè ac proprie dictum: viventem ac gloriosum alterum, & mortis cujusvis dominationi exemptum: alterum ταμείοις ciboriis suis, ut loqui amant, clausum ac reconditum, in viaticum morientium: alterum cœlo receptum, & regnantem ad dexteram Majestatis in excelsis: alterum furum contumeliis, murium dentibus, ægrorum nauseæ ac vomitui, stomachorum corruptioni, flammis ac diabolicæ malignitati obnoxium, authore ipso Innocente tertio Papa lib. 2. de Missæ mysteriis, cap. 52. Cum sacerdos, inquit, accipit patenam & urceolum, calicem & thuribulum, patenam cum hostia, urceolum cum aqua, calicem cum vino, & thuribulum cum incenso, efficit super ea crucis signaculum, ut per crucis virtutem, omnis conatus diabolicæ malignitatis effugiat, ne contra sacerdotem aut sacrificium prævaleat: alterum regnantem in cœlo, in omnem principatum & potestatem, & in omne nomen, quod & in hoc, & in futuro seculo nominatur. Prætexant Judæi somnio suo de Messia gemino, Prophetiarum obscuritatem, vilem modò & abjectum, hominem dolorum ac languorum, hominum ludibrium ac opprobrium: illustrem modò bellatorem ac Regem potentissimum, alternis vicibus Messiam exhibentium. Quid porrò causabuntur Christiani in clara nostra Euangelii luce, quæ Christum nostrum nube in cœlum pompa triumphali vehentem, dum inde redeat eadem forma ac pompa aspectabili, nobis exhibet conspicuum? Quid porrò causabuntur in Apostolum docentem. Si verò & cognovimus Christum {a}stum secundum carnem : sed & nunc non amplius cognoscimus. Scimus quod Christus excitatus e mortuis, non amplius moritur, mors in eum non amplius dominatur. Obstupescit ac lamentatur purus orbis Christianus, regnum filii hominis mere spirituale, in secularem monarchiam, ac regno Messiæ Judæorum terreno, quam simillimum, apud Pontificios commutatum. Hoc tergemina clamat Episcopi Romani, carbunculis & adamantibus radiantissima corona : hoc geminus gladius : hoc dono datum diadema Rodolpho : hoc pedibus calcatum Friderici Imperatoris collum : hoc erepta & restituta pro libitu terrena Regum imperia : hoc multitudo populorum, pax, abundantia, prosperitas, ac opulentia temporaria, insignis & essentialis Ecclesiæ nota, & quid non ? clamant. Causentur iterum Judæi Prophetias, regnum Messiæ sub involucro terrenæ opulentiæ passim sibi propositum esse. Ecquid demum causæ est, cur Christiani in hac luce Euangelii, regnum Christi opulentia ac pompa seculari terrenum, fabulentur ? Ipso Christo palam ac rotundè pronunciante, Regnum meum non est ex hoc mundo, regnum meum est regnum cœlorum, & Paulo suo reddente, Si Christo consurrexistis, tà ἄνω ζητεῖτε, tà ἄνω φρονεῖτε, quæ sunt sursum quærite, quæ sunt sursum sapite, ubi Christus est sedens ad dexteram Dei; nolite sapere quæ sunt super terra.
units.tr: O the amazing stupidity of Christians! The Jews blame the obscurity of the prophecies, and use as an excuse for their own wavering about the origin and manner of the Messiah's coming. But what cause is there, in this our very clear light of the Gospel, why Christians should doubt the origin of the coming of the Son of Man, since the holy Virgin bore the seed of the woman, Christ, who by his death conquered, by his resurrection and ascension into heaven sits at the right hand of the Majesty of God, whom heaven must receive until the time of the restoration of all things and the consummation of the ages? The Christian world marvels and is astonished when it sees, as among the dreaming Jews, so among the Papists, two Christs. One, indeed, I will grant, they confess with their mouths as Christ; but in reality they have both, two images most like the twofold Messiah of the Jews: one afflicted and inglorious, the other illustrious and glorious; the one made from the substance of bread and wine, by the intention of the priest and the truly astonishing power of the sacramental words; the other begotten from the substance of the blessed Virgin, by the ineffable power of the Holy Spirit, sixteen centuries ago and more, for the salvation of men; the one afflicted and offered in a propitiatory sacrifice, truly and properly so called; the other living and glorious, and free from the dominion of any death; the one ταμείοις [tameiois] enclosed and hidden in their ciboria, as they like to say, as viaticum for the dying; the other received into heaven and reigning at the right hand of the Majesty on high; the one exposed to the insults of thieves, the teeth of mice, the nausea and vomiting of the sick, the corruption of stomachs, flames and diabolical malice, as Pope Innocent III himself says in book 2 of his work On the Mysteries of the Mass, chapter 52: When the priest takes the paten and the little cruet, the chalice and the censer, the paten with the host, the cruet with water, the chalice with wine, and the censer with incense, he makes the sign of the cross over them, so that by the power of the cross every attempt of diabolical malice may be put to flight, lest it prevail against the priest or the sacrifice. The other reigns in heaven, over every principality and power, and over every name that is named, both in this age and in the age to come. The Jews, in their dream of a twofold Messiah, plead the obscurity of the prophecies: now a vile and abject man, a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief, the mockery and reproach of men; now an illustrious warrior and most powerful King, the Messiah presented in alternating turns. What, then, will Christians be able to plead in our clear light of the Gospel, which shows us Christ, who was carried up into heaven in a cloud with a triumphal procession, and who, when he returns from there, will be seen by us in the same form and with the same visible procession? What will they plead against the Apostle teaching: If indeed we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we no longer know him. We know that Christ, raised from the dead, dies no more; death no longer has dominion over him. The pure Christian world is astonished and laments that the kingdom of the Son of Man, which is purely spiritual, has among the Papists been changed into a worldly monarchy, very like the earthly kingdom of the Messiah imagined by the Jews. This the threefold crown of the Roman bishop shouts out, blazing with carbuncles and diamonds; this the double sword; this the diadem given as a gift to Rudolph; this the neck of Emperor Frederick trodden under foot; this the earthly empires of kings taken away and restored at will; this the multitude of peoples, peace, abundance, prosperity and temporal wealth, the distinguishing and essential mark of the Church, and what not, they cry. The Jews again plead that the prophecies everywhere set before them a kingdom of the Messiah under the veil of earthly wealth. Is there, finally, any reason why Christians in this light of the Gospel should invent a kingdom of Christ that is earthly, in worldly wealth and pomp? Christ himself has plainly and bluntly declared: My kingdom is not of this world; my kingdom is the kingdom of heaven. And Paul, his servant, replies: If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above, mind the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God; do not mind the things that are on the earth. [Col. 3:1–2; the Greek is τὰ ἄνω ζητεῖτε, τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖτε]

units.la: 7º. Hîc seu Judæos, seu Pontificios spectaveris, hominis animalis ingenium, suo, uti sorex, se prodit indicio. Hic quid & quantum in Deum valeant carnalia seculi præjudicia, planum fit & obvium lamentabili experimento. Judæi Messiam filium hominis votis calidissimis expetunt & exspectant. Exoptatum Messiam, carnalibus abrepti affectibus, rejiciunt ac repudiant, quia male præconceptis præjudiciis suis, ac voto minus respondere videtur. Messiam quærunt gloriosum, vi & armis conspicuum, ut regnum Israëlis terrenum ac opulentum restituat. Ecce jam filium hominis Christum, vel ipsis Dæmonibus tremendum, peccati, maledictionis, mortis ac Diaboli victorem æternum. Nec minus tamen eum Pontificii rejiciunt, quia constitutus in gloria ad dexteram Majestatis in excelsis, in finem, quem expetunt, non satis conducere ipsis videtur. Christum quærunt opportunum, ad imperium ministris suis, in Christianorum conscientias erigendum, quique ex libitu eorum totus pendeat, ut Dei, suique Servatoris immolandi, si Deo placet, in sacrificium verè ac reapse propitiatorium, pro peccatis vivorum ac mortuorum, creatores, sese in terræ Reges superciliosè efferant, & tantùm inter mortales emineant, quantum lenta solent inter viburna cupressi. Nec rerum suarum dum satagunt, contumeliosè tantum in humanam manam Christi naturam ac gloriam coelestem agunt: sed & veritatem primi de filio hominis oraculi, labefactant, & causam divinae filii hominis naturae, Socinianis turpiter produnt. Qui vero? Audiatur versio Bibliorum vulgata, Inimicitias ponam inter te & mulierem, & semen tuum, & semen illius: ipsa conteret caput tuum, & tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus. Hanc versionem ut suo, sicut sorex periret indicio, Tridentinum concilium authenticam declaravit, & fidei morumque regulam sub poena anathematis, Si quis autem libros ipsos integros, cum omnibus suis partibus, prout in Ecclesia Catholica legi consueverunt, & in veteri vulgata latina editione habentur, pro sacris & canonicis non susceperit, anathema sit. Et aliquot interjectis lineis, sic pergit: Insuper eadem sacro-sancta Synodus, considerans non parum utilitatis accedere posse Ecclesiae Dei, si ex omnibus latinis editionibus, quae circumferuntur sacrorum librorum, quaenam pro authentica habenda sit innotescat, statuit & declarat, ut haec ipsa vetus & vulgata editio, quae longo tot seculorum usu in ipsa Ecclesia probata est, in publicis lectionibus, disputationibus, praedicationibus & expositionibus pro authentica habeatur, & ut nemo illam rejicere, quovis praetextu, audeat vel praesumat. Conc. Trident. sess.4. Tune, Christiane Lector, infallibilem credideris conciliorum Romanensium authoritatem? Tune veritatis infallibilis scita eorum praedicaveris? Hicne vides, Tridentinum concilium erroris multiformis reum? 1°. Editionem, vel in primo de Messia oraculo, non uno modo falsam, & erroneam, authenticam declarat & canonicam, sub poena anathematis. 2°. Hac sua declaratione filium mulieris Christum, sua adversus serpentem expoliat victoria, merito & efficacia contriti calcanei sui, hoc est, mortis cruentae, privat: ipsi naturam divinam, cujus dignitate, moriendo, caput serpentis contrivit, audaci manu adimit, ut quicquid est pugnae, victoriae, mortis, divinitatis ac meriti seminis mulieris, in ipsam conferat mulierem, beatam scilicet virginem, ex qua suam proxime duxit originem filius hominis Christus. Nae multiformis criminis reos hic deprehendimus lemures conciliabuli Tridentini. Et 1°. quidem Sacer Moses non dixit הִיא הָאִשָּׁה תְּשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ ipsa mulier conteret tibi caput; sed הוּא, זֶרַע scilicet יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ ipsum semen, scilicet mulieris, conteret tibi caput. Non iterum dixit Moses, Et tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus mulieris; sed וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב, & tu conteres ei calcaneum, subfixo scil. masculino articulo relativo ad זֶרַע semen: non vero suffixo articulo foeminino, relato ad mulierem. Consentiunt & septuaginta, αὐτὸς, id est υἱὸς ἡ γυναικὸς, si magis ad sensum, quam ad verba respexerint, vel αὐτὸ, si ad nomen, ἀπέρμά σου τηρήσει κεφαλὴν, καὶ σὺ τηρήσεις αὐτῷ πτέρναν. πλέγνα: non αὐτὸς πλέγνα. Fac vero authenticam esse, & infallibilem fidei regulam, vulgatam editionem latinam, ipsa mulier, seu virgo beata in liberationem generis humani, tritam suam calcem passa fuerit, & sua illa calce contrita, caput Serpentis contriverit: non vero ipsius semen filius hominis Christus. Eccum tibi igitur beatam virginem generis humani liberatricem ac redemptricem. Necquicquam Apostolo fervide interrogante, Num Paulus fuit crucifixus pro vobis? 1. Cor. 1: 13. Beatam tamen virginem, Diaboli victricem & capitis serpentis conculcatricem exhibent, vel ipsae imagines ad contemplandum & adorandum populis propositae, in quibus beata virgo visitur, Serpentem conculcans ac conterens pedibus suis. Qui vero mera creatura, ut ut beata inter mulieres, robur ac regnum Diaboli conterere, & genus humanum valuit servare, quae ipsa servatore indiguit? Latata est anima mea in Deo salvatore meo, Luc. 1: 47. Qui alios e Diaboli tyrannide servare potuit, quae se ipsam servare non potuit? sed Deum filium suum, nacta servatorem, laetabunda celebrat, in cantico suo. Certe si beata virgo, mulier mera homo, ad caput Serpentis conterendum, non fuit impar, nec impar fuerit filius hominis, purus homo, qui tantum opus effectum daret. Vicit igitur & triumphat Socinianorum haeresis, causa divinae filii hominis naturae, miserè proditur Socinianis. Nec minus tamen, quicquid moliantur carnales homuli, Jesus filius hominis, verus est Christus Dei: in eo quippe cernimus plenum implementum primae, ex qua pendent caeterae omnes, de Messia, prophetiae ac promissionis. Unus noster Jesus verus est filius hominis, semen mulieris, Evae ac beatae virginis; unus passus est in generis humani salutem, calcanei sui contritionem; unus caput serpentis contrivit: unus Diabolum, mortis imperatorem, morte sua abolevit: unus & sibi & nobis peccatum, maledictionem, mortem, Diabolum, mundum vicit: unus vivit, regnat & imperat, nomen sortitus supra omne nomen, ut ad nomen Jesu flectatur omne genu, quicquid ringant, fremant, vel ut rumpantur Haeretici, semen pestilentissimum serpentis.
units.tr: 7. Whether we look at the Jews or the Papists, the disposition of the natural man betrays itself, as a mole does by its mound. Here one can plainly and sadly see what carnal prejudices of the age can do against God. The Jews eagerly desire and long for the Messiah, the Son of Man. Carried away by carnal feelings, they reject and spurn the longed-for Messiah, because he does not seem to answer their preconceived prejudices and wishes. They seek a glorious Messiah, conspicuous for force and arms, who will restore the earthly and wealthy kingdom of Israel. Behold, Christ the Son of Man, who is dreadful even to the demons, the eternal conqueror of sin, curse, death and the Devil. Yet the Papists reject him no less, because he, seated in glory at the right hand of the Majesty on high, does not seem to them to serve the end they desire. They seek a Christ who is convenient, a Christ whom they can set up as an instrument for their ministers over the consciences of Christians, and on whose whim everything depends. They, the creators of a Christ to be sacrificed, if God is pleased, as a true and real propitiatory sacrifice for the sins of the living and the dead, lift themselves up haughtily as kings of the earth, and stand out among mortals as much as the tall cypress stands out among the pliant viburnum. While busy with their own affairs, they do not merely insult the human nature and heavenly glory of Christ; they also undermine the truth of the first oracle about the Son of Man, and shamefully betray to the Socinians the cause of the divine nature of the Son of Man. And how so? Let the Vulgate version of the Bible be heard: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; she shall bruise your head, and you shall lie in wait for her heel. This version, which the Council of Trent declared authentic, and made a rule of faith and morals under penalty of anathema, is where the mole perishes by its own mound. The Council says: If anyone does not accept as sacred and canonical the books themselves, entire with all their parts, as they have been customarily read in the Catholic Church and are contained in the old Vulgate Latin edition, let him be anathema. And after a few lines it goes on thus: Moreover, the same most holy Synod, considering that no little advantage can accrue to the Church of God if it becomes known which of all the Latin editions of the sacred books in circulation is to be held authentic, decrees and declares that this same old and Vulgate edition, which has been approved in the Church by long use over so many centuries, is to be held authentic in public lectures, disputations, preachings and expositions, and that no one may dare or presume to reject it on any pretext whatsoever. Council of Trent, session 4. Christian reader, would you believe in the infallible authority of the Roman councils? Would you preach their decisions as infallible truth? Do you see here that the Council of Trent is guilty of a manifold error? First, it declares authentic and canonical, under penalty of anathema, an edition that, not in one way only, is false and erroneous even in the first oracle about the Messiah. Second, by this declaration it strips Christ, the Son of the woman, of his victory over the serpent, which rests on the merit and efficacy of his bruised heel, that is, of his bloody death. It takes by a bold hand from him the divine nature, by whose dignity he crushed the serpent's head in dying, so that whatever belongs to the fight, the victory, the death, the divinity and the merit of the woman's seed is transferred to the woman herself, namely the blessed Virgin, from whom the Son of Man Christ drew his immediate origin. Indeed, here we find the ghosts of the Tridentine conventicle guilty of many kinds of error. And first, the sacred Moses did not say הִיא הָאִשָּׁה תְּשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ [hi ha-ishah teshuphekh rosh], the woman herself shall bruise your head; but הוּא, the seed (זֶרַע), namely of the woman, יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ [yeshuphekha rosh], he shall bruise your head, that is the seed itself shall bruise your head. Nor did Moses say again, "And you shall lie in wait for the heel of the woman"; but וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב [ve-attah teshuphenno aqev], and you shall bruise his heel, with the masculine pronoun referring to זֶרַע, seed, not the feminine pronoun referring to the woman. The Septuagint also agrees, if they looked more to the sense than to the words, with αὐτός, that is, υἱὸς τῆς γυναικός, or with αὐτό, referring to the noun: σπέρμα σου τηρήσει κεφαλήν [sperma sou tērēsei kephalēn], your seed shall guard the head, καὶ σὺ τηρήσεις αὐτῷ πτέρναν [kai sy tērēseis autō pternan], and you shall guard his heel, not αὐτὴ πτέρναν. But suppose the Latin Vulgate were authentic and the infallible rule of faith: then the woman herself, or the blessed Virgin, would have suffered her heel to be bruised for the deliverance of the human race, and by that bruised heel would have crushed the serpent's head; and it would not be the Son of Man Christ who did so. Behold, then, the blessed Virgin as the deliverer and redeemer of the human race. In vain does the Apostle ask earnestly, Was Paul crucified for you? 1 Cor. 1:13. Yet they present the blessed Virgin as the conqueror of the Devil and the trampler of the serpent's head; even the images set before the people for contemplation and adoration show the blessed Virgin treading down and crushing the serpent with her feet. But how could a mere creature, however blessed among women, crush the strength and kingdom of the Devil and be able to save the human race, when she herself needed a Saviour? My soul rejoices in God my Saviour, Luke 1:47. How could she save others from the tyranny of the Devil who could not save herself? Rather, having found God her Saviour, she joyfully celebrates him in her song. Certainly, if the blessed Virgin, a mere woman and man, was not unequal to crushing the serpent's head, then neither would the Son of Man, a mere man, be unequal to accomplishing so great a work. So the heresy of the Socinians is conquered and triumphs, and the cause of the divine nature of the Son of Man is wretchedly betrayed to the Socinians. Nevertheless, whatever the carnal little men may contrive, Jesus the Son of Man is the true Christ of God. In him we see the full fulfilment of the first prophecy and promise about the Messiah, on which all the others depend. Our one Jesus is the true Son of Man, the seed of the woman, of Eve and of the blessed Virgin; he alone suffered for the salvation of the human race, his heel being bruised; he alone crushed the serpent's head; he alone abolished the Devil, the emperor of death, by his death; he alone conquered for himself and for us sin, curse, death, the Devil and the world; he alone lives, reigns and rules, having received a name above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow. Whatever the heretics, the most pestilential seed of the serpent, may rage, roar or burst with rage.

units.la: 8o. Quid te in stuporem dat, fidelis anima, quam cernis in filio hominis, infirmitatis ac potentiae, authoritatis & ministerii, humilitatis & magnitudinis, perpessionum & gloriae, stupendam commissuram? Quid vagientem in cunis, & in stabuli praesepi jacentem, adoratum a Magis, & novae fulgore stellae signatum? Quid baptisatum in peccatoribus, & coeli aperti miraculo, ac solemni voce coelesti, filium Dei proclamatum? Quid tentatum a Diabolo, Angelorum famulitio con-decoradecoratum? Quid in scapha dormientem, imperio vocis ventos tempestatemque sonoram, fluctusque maris componentem? Quid Cæsari pendentem tributum, & simul exigentem ex pisce? Quid asino vehentem, ramorum palmis, ac Hosanna regio dignatum? Quid morientem in cruce, inter latrones ignominiosè pendulum, soli eclypsim, terræ horrorem, rupibus ac aulæo scissuram, sepulchris aperturam inferentem, ac mortuis viam præparantem ad vitam, stupescis? Discè mysterium filii hominis, & tritum ipsius calcaneum, Serpentis caput conterens, divinam filii hominis naturam, dignitatem ac potentiam infinitam, humanæ ac afflictissimæ naturæ conjunctissimam, dum te luculenter docebit, & admirationem eximet, quia aperiet causam ac rationem stupendæ plane commissuræ infirmitatis ac potentiæ, perpessionum ac gloriæ, filii hominis, in terris πολιτευομένυς.
units.tr: 8. What, faithful soul, fills you with astonishment, when you see in the Son of Man such a wonderful joining of weakness and power, authority and service, humility and greatness, sufferings and glory? Why do you marvel at him wailing in the cradle and lying in the manger of a stable, worshipped by the Magi and marked by the brightness of a new star? Why at him baptized among sinners, and proclaimed the Son of God by the miracle of the opened heavens and a solemn heavenly voice? Why at him tempted by the Devil, and attended by the service of angels? Why at him sleeping in a boat, and by the command of his voice calming the winds, the roaring storm and the waves of the sea? Why at him paying tribute to Caesar, and at the same time providing it from a fish? Why at him riding on an ass, and honoured with palm branches and a royal Hosanna? Why do you stand amazed at him dying on the cross, hanging shamefully among thieves, bringing an eclipse of the sun, a horror to the earth, a tearing of the rocks and the veil, an opening of the tombs, and preparing a way to life for the dead? Learn the mystery of the Son of Man: his bruised heel and his crushing of the serpent's head. This will teach you clearly and remove your wonder, for it will reveal the cause and reason of that wonderful joining of weakness and power, of sufferings and glory, in the Son of Man, who lived his life on earth [πολιτευόμενον].

units.la: 9º. Hinc docemur Ecclesiæ, cœtus fidelium, conditionem in terris. Ecclesia est Christus mysticus, & filius hominis, utpote semen mulieris, Apoc. 12:17. Quia filium hominis verbo & spiritu fidei in corde fictum ac vivum, & in ore, confessione partum gerit ac promit. O beatum prædestinationis in conformitatem filii Dei documentum! Callidas struet tibi insidias callidissimus Serpens, concupiscentia carnis, concupiscentia oculorum, vitæ superbia, te iteratis tentabit insultibus, mysticum semen mulieris. Fame laborabis ac siti, hominum opprobrium, mundi retrimentum habebere, plorabis, lamentaberis, & mundus lætabitur, crucem pone Christum gestabis, tritum patiere calcaneum, infirmum ac terrenum depones corpusculum. Mafte animo tamen, dum illæsum caput servabis, modicum adhuc tempus, Deus pacis Satanam conteret sub pedibus tuis. Interea temporis Angeli Dei descendentes in omnibus viis tuis te custodient, circumquaque castrametati, victoriam tandem, mysticum semen mulieris, reportabis æternam, de peccato, mundo, morte, ac Diabolo, necquicquam furente dracone: in nubibus triumphabis, ad occursum filii hominis, in cœlum rapiere, ut sis æternum cum Domino, alta quiete cum adorando Christo tuo in secula seculorum, victurum ac regnaturum, Amen.
units.tr: 9th. Hence we are taught the condition of the Church, the assembly of the faithful, on earth. The Church is the mystical Christ and the Son of Man, inasmuch as she is the seed of the woman (Rev. 12:17), because she bears and brings forth the Son of Man, formed in the heart by the word and the Spirit of faith and brought forth in the mouth by confession. O blessed proof of predestination to conformity with the Son of God! The most crafty Serpent, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, will lay cunning snares for you and assail you again and again, the mystical seed of the woman. You will labour with hunger and thirst, you will be the reproach of men and the offscouring of the world; you will weep and lament, and the world will rejoice. You will bear the cross of Christ, you will suffer your heel to be bruised, and you will lay down your weak and earthly little body. Yet take courage, while you keep your head unharmed: only a little while more, and the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet. Meanwhile the angels of God, descending, will guard you in all your ways, encamped on every side; and at last you will win eternal victory, O mystical seed of the woman, over sin, the world, death and the Devil, though the dragon rages in vain. You will triumph in the clouds, and at the meeting with the Son of Man you will be caught up into heaven, so that you may be eternally with the Lord, in deep rest, with your Christ whom you adore, living and reigning for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: QUÆSTIO III.
units.tr: QUESTION III.

units.la: Cur Jesus interdixerit discipulis suis ut nemini dicerent eum esse Christum, cum ipse se Filium hominis passim appellaverit, ut se esse Christum significaret?
units.tr: Why did Jesus forbid his disciples to tell anyone that he was the Christ, when he himself often called himself the Son of Man, in order to signify that he was the Christ?

units.la: Tunc interdixit discipulis suis, ut nemini dicerent, se esse Jesum illum Christum. Matth. 16: 20. Respondens vero Petrus dicit ei. Tu es ille Christus. Tunc interminatus est eis, ut nulli id dicerent de illo. Marc. 8: 29. 30. Vos vero quem me esse dicitis? Respondens autem Petrus dixit, Christum illum Dei. Ipse vero increpans illos, mandavit, ut nulli hoc dicerent. Luc. 9: 20. 21.
units.tr: Then he charged his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ. Matth. 16: 20. And Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ. And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing. Marc. 8: 29. 30. He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God. And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing. Luke 9: 20. 21.

units.la: IBERIUM Imperatorem, cognita, per litteras ex Palaestina, Jesu Christi apertè revelata divinitate, contendisse apud Senatum suffragii sui praerogativâ, ut consecratus in Deorum numerum referretur: sed & senatum respuisse, scribit Tertullianus apologet. c. 5. Nec mirum, noluisse Jesum, sapienter procurante ipsius providentia, nec homines habere propitios ut esset Deus, nec ex hominum arbitratu aeternam suam divinitatem pensari, nec inter fictitios gentium Deos censeri, qui erat aeternum Deus in saecula benedictus. Nihil pariter mirum, Jesum ab impuris spiritibus sibi testimonium perhiberi noluisse. Spiritus impurus clamat, Novi te quis sis, sanctus ille Dei, & objurgavit eum Jesus dicens, Obmutesce. Marc. 1: 24. 25. Spiritus impuri cum eum conspexerant, procidebant ei, & clamabant, dicentes, Tu es filius ille Dei, ipse vero vehementer interminabatur eis, ne manifestarent illum. Marc. 3: 11. 12. Luc. 4: 34. 35. Non passus est se promulgari Christum, ab impuris spiritibus, tum quia nulla est Christo cum Beliale communio, tum quia suprema veritas, ore mendacissimi Diaboli, mendacii suspicione, non erat commaculanda. Puri erant Angeli lucis, purus erat Johannes Baptista, plenus Spiritu sancto ex utero matris, puri erant discipuli Christi, jam vos puri estis propter sermonem, quem locutus sum vobis, Joh. 15: 3. Non abs re igitur voluit Jesus, ut Angeli lucis eum nascentem, e mortuis resurgentem, in coelum ascendentem, & e coelo denuò redeunredeuntem, Christum esse, mortalibus declararent. Voluit ut Johannes Baptista, eum Israeli manifestaret Christum, & venientem digito monstraret, sicut agnum Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Noluit vero discipulos suos, eum palam profiteri Christum: sed vehementer illis interdixit, ut nemini dicerent, illum esse Christum. Eccur vero memorabilis ista differentia in ferendo, vel non ferendo ifthoc solemni testimonio? Cur primum, Angelorum testimoniuum adhibuit, dum dilectorum suorum discipulorum testimonium vehementer recusavit? Eccur vero post triumphalem suam in coelum ascensionem, discipulorum adhibuit testimonium, de se Christo per orbem terrarum longe lateque ferendum, ubi sese constanter abstinuit ab adhibendo Angelorum testimonio? Respondemus, Jesum primum omnium Angelorum lucis testimonio usum, 1º. Quia Angelorum testimonium nullo jure poterat in dubium, vel suspicionem vocari: sunt enim Angeli lucis, quia Angeli sunt veritatis ac sanctitatis: non igitur ab iis metuendum est, ut falsum perhibeant testimonium: at nemo homo tunc plane conscius erat Jesum nascentem esse Christum, vel Jesum Christum esse e mortuis excitatum, vel Jesum ad coelum nube vehentem, esse denuo rediturum: nemo homo igitur hac de re testis locuples ac exceptione major erat & videbatur. 2º. Sicut in Jesu Christo duo sunt: alterum e coelo, alterum e terra: est enim e coelo, tum quatenus filius Dei, tum quatenus filius hominis, seu Christus, secundus Adam: est vero e terra, quatenus homo, non equidem ratione supernaturalis & miraculosae suae generationis: sed ratione humanae substantiae, quam duxit ab Adamo e terra creto: hac vero lege, ut quod in Christo e coelo est, primum fuerit; quod vero e terra, secundum. Ita sane divinae sapientiae conveniebat, ut primum omnium numen, Christo testes e coelo Angelos daret, homines vero postremum. Johannem Baptistam plenum Spiritu sancto ex utero matris, quod attinet, divina revelatione Dei mittentis, non modo Jesum esse Christum: quem Prophetae praenunciaverant, sed & implemento promissi indicii spiritus descendentis in eum sub specie columbae, noverat, Joh. 1: 32. 33. Quin & eum esse immolandum, uti victimam piacularem in mundi salutem noverat, plena revelatione facta sibi coelitus a Deo mittente: nec suspectum collusionis ejus testimonium, ullo jure quivis habere poterat: sancte enim non semel, sed iterum protestatur, Jesum sibi antehac fuisse incognitum, puta sicut mediatorem & Christum, Joh. 1: 31. 33. Cur vero Jesus non modo noluerit discipulorum suorum, tunc temporis, uti testimonio; sed & vehementer interdixerit, rit, ut nemini dicerent se esse Christum, cum ipse passim se filium hominis, dum Judaeos alloquererur, appellaverit, eo nempe consilio, ut se esse Christum, Judaeos doceret? Ardua quaestio est, solutuque dignissima, quam ut, allucente nobis Scriptura sacra, dextrè ac solidè perstringamus.
units.tr: We are told by Tertullian in his Apology, ch. 5, that the Emperor Tiberius, having learned from Palestine that the divinity of Jesus Christ had been plainly revealed, asked the Senate, by the prerogative of his own vote, that he be consecrated and enrolled among the gods, but that the Senate rejected the proposal. It is no wonder that Jesus did not want men to be favourable to him so that he might be God, nor that his eternal divinity should be weighed by human judgment, nor that he should be counted among the fictitious gods of the nations, when he is the God who is blessed for ever, the eternal God. Nor is it any more surprising that Jesus did not want to be given testimony by unclean spirits. The unclean spirit cried, saying, I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God. And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace. Marc. 1: 24. 25. And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God. And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known. Marc. 3: 11. 12. Luke 4: 34. 35. Christ did not allow himself to be proclaimed by unclean spirits, both because there is no fellowship between Christ and Belial, and because the supreme truth was not to be stained by the suspicion of falsehood coming from the mouth of the most lying Devil. The angels of light were pure, John the Baptist was pure, filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb, and the disciples of Christ were pure: now you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you, John 15: 3. It was therefore not without reason that Jesus willed the angels of light to declare to mortals that he was the Christ, when he was born, when he rose from the dead, when he ascended into heaven, and when he would come again from heaven. He willed that John the Baptist should make the Christ known to Israel, and point him out with his finger as he came, as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. But he did not want his disciples to profess openly that he was the Christ; rather he strictly forbade them to tell anyone that he was the Christ. Why this remarkable difference in accepting or not accepting such solemn testimony? Why did he first use the testimony of the angels, while he firmly refused the testimony of his beloved disciples? Why, after his triumphant ascension into heaven, did he use the testimony of the disciples, to be carried far and wide through the world concerning himself as Christ, when he had constantly refrained from using the testimony of the angels? We answer: Jesus used the testimony of the angels of light first of all, (1) because the testimony of the angels could by no right be called into doubt or suspicion. For they are angels of light, because they are angels of truth and holiness; there is therefore no fear that they will bear false witness. But no man at that time was fully aware that Jesus, when he was born, was the Christ, or that Jesus Christ had been raised from the dead, or that Jesus, carried up to heaven in a cloud, would return again. No man, therefore, was a witness in this matter who was adequate and beyond exception. (2) In Jesus Christ there are two things: one from heaven, the other from earth. For he is from heaven, both as the Son of God and as the Son of Man, or Christ, the second Adam; and he is from earth as man, not indeed by reason of his supernatural and miraculous generation, but by reason of the human nature which he took from Adam, who was formed from the earth. Yet the order holds that what is from heaven in Christ came first, and what is from earth came second. Thus it was fitting for divine wisdom that God should give witnesses from heaven, the angels, first of all, and men last. As for John the Baptist, filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb, he knew by the divine revelation of God who sent him not only that Jesus was the Christ whom the prophets had foretold, but also, by the fulfilment of the promised sign of the Spirit descending upon him in the form of a dove, he knew it. John 1: 32. 33. Indeed he also knew, by a full revelation made to him from heaven by God who sent him, that Jesus must be slain as the sacrificial victim for the salvation of the world. And no one could rightly have any reason to suspect that his testimony was a matter of collusion; for he solemnly protests, not once but again, that Jesus had been unknown to him until then, namely as Mediator and Christ. John 1: 31. 33. But why did Jesus not only refuse to use the testimony of his disciples at that time, but also strictly forbid them to tell anyone that he was the Christ, when he himself repeatedly called himself the Son of Man while speaking to the Jews, and that surely with the purpose of teaching the Jews that he was the Christ? This is a difficult question, most worthy of a solution, which we shall treat rightly and soundly, with holy Scripture shining upon us.

units.la: Observare operae pretium erit, 1º. Cum universa fere Judaeorum natio, & imprimis Scribae, Pharisaei, sacerdotum primarii, caeterique principes seculi Judaici, malè praeconceptis de Messia opinionibus, abrepti, vehementer negarent, Jesum esse Christum, quem Deus venturum promiserat, & Prophetae identidem praenunciaverant. Jesu discipulos, Deo Patre ipsis revelante, Matth. 16: 17. Eum esse verum Messiam, & firmiter credidisse, & saepe confessos fuisse Ioh. 6: 69. Verum ipsorum fidem, multis tunc implicitam, & labefactatam erroribus, quis negaverit? Noverant equidem Jesum esse Christum: sed parum assecuti mentem sapientissimam Dei, qualis reapse erat, non noverant. Jesum esse Christum, qualem universa Iudaeorum somniarat natio, credebant, regem puta terrenum ac opulentum; unde non semel eos audias, de primatu in regno Christi fervidè disceptantes, Matth. 18: 1. Luc. 9: 46. & Zebedaei filios, matre ipsorum obnixè efflagitante, primas sedes ad dextram & sinistram Christi in regno ipsius affectantes, Matth. 20: 20. 21. Jesum credebant esse Christum: sed hostibus suis terribili vindicta, Eliae ad instar, tremendum: unde Jacobum & Johannem audias, dicentes, Domine, vis dicamus ut ignis descendat è coelo & consumat eos, Luc. 9: 54. Jesum denique dum verum Christum credebant, eum venisse ut mortem oppeteret in salutem hominum, nedum mortem ignominiosam crucis, non ignorabant modò: sed & vehementer abhorrebant. Hinc Petrus, os Apostolorum, tacentibus ac consentientibus condiscipulis suis, audita Christi morte futura, eum coepit objurgare, dicens, propitius tibi esto, Domine, nequaquam erit tibi hoc, ut Christus illi repositerit, abscede à me, Satana, offendiculo es mihi, nam non sapis quae sunt Dei, sed quae sunt hominum: Matth. 16: 22. 23. Nec Petrus modò, sed & omnes discipuli, vel dum ipse Christus ore rotundo declarabat futuram suam mortem ac resurrectionem, penitus ignorabant, Christum moriturum & resurrecturum, Marc. 9: 10. 32. Ex fide, mundanis ejuscemodi conflictatâ erroribus, originem duxit tristis illa discipulorum animi infirmitas, & timor, quo subitò perculsi, omnes Jesum turpiter deseruere, & Petrus ipse, necquicquam obstante solemni promissione, quâ se Christo, vel ad mortem addixerat, in ternam incidit ipsius abnegationem, lapsu lamentabili. mentabili. Si quaeras, cur Deus majorem Spiritus revelationis mensuram de Christo suo, ipsius discipulis admetiri noluerit? Respondet Euangelista sacer, Nondum erat Spiritus sanctus, quia Jesus nondum erat glorificatus, Joh. 7: 39. Nam 1º. Spiritus sancti dona Christi regalia, plenum regii muneris Christi exercitium, sequi ac comitari par erat, Psal. 68: 19. 2º. Quia nec sapientiam nec justitiam Dei decebat, plenam Spiritus sui, communicationem affundere hominibus, eaque communionem, cum iis nectere intimam, nondum reapse placata sacrificio mortis Christi, ipsius ira, seu justitia, necdum per Christi resurrectionem, ascensionem in coelum, & sessionem ad dexteram Majestatis, justitiae divinae plena placatione declarata: nam Christus obedientia sua ad mortem crucis, non modo divinam placavit justitiam; sed & dona, tum extraordinaria, tum ordinaria Spiritus sancti, in electorum salutem consecutus est, ut jus eorum conferendorum per resurrectionem & glorificationem, & possessionem adiret. Unde Johannes, in spatio medio, thronum inter & quatuor animalia, & viginti quatuor seniores, agnum, sicut occisum, h. e. Christum, vidit stantem, habentem cornua septem & oculos septem, qui sunt septem Spiritus Dei missi in omnem terram, Apoc. 5: 6. En tibi agnum Christum, mortuum, & excitatum e mortuis: est enim sicut occisus: sed simul stans, h. e. e morte excitatus: sed ecce eum habentem plenitudinem donorum Spiritus sancti, ut eam mittat, & regalem in modum effundat in universam terram. 3º. Cum juxta adorandam trium personarum in salutis negotio oeconomiam, Spiritus sancti partes sint, intus revelare objecta, quae extra Euangelii praeconio revelavit, ut efficaci appulsu objectorum, externa praedicatione propositorum, fides cordibus electorum ingeneretur, (ideo enim tertia persona, & est, & dicitur Spiritus sanctus, & virtus altissimi.) Divinam sane decebat sapientiam, ut dona Spiritus sancti, externae objectorum Euangelii salutarium revelationi, commensurarentur. Cum igitur Jesu in terris πολιτευομένῳ, nondum omnia de eo ad credendum necessaria, ipso facto, ac implemento revelata forent objecta, nimirum violenta ejus, cruenta, ignominiosa, ac maledicta mors, victrix e sepulchro resurrectio, in coelum ascensio, & ad dexteram Dei patris sessio. Divinam sapientiam haud decuit, dona Spiritus illuminantis ac sanctificantis, tanta mensura effundere, quanta erant effundenda, post revelata externe per Jesu glorificationem, objecta omnia ad credendum de eo necessaria. 4º. Deus, qui edixit ut lux splendesceret e tenebris, lux radiantissima veritatis, tum Christi sui, tum Euangelii, ex erroribus, quibus super Christo tunc labefactabatur fides discipulorum, ut pelluceret, sapienter procuravit. Cum enim discipuli contra spem & opinionem suam, Jesum quem verum Messiam credebant, nec regnum terrenum Israëlis restituere, nec hostes suos carnales profligare, nec in media divitiarum affluentia regnare: sed in crucem ignominiosam, proh dolor, truculenter datum cernerent. Anne animo fracti, & qua sibi blandiebantur spe, prorsum decollata, Jesum æternùm deseruissent, ni ipse verus Dei Christus fuisset, qui omnipotenti Spiritus sui vorticordi efficacia, mentem, animosque eorum in melius commutasset?
units.tr: It will be worth observing, (1) that when almost the whole nation of the Jews, and especially the scribes, the Pharisees, the chief priests, and the other princes of the Jewish age, were carried away by wrongly preconceived opinions about the Messiah, they vehemently denied that Jesus was the Christ whom God had promised to send and whom the prophets had repeatedly foretold. The disciples of Jesus, with God the Father revealing it to them, Matth. 16: 17, both firmly believed that he was the true Messiah and often confessed it, John 6: 69. Yet who could deny that their faith, at that time entangled and weakened by many errors, was not sound? They indeed knew that Jesus was the Christ, but they had not grasped the most wise purpose of God, and did not know it as it truly was. They believed that Jesus was the Christ in the sense in which the whole nation of the Jews had dreamed him to be, namely an earthly and wealthy king. Hence you may hear them more than once disputing eagerly about primacy in the kingdom of Christ, Matth. 18: 1; Luke 9: 46, and the sons of Zebedee, their mother earnestly pleading for them, aspiring to the first seats at the right hand and the left of Christ in his kingdom, Matth. 20: 20. 21. They believed that Jesus was the Christ, but that he would be terrible to his enemies by a dreadful vengeance, after the manner of Elijah; hence you may hear James and John saying, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven and consume them? Luke 9: 54. Finally, while they believed him to be the true Christ, they not only knew that he had come to suffer death for the salvation of men, and above all the shameful death of the cross, but they also strongly shrank from it. Hence Peter, the mouth of the Apostles, while his fellow-disciples kept silent and agreed, when he heard of Christ's coming death, began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord; this shall not be unto thee; to whom Christ replied, Get thee behind me, Satan; thou art an offence unto me; for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men. Matth. 16: 22. 23. Not only Peter, but all the disciples, even while Christ himself plainly declared his coming death and resurrection, were utterly ignorant that Christ would die and rise again. Mark 9: 10. 32. From faith so troubled by such worldly errors arose that sad weakness and fear of the disciples' minds, by which, suddenly struck down, they all shamefully deserted Jesus, and Peter himself, though he had solemnly promised to go with Christ even to death, fell into threefold denial, a lamentable fall. If you ask why God was unwilling to grant his disciples a greater measure of the Spirit's revelation about his Christ? The sacred evangelist answers, The Holy Ghost was not yet given, because that Jesus was not yet glorified, John 7: 39. For (1) it was fitting that the royal gifts of the Holy Spirit should follow and accompany Christ's royal office, the full exercise of his kingly office, Psalm 68: 19. (2) Neither the wisdom nor the justice of God was becoming to pour out upon men the full communication of his Spirit, and to bind himself to them by an intimate fellowship, while his own wrath, or justice, had not yet been truly appeased by the sacrifice of Christ's death, and while it had not yet been declared, by Christ's resurrection, ascension into heaven, and sitting at the right hand of the Majesty, to be fully satisfied. For Christ, by his obedience unto the death of the cross, not only appeased divine justice, but also secured, for the salvation of the elect, both the extraordinary and the ordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit, so that he might acquire the right to bestow them by his resurrection, glorification, and possession of them. Hence John, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, saw a Lamb as it had been slain, that is, Christ, standing, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent forth into all the earth, Rev. 5: 6. Behold the Lamb, Christ, dead and raised from the dead; for he is as one slain, yet standing, that is, raised from death; and behold him possessing the fullness of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, so that he may send them and pour them out in royal fashion over the whole earth. (3) Since, according to the adorable economy of the three persons in the business of salvation, it is the part of the Holy Spirit to reveal inwardly the objects which the proclamation of the Gospel has revealed outwardly, so that by the effective impulse of the objects, the faith proposed by external preaching may be engendered in the hearts of the elect (for this is why the third person both is and is called the Holy Spirit, and the power of the Most High), it was truly fitting for divine wisdom that the gifts of the Holy Spirit should be proportioned to the external revelation of the saving objects of the Gospel. Therefore, while Jesus was still living on earth [πολιτευομένῳ, living as a citizen], not all the objects necessary for believing in him had yet been revealed by the actual fact and its fulfilment: namely his violent, bloody, shameful, and accursed death, his victorious resurrection from the tomb, his ascension into heaven, and his sitting at the right hand of God the Father. It did not become divine wisdom to pour out the gifts of the enlightening and sanctifying Spirit in such measure as they were to be poured out after the objects necessary for believing in him had been outwardly revealed through the glorification of Jesus. (4) God, who commanded that light should shine out of darkness, the most radiant light of truth, both of his Christ and of the Gospel, wisely arranged that it should shine forth out of the errors by which the faith of the disciples was then weakened concerning Christ. For when the disciples, contrary to their hope and opinion, saw that Jesus, whom they believed to be the true Messiah, neither restored the earthly kingdom of Israel, nor overthrew his carnal enemies, nor reigned in the midst of abundant riches, but was, alas, cruelly handed over to a shameful cross, would they not, broken in spirit and with the hope in which they had been flattering themselves utterly cut off, have forsaken Jesus for ever, unless he had been the true Christ of God, who by the powerful whirlwind of his almighty Spirit changed their minds and hearts for the better?

units.la: Observa 2°. Scribas & Pharisæos, cæterosque gentis Judaïcæ principes, abreptos perperam præconceptis de Christo opinionibus, Jesum odio æstuantissimo prosecutos, quòd se filium hominis & Christum palam profiteretur, vel dum sine forma ulla aspectabili, Christo, quem præstolabantur Judæi, dissimillimus videretur, ut Jesum in crucem dandum petierint, & tandem effecerint: hæc enim fuit condemnationis illius causa, ut ex Romanorum consuetudine αἰτία, crimen, seu titulus condemnationis omnibus conspiciendus Hebraicè, Græcè, ac Latinè propositus fuerit, Hic est Jesus Rex ille Judæorum. Matth. 27: 37.
units.tr: Observe, second. The Scribes and Pharisees, and the other leaders of the Jewish nation, carried away by preconceived opinions about Christ, pursued Jesus with the most burning hatred because he openly professed himself the Son of Man and the Christ, or because, lacking the outward appearance the Jews expected of Christ, he seemed utterly unlike him. So they sought and at last effected his being given up to the cross. For this was the cause of that condemnation: according to Roman custom the charge [αἰτία], the crime or title of the condemnation, was set out for all to see in Hebrew, Greek and Latin: This is Jesus the King of the Jews. Matt. 27:37.

units.la: Observa 3°. Internecinum, quo Pharisæi in Jesum æstuabant, odium, hoc longè vehementius fuisse inflammatum, quò magis Jesus inclarescebat miraculis: audito etenim aliquo Jesu miraculo, vel occultæ eum cum Diabolo insimulare amicitiæ, vel de eo perdendo, consilium protinus inire solebant. Matth. 12: 14. 24. Marc. 3: 6. Luc. 6: 11. Joh. 11: 47. 48. 49. 53.
units.tr: Observe, third. The deadly hatred with which the Pharisees raged against Jesus was kindled all the more fiercely the more he grew famous for his miracles. For whenever they heard of some miracle of Jesus, they straightway either accused him of a secret alliance with the Devil or set about plotting his destruction. Matt. 12:14, 24. Mark 3:6. Luke 6:11. John 11:47, 48, 49, 53.

units.la: Observa 4°. Jesum, quâ erat divinâ sapientiâ, & charitate adversus miseros homines, nec quicquam flagrante in se vatiniano Pharisæorum odio, noluisse abstinere sese à miraculosis sanationibus ægrorum mortalium: nec voluisse simul omnipotentem suam virtutem in coërcendis & profligandis Pharisæis, acerrimis suis adversariis, exercere, quia non venerat ad perdendos, sed servandos homines. Noluisse denique famam sibi conciliare ex miraculis, vel vim & authoritatem suam regalem, regum terrenorum ad instar, ostentare, ne Pharisæis Principibusque cæteris Iudæorum allubesceret, & perperam præconceptum de Messia rege terreno, errorem foveret, ne denique quovis modo sapientissimo ac justissimo Dei decreto, de Christo in crucem dando obstare videretur. Hinc factum, ut ita sapienter vitam suam attemperaverit, ut nec à miraculis in bonum & salutem hominum patrandis sese abstinuerit, nec ea in vulgus promulgari siverit: sed vehementer interdixerit, ne cuiquam decladeclararentur, ut sibi ab exacerbandis Pharisæorum animis caveret, ne ante præstitutum mortis tempus in eum furenter sævirent, & cursum prædicationis ipsius, vel beneficiorum retardarent, quandoquidem nolebat, vim & authoritatem suam potentem in iis coërcendis exercere, propter rationem quam memoravimus. Unde si quando, ut fieri assolet, præclari alicujus miraculi rumor percrebuisset, inflammatis hinc, & in ipsius perniciem grassantibus Pharisæis, clam ac dextrè eorum furori sese subducebat.
units.tr: Observe, fourth. Jesus, out of his divine wisdom and his love for wretched mortals, and with no regard for the Vatinian hatred of the Pharisees blazing against him, was unwilling to refrain from miraculous healings of sick mortals. Nor did he wish at the same time to exercise his almighty power in restraining and crushing the Pharisees, his bitterest adversaries, because he had not come to destroy men but to save them. Finally, he was unwilling to win fame for himself from his miracles, or to display his power and royal authority after the manner of earthly kings, lest he should please the Pharisees and the other leaders of the Jews, or foster their mistaken preconception of the Messiah as an earthly king, or in any way seem to stand in the way of God's most wise and just decree that Christ should be given up to the cross. Hence it came about that he so wisely regulated his life that he neither abstained from performing miracles for the good and salvation of men, nor allowed them to be publicized among the common people; rather, he strictly forbade that they be declared to anyone, so that he might guard against inflaming the minds of the Pharisees, lest they rage furiously against him before the appointed time of his death, and lest they hinder the course of his preaching or his benefits. For since he was unwilling to exercise his powerful authority in restraining them, he did so for the reason we have mentioned. Therefore, whenever, as is customary, the report of some distinguished miracle had spread, he would quietly and adroitly withdraw from the fury of the Pharisees, who were raging against him and kindled by it to his ruin.

units.la: Præmissis observationibus. Quæstioni præpositæ respondemus. Sapientissimè Iesum interdixisse discipulis, ne cuiquam dicerent eum esse Christum, vel dum ipse hac solemni filii hominis nomenclatura, sese identidem insigniërit, ut palam, se esse Christum, Iudæos doceret.
units.tr: Having set out these observations, we answer the question posed. Jesus most wisely forbade his disciples to tell anyone that he was the Christ, while he himself repeatedly marked himself out by this solemn title, Son of Man, so as to teach the Jews plainly that he was the Christ.

units.la: Primò quidem sapientissimè ex parte Discipulorum, multis de causis. 1º. Cum Iesum crederent esse Christum, non qualem Prophetæ prædixerant: sed qualem Iudæi somniarant venturum. Regem nempe terrenum, gentem suam à jugo Romanorum potenter liberaturum, & regnum Israëlis florentissimum in modum restauraturum. Cæterùm mortem ejus, nedum ignominiosam mortem crucis, ac resurrectionem ignorantes. Si nihil mentiti bona fide: sed pravâ sententiâ, Iesum esse Christum, palam annunciassent, falsum ex parte Christo perhibuissent testimonium, quod abs Christo veritatis Principe, oraculis Prophetarum, cœlesti Euangelii veritate, & miraculis, quibus ipsi Discipuli inclaruerant, quæque Deus omnipotenti sua virtute nunquam ac nusquam abusus, in mendacii aut falsitatis confirmationem adhibuit, quam maximè abhorrebat. 2º. Discipuli, juxta sententiam suam annunciantes, Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum, illum scilicet Regem Iudæorum, quem natio expectabat hostes suos profligaturum, Iudæos super Messia docuissent doctrinam planè contrariam doctrinæ, quam Iesus ipse docebat, dum se filium hominis appellabat, ad docendum, se esse semen promissum mulieris, passurum calcis contritionem, h. e. mortem, ex venenatis serpentis jaculis. Quare sanctus veritatis amor Christi, vetabat, ne per eum tunc liceret discipulis annunciare Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum. 3º. Fac, discipulos fuisse concionatos Iesum esse Christum, qualem nimirum Iudæi exspectabant, bellatorem illustrem, gentis suæ è Romanorum servitute liberatorem, ac præpotentem regni Israëlis restauratorem. Eventus contrarius, mortis nempe, resurrectionis & ascensionis Christi in cœlum, & eos miraculis spectatissimos, falsitatis reos, vel invitos palam arguisset, ut ipsi sua illa falsa prædicatione, & sibi, & testimonio, quod Christo post resurrectionem dicturi erant, fidem omnem abstulissent, & Iudæi jure optimo reposuissent. Inepti simus & stulti, si vobis vel miraculis claris, & contestantibus de Iesu resurrectione, & ascensione in cœlum, fidem adhibeamus, quos vel dudum miraculis spectatissimos, reos tenemus subleste fidei ac falsi testimonii. 4º. Si discipuli prædicassent Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum, qualem ipsi credebant, illum nempe Iudæis expectatum Messiam, Regem terrenum, hostes gentis suæ profligaturum: vel Iudæorum errorem super Messia fovissent, vel se deridendos ac exibilandos propinassent Pharisæis, nihil quicquam in Iesu Nazareno intuitis, quod expectati Messiæ sui, pompam secularem redoleret. 5º. Præposte-ra illa discipulorum prædicatio, Pharisæorum ac Scribarum nemini persuasisset, Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum, tum quia plebei erant, tum quia Iesu discipuli. Qui enim obsecro, despectissimorum aliquot homulorum ob legis ignorantiam, prædicatio, obstinatissimam vicisset Pharisæorum incredulitatem, quam vel ipsa miracula, quibus Prophetæ Messiam insignierant, quibusque se tunc Iesus commendabat, non poterant profligare? Frustra sane fuisset discipulorum prædicatio, suspecta conspirationis apud malignos seculi principes, continenter crediturós, discipulos in dicendo hujusmodi testimonio de compacto agere cum Christo, quem, dum miracula ederet, occultæ societatis, & nefariæ conspirationis cum Beelzebul Diabolorum principe, insimulare solebant. 6º. Cum Iudæi tunc temporis Christum in Regem Iudæorum spectarent, magis quam in Prophetam, non vero in Pontificem, animam suam positurum in victimam piacularem, & oblationem pro peccato. Si discipuli concionati Iesum Nazarenum esse illum Regem, plebem Iudaicam suo illo præconio in hanc pertraxissent sententiam, invidiam, & odium, tum principum seculi Iudaici, tum Romanorum, tantum Iesu creassent, ut continenter Iesum, rebellionis in Cæsarem, & regni affectati reum peractum, vi & armis ubivis exterminandum appetiissent. Unde alterutrum necessario consecuturum videbatur, vel Iesum exerciturum suam omnipotentem virtutem, ut vim coërceret hostilem, tum Pharisæorum, tum Romanorum, in ejus perniciem grassantium, quandoquidem nondum tempus mortis Christi venerat. Sed ne omnipotentem suam virtutem Christus tunc exerceret in profligandis hostibus suis, vetabant Prophetiæ, Jes. 42:1. 2. 3. 4. Matth. 12:18. Vetabant finis adventus Christi, non in perdendos, sed in servandos homines comparatus: status & conditio humilitatis & perpessionis, sapientia denique Christi: nam exercitio omniómnipotentis suæ virtutis in coërcendis & profligandis hostibus, errorem discipulorum, de se Christo, & gentis Iudaicæ de præpotenti Messia Rege terreno, foviflet, nedum curasset. Alterum igitur ex præpostera illa discipulorum prædicatione, ut consequeretur necesse erat, nimirum, ut Christus & sibi & discipulis viam omnem præcluderet annunciandi regnum Cœlorum, & miracula in bonum Iudaicæ gentis, veri Messiæ insignia, patrandi. 7º. Cum nec Christum fugeret, discipulos impulsu amoris adversus se, concionaturos, Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum, & ex illa prædicatione odium Pharisæorum immaniter exacerbandum, ut mortem ejus omni animi contentione accelerarent. Noluit, quâ erat sapientia, sanctum illum suorum discipulorum amorem, alió & in contrarium prorsus tendere, atque illi direxissent, nimirum in mortem venerabilis sui magistri promovendam. 8º. Cum juxta sapientissimum Dei consilium, Filius hominis Christus, mortem diram esset passurus ex inimicitia serpentis, Diaboli, & seminis ejus mundi. Noluit Christus, discipulos, semen suum spirituale, quicquam vel incogitantes conferre in mortem filii hominis. Momentum verò ac pondus præpostera illa prædicatione, invidiam & odium Pharisæorum in Christum inflammaturâ, contulissent. 9º. Hac sua interdictione, futuræ discipulorum afflictioni, sapiens ac bonus magister parcere voluit. Percellendos noverat discipulos suos vehementissima afflictione, cum eum viderent in crucem ignominiosam datum. Quantò verò penitius acriusque eos doluisset mortis ignominiosæ Domini sui, conscios se sua prædicatione odium Pharisæorum, proximam causam mortis Christi, proritasse & inflammasse. 10. Cum testimonium de Iesu, uti filio hominis, seu Christo, odium vatinianum parceret, apud animos Principum Iudæorum, discipulos illius veritatis præcones, opprobriis & morti multifariæ expositurset, discipulos inquam, tantæ tentationi ferendæ adhuc imparés, quod & fuga eorum, & tristis Petri Christum confessi, abnegatio, compertum fecit. Noluit igitur Iesus, quâ erat sapientia & bonitate, discipulos suos hac prædicatione, periculis, & atrocibus suppliciis exponere, ne infirmi metu mortis ad palinodiam adigerentur, quæ & veritatem muneris Mediatorii, & gloriam Christi labefactasset. Nihil ejusceinodi metuendum erat abs discipulis, Iesum Nazarenum esse Christum contestaturis, post ipsius mortem, resurrectionem, ascensionem in cœlum, & Spiritus sancti solemnem in eos effusionem. Nam & eventus, & plena Spiritus doctoris effusio, eorum animos pravis & perperam præconceptis de Christo erroribus purgaverat, & ipsis & univer-sis fis Iudæis percompertum fecerat, verum Dei Christum non esse Regem terrenum, nec in regnum seculare Israëlis restaurandum, venisse: sed in liberandos homines è Diaboli tyrannide, peccati, maledictionis, legis, & mortis servitute, & regnum ac cultum Dei, longè lateque per orbem universum, ejecto foras Principe hujus mundi Diabolo, constabiliendum. Nec metuendum erat, ut quovis obtentu legitimo, Pharisæi prætexerent, Christi discipulos falsum Iesu de compacto perhibere testimonium: nam ipsius discipuli, quæ propriis oculis usurpaverant, utut invidiosa ac exosa Pharisæis atque Romanis, imperterriti, vel sub flagris, & dira morte multifaria prædicabant, victi nempe veritatis evidentiâ, cum hinc, nec dignitates seculi, nec vitæ commoda aut divitias exspectarent: sed contraria plane opprobria, perpessiones, egestatem, flagrorum & suppliciorum omne genus ignominiam, ferrent ac consequerentur. Non denuò metuendum erat, ut salutari veritate plenè imbuti, & Spiritus sancti virtute muniti ac roborati, metu mortis fatiscerent, & ad palinodiam adigerentur. Supererat igitur, ut ipse Jesus, dum expectaret gloriosam suam resurrectionem, ascensionem, & plenam Spiritus sui in discipulos effusionem, unus prædicaret se esse filium hominis & Christum, quia nihil sibi metuebat, non nescius se esse Christum, qualem Prophetæ prædixerant, mortem oppetiturum maledictam & ignominiosam crucis, sua illa morte contriturum caput serpentis, exiturum è maledictione & morte per resurrectionem, & ascensurum in cœlum, victurum & regnaturum in omnem carnem. Cum enim in mundum venisset impulsu æterni amoris sui adversus Deum & electos, ut Deo se præberet obsequiosum ad mortem crucis, & Ecclesiam proprio sanguine redimeret. Tantum abest, ut mortis metu, ab hac veritate, de se Messia prædicanda, deterrendus foret, ut hanc illustrem confessionem coram Pilato ediderit, etsi hinc certò se manere maledictam & ignominiosam mortem resciret, Matth. 27: 11. Joh. 18: 37. 1. Tim. 6: 13.
units.tr: First, and most wisely, on the part of the disciples, for many reasons. (1) They believed Jesus to be the Christ, but not the kind the prophets had foretold, only the kind the Jews had dreamed would come: an earthly king who would powerfully free their nation from the yoke of the Romans and restore the kingdom of Israel to its former flourishing. They did not know of his death, still less of the shameful death of the cross, or of his resurrection. If they had openly proclaimed, in an evil opinion, that Jesus was the Christ, even though they were not lying and acted in good faith, they would have borne false witness on Christ's behalf. That would have been contrary to Christ, the Prince of truth, to the oracles of the prophets, to the heavenly truth of the Gospel, and to the miracles by which the disciples themselves had become famous. God, who is omnipotent, never and nowhere misuses his power, and he least of all would have employed it to confirm a lie or a falsehood. (2) If the disciples, announcing in their own sense that Jesus of Nazareth was the Christ, that is, that royal King of the Jews whom the nation expected to crush its enemies, had taught the Jews about the Messiah a doctrine utterly opposed to the one Jesus himself taught when he called himself the Son of Man, to teach that he was the promised seed of the woman who would suffer the bruising of the heel, that is, death, from the venomous strikes of the serpent, then Christ's holy love of truth forbade that it be permitted to the disciples at that time to proclaim that Jesus of Nazareth was the Christ. (3) Suppose the disciples had preached that Jesus was the Christ in the sense the Jews expected: a famous warrior, a liberator of his nation from Roman slavery, and a mighty restorer of the kingdom of Israel. The contrary outcome, namely the death, resurrection and ascension of Christ into heaven, would have openly convicted them, against their will, of falsehood, the very men who had been most conspicuously attested by miracles. Thus by that false preaching they would have stripped away all faith both from themselves and from the testimony they were to give about Christ after the resurrection, and the Jews would rightly have rejected them.
