The most wise Deity, therefore, who very often immediately appended to his proper name יהוה either the name אֲדֹנָי, or the name אֵלִין, as in Josh. 3:13, etc., or אֵל אֱלֹהִים, "God of gods," or simply, by ellipsis, אֱלֹהִים, by that glorious designation of himself signified that in the fullness of time he would be the Lord and God of gods over the whole earth. Therefore how very wisely the Seventy, Christ and the Apostles always rendered the tetragrammaton, wherever it occurs in the Old Testament, by Κύριον or Θεὸν.

units.la: Octavò, Quia ex nomine Dei proprio יהוה, invictissimum ducitur argumentum adversus Socinum, & gregales hæreticos divinæ naturæ Christi hostes infensissimos, illud enim Christo Dei filio non raró tribuitur in novo Instrumento, Christus enim passim Κύριος Dominus, & Θεὸς Deus appellatur. Sed enim verò firmum solidumque ut sit ductum pro Divinitate Christi ex nomine Κύριος, vel Θεὸς, argumentum, primùm omnium constituendum, certòque tenendum est quid Deus Israëlis proprie, directè, & per se se significare voluerit suo illo nomine proprio יהוה, quod Septuaginta, Christus, & Apostoli per Κύριον, vel Θεὸν, reddidere. Hic enim itur in varia sententiarum divortia. Alii enim existimant sibi Deum fecisse proprium indigitamentum יהוה, æternam suam essentiam, quatenus auctor, & causa est existendi rebus omnibus, ut indigitaret. Alii suam veracitatem, fidelitatem, & constantiam in exequendis minis, & implendis promissionibus, vel utrumque simul, suo illo nomine proprio, proprie significasse. Ambæ illæ sententiæ de propria significatione nominis Tetragrammati apud omnes veteres Hebræos, Græcos, Latinosque Doctores, ita passim obtinuere, ut vix unus contra hiscere ausus fuerit, ne cornicum oculos configere videretur. Quibus fulti rationibus utramlibet sententiam propugnaverint, ad lancem sanctuarii, rectæque rationis stateram ponderare, momentosum erit operæ pretium, ut vera demum sententia in clara luce constituta, & ab omnibus Socinianorum strophis solidè vindicata, ex nomine Κύριος, vel Θεὸς in fœdere novo, nominis proprii יהוה vicario, sua constet Christo Divinitas æterna illibata, & intemerata.
units.tr: Eighthly, because a most invincible argument against Socinus and his fellow heretics, the most hostile enemies of the divine nature of Christ, is drawn from the proper name of God, יהוה. For in the New Testament that name is frequently ascribed to Christ the Son of God, since Christ is everywhere called Κύριος, Lord, and Θεὸς, God. But in order that the argument for the divinity of Christ from the names Κύριος or Θεὸς may be firm and solid, it must first of all be established and held for certain what the God of Israel properly, directly and of himself meant to signify by that proper name יהוה, which the Seventy, Christ and the Apostles rendered by Κύριον or Θεὸν. For here opinions diverge in various directions. Some think that God made יהוה his proper designation in order to signify his eternal essence, insofar as he is the author and cause of the existence of all things. Others hold that by that proper name he properly signified his truthfulness, faithfulness and constancy in carrying out his threats and fulfilling his promises, or both together. Both of these opinions about the proper meaning of the tetragrammaton have so widely prevailed among all the ancient Hebrew, Greek and Latin teachers that scarcely anyone has dared to object, lest he seem to be poking the eyes of crows. It will be a worthwhile labour to weigh on the scales of the sanctuary and the balance of right reason the reasons with which each side has defended its view, so that, once the true opinion has been set in clear light and solidly vindicated from all the twistings of the Socinians, it may be established from the name Κύριος or Θεὸς in the New Testament, as a substitute for the proper name יהוה, that the eternal divinity of Christ stands unimpaired and inviolate.

units.la: QUÆSTIO XVIII. Vtrum Deus יהוה nomen proprium sibi fecerit, ut proprie, directè ac per sese significaret æternam essentiam suam, quatenus auctor & causa est rerum omnium?
units.tr: QUESTION XVIII. Whether God made יהוה his proper name so that it would properly, directly and of itself signify his eternal essence, insofar as he is the author and cause of all things?

units.la: Ita sentiunt. 1°. Omnes Hebræorum magistri, unde nomen יהוה vocant שם ההויה & שם הטצם nomen essentiæ, seu substantiæ, ut liquidò constat ex Maimonide lib. 1. More Nevochim. c. 60. Et laudant Esa. 42. 5. Amo. 5. 9. 2°. Philo Judæus, qui nomen quadriliterum vocat ὄνομα τὸ ὂν, nomen entis, h. e. illius qui est κατ' ἐξοχὴν, & cæteris omnibus causa est ut sint. 3°. Septuaginta Interpretes, qui Dei responsum ad Mosem אהיה אשר אהיה Ero qui ero, vertunt ἐγὼ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ego sum qui sum. Exod. 3: 14. etsi alias nomen יהוה vertunt ἔσται, Erit, ut infra notabimus. 4°. Latini Doctores ut Hieronymus in Epist. ad Ephes. c. 3. Loquitur, inquit, in Exodo Dominus, Ego sum qui sum. Et hæc dices filiis Israël, qui est misit me ad vos. Nunquid solus Deus erat, & cætera non erant? Utique Angeli, cœlum, terra, & maria, & ipse Moses cui Dominus loquebatur, & Israël, & Ægyptii, ad quos & contra quos princeps & adversarius mittebatur, erant. Et quomodo nomen commune substantiæ sibi proprium vendicat Deus? Illa ut diximus causa, quia cætera ut sint, Dei sumpsere beneficio, Deus verò qui semper est, nec habet aliunde principium, & ipse sui origo est, suaque causa substantiæ, non potest intelligi aliunde habere quòd subsistit. Augustino eadem mens fuit. Ego sum qui sum. Ecce, inquit, nomen incommutabilitatis. Omnia enim quæ mutantur, desinunt esse quod erant, & incipiunt esse quod non erant. Esse verum, esse sincerum, esse germanum non habet, nisi qui non mutatur. Ille habet esse, cui dicitur, mutas ea & mutabuntur; tu autem idem ipse es. Quid est ego sum qui sum, nisi æternus sum? Quid est ego sum, qui sum, nisi mutari non possum? Nulla creatura, non cœlum, non terra, non Angelus, non virtus, non sedes, non potestates. 5°. Ita sentit Bellarminus, & ferè omnes Pontificii Doctores. 6°. Ita sentiunt plerique omnes Orthodoxi Doctores, unde Galli in sua Versione nomen Tetragrammatum constanter reddunt l'Eter-
units.tr: They hold this view. (1) All the Hebrew teachers, whence they call the name יהוה the שם ההויה [shem ha-havayah] and the שם הטצם [shem ha-etzem], the name of essence or substance, as is clear from Maimonides, More Nevochim, book 1, ch. 60. They also cite Isa. 42:5 and Amos 5:9. (2) Philo the Jew, who calls the four-letter name ὄνομα τὸ ὂν [onoma to on], the name of Being, that is, of him who is κατ' ἐξοχὴν [kat' exochēn], preeminently, and is the cause of all other things that they exist. (3) The Seventy, who render God's answer to Moses, אהיה אשר אהיה [Ehyeh asher ehyeh], "I will be who I will be", as ἐγὼ εἰμι ὁ ὤν [egō eimi ho ōn], "I am who I am" (Exod. 3:14), although elsewhere they render the name יהוה as ἔσται [estai], "he will be", as I shall note below. (4) The Latin teachers, such as Jerome in his Epistle to the Ephesians, ch. 3: "The Lord speaks in Exodus", he says, "I am who I am. And you shall say these things to the sons of Israel: he who is has sent me to you. Was God alone then, and the other things were not? Surely the angels, heaven, earth and seas, and Moses himself to whom the Lord was speaking, and Israel, and the Egyptians, to whom and against whom the prince and adversary was sent, were there. And how does God claim for himself a name common to substance?" For the reason, as we have said, is that other things, that they may exist, have received it by God's favour, but God, who always is, and has no principle from elsewhere, is himself the origin of himself and the cause of his own substance; he cannot be understood to have from elsewhere that he subsists. Augustine held the same mind: "I am who I am. Behold," he says, "the name of unchangeableness. For all things that change cease to be what they were and begin to be what they were not. He alone has true, pure and genuine being who does not change. He has being to whom it is said: you change them and they will be changed, but you are the same. What is 'I am who I am' but 'I am eternal'? What is 'I am who I am' but 'I cannot be changed'? No creature has this, not heaven, not earth, not an angel, not a power, not a throne, not the authorities." (5) So Bellarmine thinks, and nearly all the Papist teachers. (6) So think almost all the orthodox teachers; hence the French, in their version, consistently render the Tetragrammaton as l'Eternel,

units.la: Inter opera Augustini. Tomo sexto ad finem. l'Eternel, quasi Deus augustissimo isthoc indigitamento essentiae suae aeternitatem significare voluerit. Liceat nobis non novitatis, sed potius antiquitatis studio, Dei veritatis in Scriptura revelatae amore, pioque desiderio non nihil lucis foenerandae veteris Scripturae mysteriis, hac in re, bona cum eorum venia, ab hac ipsorum, Rabbinorumque sententia discedere. Quibus fulti rationibus, aequo ut perpendant animo, pro solita sua charitate, etiam atque etiam rogamus.
units.tr: "the Eternal", as if God had wished to signify the eternity of his essence by this most august designation. Among the works of Augustine, vol. 6, at the end. Let us be allowed, not from a love of novelty but rather from a zeal for antiquity, from love of the truth of God revealed in Scripture, and from a pious desire to gain some light from the mysteries of the old Scripture, in this matter, with their good leave, to dissent from this opinion of theirs and of the rabbis. Supported by these arguments, we ask them, in their accustomed charity, to weigh them fairly, again and again.

units.la: Primum omnium notasse operae pretium erit, hic non quaeri num per legitimam consequentiam ex nomine proprio יהוה, Dei aeternitas ut causa est rerum omnium, elici possit. Sed vero id dumtaxat quaeritur, num Deus ea mente, eoque consilio, nomen יהוה proprium sui fecerit indigitamentum ut proprie, & directe significaret se esse essentia aeterna praeditum, & causam rerum omnium? Ita fere omnes sentiunt. Nos Deum aeternum coeli & terrae ab initio viarum suarum conditorem venerati, non existimamus tamen sapientissimum illum rerum omnium auctorem sibi fecisse proprium indigitamentum יהוה aeternam suam essentiam ut causa est rerum omnium Mosi & Israelitis proprie, directe, & per se ut significaret.
units.tr: First of all it will be worth noting that the question here is not whether the eternity of God as the cause of all things can be drawn by legitimate inference from the proper name יהוה. Rather, the question is only this: did God, with that mind and purpose, make יהוה his proper designation, so that it would properly and directly signify that he is endowed with an eternal essence and is the cause of all things? Almost everyone holds this. We, who worship the eternal God, the Creator of heaven and earth, the beginning of his ways, do not, however, think that that most wise author of all things made יהוה his proper designation so that it would properly, directly and of itself signify to Moses and the Israelites his eternal essence as the cause of all things.

units.la: Primo igitur quaerimus num propria illa nominis יהוה significatio Mosi innotuerit, cum primum Deus ipsi praecepit. Dices filiis Israel יהוה ad vos me misit? Si negent, rogabo, quomodo illis propria isthaec augustissimi nominis significatio potius innotuerit quam Mosi? Si ajunt. Quando significatio isthaec nominis proprii obvia Mosi supponitur. Qui factum cum Deus יהוה sit, & passim perhibeatur coeli & terrae creator, ut Job. 12:9. Zachar. 12:1. Ut Moses ubi historiam creationis pertexuit toto capite primo Genes. nusquam tamen Deum יהוה appellaverit? Moses enim primo illo capite GenesEos Deum triginties ut minimum nominavit Elohim: Sed constanter abstinuit se se ab isthoc glorioso Dei nomine. Imo quod summa consideratione dignum nemini non videbitur, postquam secundo, tertio, & quarto capitibus saepe saepius Deum vocaverit יהוה אלוהים, aliquanto post ubi repetit memoratque creationem hominis, constanter sese abstinet ab hoc nomine יהוה, ut semper Deum vocet Elohim, ut Genes. 5:1 Hic est numerus generationum hominis in die quo Elohim creavit hominem, fecitque illum in similitudine Elohim. Et Genes. 9:6. Sanguis ejus effundetur, qui effundet sanguinem hominis, per hominem, quia in imagine Elohim fecit hominem. Utique dicendum erat in principio creavit יהוה cælum & terram. In imagine יהוה fecit hominem. Quia in imagine יהוה fecit hominem. Utique nemo non videt in omnibus creationis diebus creatorem Deum proprio sui indigitamento יהוה difignandum fuisse, fi Moysi revelaverit se vocatum iri יהוה ad significandum proprie æternam suam essentiam quatenus creator est cœli & terræ, & singulari ratione hominis, quandoquidem homo anima sua spirituali, & immortali eximia imago est Dei spiritualis & immortalis, & aeterna Dei cum potentia, tum divinitas ex creatione mundi animadversa pervidentur. Rom. 1: 20. Hinc liquidius mero meridie colligitur, nomen istud gloriosum יהוה non esse signum & memoriale æternæ Dei essentiæ, quatenus creator est, & causa rebus omnibus ut sint.
units.tr: First, then, we ask whether that proper meaning of the name יהוה was known to Moses when God first commanded him: Say to the sons of Israel, יהוה has sent me to you? If they deny it, I will ask how that proper meaning of this most august name became known to others rather than to Moses. If they affirm it, then this meaning of the proper name is assumed to have been obvious to Moses. Since God is יהוה, and is everywhere called the creator of heaven and earth, as in Job 12:9 and Zech. 12:1, why did Moses, when he related the history of creation throughout the whole first chapter of Genesis, nowhere call God יהוה? For in that first chapter of Genesis Moses named God at least thirty times Elohim, but he consistently abstained from that glorious name of God. Indeed, what will seem worthy of the greatest consideration to anyone: after he had often called God יהוה אלהים in the second, third and fourth chapters, a little later, when he repeats and recounts the creation of man, he consistently abstains from this name יהוה and always calls God Elohim, as in Gen. 5:1: This is the book of the generations of man; in the day that Elohim created man, in the likeness of Elohim he made him. And Gen. 9:6: Whoso sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of Elohim he made man. Surely it should have said in the beginning יהוה created heaven and earth; in the image of יהוה he made man; because in the image of יהוה he made man. Surely everyone sees that on all the days of creation the Creator God ought to have been designated by his proper designation יהוה, if he had revealed to Moses that he would be called יהוה to signify properly his eternal essence insofar as he is the creator of heaven and earth, and by a singular reason of man, since man, by his spiritual and immortal soul, is the distinguished image of God, spiritual and immortal, and the eternal power and divinity of God are clearly seen from the creation of the world (Rom. 1:20). Hence it is more plainly gathered, in broad daylight, that this glorious name יהוה is not a sign and memorial of the eternal essence of God insofar as he is the creator and the cause of all things that they exist.

units.la: Percontanti nunc temporis cur Moses Deum appellavit יהוה אלהים ubi aggreditur ad Historiam creationis Adami τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος, figura futuri Adami. Rom. 5: 14. lapsus Adami, & ad promissionem seminis mulieris contrituri caput serpentis? Respondemus quia Moses noverat, & nos docere voluerat nomen tremendum יהוה non significare æternam Dei essentiam, ut causa est rerum omnium: sed habere necessariam habitudinem ad Adamum futurum, & hominem peccatorem liberandum, & caput serpentis hoc est diaboli conterendum, ut liquidius infra parebit.
units.tr: Now, if someone asks why Moses called God יהוה אלהים when he came to the history of the creation of Adam, the type of the one to come [τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος], the figure of the future Adam (Rom. 5:14), with the fall of Adam and the promise of the seed of the woman who would crush the serpent's head? We answer: because Moses knew, and wished to teach us, that the awesome name יהוה does not signify the eternal essence of God as the cause of all things, but has a necessary relation to the future Adam, and to the man who is to be freed from sin, and to the crushing of the serpent's head, that is, of the devil, as will become clearer below.

units.la: Secundò, Deus asserit se hactenus revelasse Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo, in nomine אל שדי Dei omnipotentis & sufficientis: sed non innotuisse illis in nomine suo יהוה. Exod. 6: 3. Sed hæc à tramite veritatis longe abessent (absit verbo blasphemia) si nomen יהוה proprie, & ex primo Dei instituto essentiam illius æternam significaret. Quod liquet 1°. quia impossibile est Deum cognoscere omnipotentem, & omni creatura sufficientem, quin prius eum cognoscas simul ut Deum, hoc est essentia æterna, & infinita præditum, simul ut creatorem. Unde sequeretur Abrahamum, Isaacum, & Jacobum, prius cognovisse Deum in nomine יהוה, hoc est ut ens æternum, & causam rerum omnium, quam in nomine El Schaddai, omnipotentis & sufficientis. Sed Deus contrarium ἀλγεινόν asserit. 2°. Quia conceptus essentiæ & existentiæ (quæ in Deo unum sunt) antecedit necessariò conceptum omnipotentiæ, & sufficientiæ; nempè, impossibile est aliquem concipere potentissimum, & sufficientissimum, quin prius concipiat eum esse, seu existere. Ergò cum Abrahamus cognoverit Deum esse omnipotentem, & sibi omnibusque creaturis sufficientem, prius noverat Deum esse, seu existere, æternum causam rerum omnium. Noverat igitur Deum esse יהוה, utique si nomen illud significaret essentiam Dei aeternam, & immutabilem, sed id Deus verbotim negat, & absolutam esse negationem, quae omnem ab Abrahamo nominis יהוה notitiam removet, adversus Buxtorfium caeterosque supra demonstravimus.
units.tr: Second, God asserts that hitherto he had revealed himself to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the name אל שדי [El Shaddai], God Almighty and All-sufficient, but had not made himself known to them by his name יהוה (Exod. 6:3). But these things would be far from the path of truth (let me not say blasphemy) if the name יהוה properly, and from God's first institution, signified his eternal essence. This is clear, first, because it is impossible to know God as almighty and sufficient for every creature without at the same time knowing him as God, that is, endowed with eternal and infinite essence, and at the same time as the Creator. Whence it would follow that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob knew God first in the name יהוה, that is, as the eternal being and the cause of all things, before they knew him in the name El Shaddai, almighty and all-sufficient. But God asserts the contrary, a grievous thing [ἀλγεινόν]. Second, because the concept of essence and existence (which are one in God) necessarily precedes the concept of omnipotence and sufficiency; that is, it is impossible to conceive someone as most powerful and most sufficient without first conceiving that he is, or exists. Therefore, since Abraham knew God to be almighty and sufficient for himself and for all creatures, he had first known that God is, or exists, eternal, the cause of all things. He therefore knew God to be יהוה, certainly if that name signified the eternal and unchangeable essence of God. But God plainly denies this, and that denial is absolute, and it removes from Abraham all knowledge of the name יהוה, as we have demonstrated above against Buxtorf and the others.

units.la: Tertiò, Qui Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo innotuit ut creator & conservator, summus coeli & terrae possessor, uterum claudens & aperiens, utique illis innotuit in nomine יהוה; si id indigitamenti proprie & directe significet Deum, quatenus est ens aeternum creator coeli & terrae, daneque rebus omnibus ut sint. Atqui Deus innotuit Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo ut summus possessor coeli & terrae. Gen. 14: 22. ut uterum claudens & aperiens. Genes. 20: 18. Fuit igitur Patriarchis cognitus nomine suo יהוה siquidem id nominis proprie significet Deum, quatenus est ens aeternum, & creator coeli & terrae. Sed enim vero ipse Deus expressis verbis negat se fuisse cognitum Patriarchis nomine suo יהוה, quod absolutam Dei in nomine יהוה ignorantiam significat, ut supra solidis rationibus addiximus.
units.tr: Thirdly, he who was made known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as creator and preserver, the highest possessor of heaven and earth, who closes and opens the womb, was surely made known to them under the name Jehovah [יהוה]. That would be so if this designation properly and directly signified God as the eternal being, the creator of heaven and earth, who gives existence to all things. But God was made known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as the highest possessor of heaven and earth. Gen. 14:22. Who closes and opens the womb. Gen. 20:18. Therefore the name Jehovah would have been known to the patriarchs, if that name properly signifies God as the eternal being and creator of heaven and earth. But God himself expressly denies that he was known to the patriarchs by his name Jehovah, which signifies complete ignorance of God in the name Jehovah, as we have shown above with solid reasons.

units.la: Quartò. Si nomen יהוה directe & proprie significaret Deum, ex ipso Dei instituto, quatenus est ens aeternum, non solum Abrahamus, Isaacus, & Jacobus Deum cognovisset in nomine יהוה, quod supra addiximus: Sed & gentes quaevis idololatrae. Ratio consequentiae est. 1°. Quia gentes noverunt Deum esse ens aeternum, & mundi conditorem: Nam τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, Ethnicis fuit manifestatum, nempe, cum ipsius aeterna potentia, tum divinitas in operibus creationis. Rom. 1: 20. 21. 2°. Quia Ethnicorum monumenta ubivis clamant eos cognovisse Deum esse ens aeternum, & causam rerum omnium. Hinc Minerva Aegyptiorum Saitana. Ἐγὼ εἰμὶ πᾶν τὸ γεγονὸς, καὶ ὂν, καὶ ἐσόμενον. Τὸν ἐμὸν πέπλον οὐδεὶς πω ἀπεκάλυψεν· ὃν ἔτεκον καρπὸν ἠλιος ἐγέννησε. Ego sum, quae fuerunt, quae sunt, quae futura sunt. Velum meum nemo mortalium revelavit, quem peperi fructum, sol est natus. Hinc Ethnicis sol ὁ ἥλιος, יִוְיִ, excelsus, supremus. Et Apollo pictus semper juvenis, scilicet senectutis expers ad perpetuam & umbrae mutationis nesciam, numinis constantiam, indigitandam. Et valvis templi Delphici affixum literis uncialibus EI, ut Deum nunquam de statu suo exire significarent, quod & apprime noverat Plutarchus ubi ita commentatur. Est illa, inquit, perfectissima compellatio Dei, Una cum verbo ipso considerandam animo pronuntiantis vim numinis objiciens. Deus enim unquamquemque nostrum huc accedentem, veluti salutans compellat, inquiens, nosce te ipsum, quod nihilo est, quam salve deterius. Nos vicissim respondentes Deo Et, Es dicimus: veram, certam, & solam, soli convenientem appellationem illi vendicantes. Etenim revera, nos quidem essentia non sumus participes: verum universa mortalis natura, tanquam in medio versatur ortus, & interitus: obscuram atque instabilem, & veluti fugientem existendi opinionem, atque speciem exhibens. Praeterea Ethnici idololatrae noverunt Deum esse hominum parentem. Unde Aratus Ζεὺς ἐκ γὰρ ἡμέτερον γένος ἐσμέν. Summus enim Dei progenies. Act. 17: 28. Et Homerum, Hesiodumque audias, Deum in haec verba compellantes Ζεῦ πάτερ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε. Jupiter pater hominum atque Deorum. Atqui idololatrae, Israelita, Ethnicusve suat, יהוה non cognoverunt. Non dirigunt opera sua ad reverendum ad Deum suum, quia spiritus fornicationum, h. e. idololatriae, est in interiori eorum & יהוה non cognoverunt. Hos. 5: 4. Haec de Israelitis.
units.tr: Fourthly. If the name <bl>Jehovah</bl> directly and properly signified God, as the eternal being, by God's own appointment, then not only Abraham, Isaac and Jacob would have known God by the name <bl>Jehovah</bl>, as we have said above, but also every idolatrous nation. The reasoning behind this consequence is as follows. First, because the nations knew that God is an eternal being and the author of the world. For what is known of God [τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ] was made manifest to the heathen, namely his eternal power and his divinity, seen in the works of creation. Rom. 1:20, 21. Second, because the monuments of the heathen cry out everywhere that they knew God to be an eternal being and the cause of all things. Hence the Egyptian Minerva of Sais: "I am all that has been, that is, and that will be; no mortal has yet lifted my veil; the fruit that I bore is the sun that was born" [Ἐγὼ εἰμὶ πᾶν τὸ γεγονὸς, καὶ ὂν, καὶ ἐσόμενον. Τὸν ἐμὸν πέπλον οὐδεὶς πω ἀπεκάλυψεν· ὃν ἔτεκον καρπὸν ἠλιος ἐγέννησε.]. Hence among the heathen the sun was called ho hēlios [ὁ ἥλιος], and Jove [יִוְיִ], meaning exalted, supreme. Apollo was always painted as a youth, free of old age and so of any change of shadow, to signify the constancy of the godhead. And the letters EI, in capitals, were affixed to the doors of the Delphic temple, to signify that God never departs from his state; Plutarch knew this very well and comments thus: This is that most perfect address of God, he says, which, together with the word itself, sets before the mind the power of the one who pronounces it. For God, as it were greeting each of us as we approach, addresses us, saying, "Know yourself," which is nothing less than "Hail" [χαῖρε]. In turn we answer God with "Thou art" [Εἶ]: claiming for him the true, certain and only appellation, which belongs to him alone. For in truth we ourselves do not share in being; rather, all mortal nature, lying between birth and death, presents only an obscure and unstable opinion of existence, a fleeting appearance.* Moreover, the idolatrous heathen knew that God is the father of men. Hence Aratus: "For we are indeed his offspring" [Ζεὺς ἐκ γὰρ ἡμέτερον γένος ἐσμέν]; for this is the highest progeny of God. Acts 17:28. And if you listen to Homer and Hesiod, they address God in these words: "Father Zeus of men and gods" [Ζεῦ πάτερ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε]: Jupiter, father of men and of gods. But idolaters, whether Israelite or heathen, did not know <bl>Jehovah</bl>. They do not direct their works toward returning to their God, because the spirit of harlotry, that is, of idolatry, is within them, and they did not know <bl>Jehovah</bl>. Hos. 5:4. So much for the Israelites.

units.la: Ethnicos quod attinet, centies apud Prophetas praenuntiatur fore ut gentes cognoscant Deum esse יהוה. Gentes igitur non noverant Deum esse יהוה. Verum apprime noverant Deum esse ens aeternum, parentem hominum & causam rerum omnium, ut supra. Unde in expedito concludere est, nomen יהוה non significare proprie & directe Deum, quatenus est ens aeternum, & causa rerum omnium.
units.tr: As for the heathen, it is foretold a hundred times by the Prophets that the nations will come to know that God is <bl>Jehovah</bl>. Therefore the nations did not know that God is <bl>Jehovah</bl>. Yet they very well knew that God is an eternal being, the parent of men and the cause of all things, as above. Hence it is easy to conclude that the name <bl>Jehovah</bl> does not properly and directly signify God as an eternal being and the cause of all things.

units.la: Nec quicquam regerere juvat nosse Deum esse יהוה, apud Prophetas significare, amare Deum יהוה, figura antecedentis pro consequente, quia ex cognitione amor. Reponimus enim ut haec figura obtineat multis in Scripturae locis, nullum tamen habere usum, in locis illis frequentissimis, ubi Prophetae recipiunt fore ut gentes cognoscant Deum esse יהוה, id enim passim asserunt ubi sermonem habent, de Dei vindicta in perdendos Deos, & delendos Ethnicos idololatras, idolorum cultores. Illa enim יהוה indenda Ethnicis notitia, nulla erat ad amorem יהוה ingenerandum, comparata; sed contra ad metum, odiumque, severi illius vindicis ad internecionem יהוה.
units.tr: Nor does it help to reply that, in the Prophets, to know that God is <bl>Jehovah</bl> means to love God <bl>Jehovah</bl>, a figure in which the antecedent stands for the consequent, since love arises from knowledge. For we answer that although this figure holds in many places of Scripture, it has no place in those most frequent passages where the Prophets declare that the nations will come to know that God is <bl>Jehovah</bl>. For they say this everywhere when they speak of God's vengeance on the gods who are to be destroyed and on the heathen idolaters, the worshippers of idols. For that knowledge of <bl>Jehovah</bl> which the heathen were to gain was not designed to produce love for <bl>Jehovah</bl>, but on the contrary fear and hatred of that severe avenger, and destruction at his hand.

units.la: Quintò. Robur non mediocre praecedenti rationi accedit, quod & novam suppeditat ex isthac observatione non contemnenda. Nempe, ubivis viri Dei alloquuntur Ethnicos Dei viventis ignaros, nunquam, nusquam Deum vocant יהוה, si loca illa seposueris ubi notitiam Dei sui cujus nomine loquuntur, iis indere satagunt. Ita Moses ad Pharaonem, hoc cognosces me esse יהוה Exod. 7: 16, 17. Expandam volas manuum ad יהוה, & tonitrua cessabunt, &c. ut noveris terram pertinere ad יהוה. Exod. 9: 29. Ita Jonas, ubi voto navitarum Tharsensium, qui ab eo effligim petunt, Quis est Deus tuus? Satisfactum cupit, respondet, Ego יהוה Deum caeli. Jon. 1: 9. Caeterum seclusa isthac ratione, ubi viri Dei Ethnicos alloquuntur nusquam memorantur Deum appellasse יהוה. E multis aliquot exempla in medium protulisse sufficiat. Josephus ad uxorem Potiphar. Et quomodo faciam malum grande hoc, & peccabo contra לאלהים Deum. Non dixit contrâ יהוה. Et ad Eunuchos Pharaonis Nonne לאלהים Dei est solutiones somniorum narrare. Gen. 40:8. Et respondit Joseph Pharaoni dicendo, sine me אלהים Deus respondebit. Gen. 41: 16,32. Et ubi fratres alloquitur, qui nondum noverant Deum in nomine יהוה : האלהים Deum ego timeo. Gen. 42:18. Nec quicquam juvat respondere nomen יהוה nondum innotuisse Josepho, hac enim responsione, proprias ut ajunt, sicuti Hercules furens caedunt sibi tibias. Josephus enim ipsiusque fratres utique Deum noverant nomine יהוה, si illud Dei indigitamentum directe & proprie, Deum significaret, quatenus est ens aeternum, & causa rerum omnium, tritam juxta quam refellimus sententiam. Praeterea integris octo primis Danielis capitibus, Deus memoratur saepe saepius, nusquam tamen audit יהוה. Eccur vero? Nempe sermones Danieli feruntur cum Chaldaeis, quibus Deus non innotuerat in nomine יהוה. Verum nono demum capite, Deus appellatur יהוה. Nempe, quia de numine agitur, ut populo suo, Jerusalem, Prophetis, Sacerdotibus, Regibusque Judae innotuerat. Ut quid autem memorandum istiusmodi discrimen? Utique non erat abstinendum ab appellatione יהוה, quando Deus Ethnicis memorabatur, siquidem augustum illud numinis indigitamentum, Deum proprie, & directe significaret, quatenus est ens aeternum, & causa rerum omnium, ea enim notione, Deus gentibus innotuerat. Quod vero viri Dei sese ab illo nomine abstinuerint, ubi verba commutarunt cum Ethnicis, solidum argumentum est, nomen יהוה proprie, & directe, aliud ab essentia aeterna numinis significare, quod clam Ethnicis omnibus erat.
units.tr: Fifthly. No small strength is added to the preceding argument by a new observation, which is not to be despised. Namely, wherever the men of God address heathen who are ignorant of the living God, they never, nowhere call God Jehovah, unless you set aside those passages where they strive to impart to them the knowledge of their God, in whose name they speak. Thus Moses to Pharaoh: "that you may know that I am Jehovah." Exod. 7:16, 17. "I will spread out my hands to Jehovah, and the thunders will cease," etc., "that you may know that the earth belongs to Jehovah." Exod. 9:29. So too Jonah, when the sailors of Tarshish, who were fleeing from him, asked, "What is your God?" and he wanted to satisfy them, he answered, "I am Jehovah, the God of heaven." Jon. 1:9. Apart from this reason, however, where the men of God address heathen, they are nowhere recorded as calling God Jehovah. It is enough to bring forward a few examples out of many. Joseph to Potiphar's wife: "How then could I do this great evil and sin against Elohim [לאלהים]?" He did not say against Jehovah. And to the eunuchs of Pharaoh: "Do not solutions of dreams belong to Elohim [לאלהים]?" Gen. 40:8. "And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying: without me, Elohim [אלהים] will answer." Gen. 41:16, 32. And when he addresses his brothers, who did not yet know God by the name Jehovah: "I fear Elohim [האלהים]." Gen. 42:18. Nor does it help to reply that the name Jehovah was not yet known to Joseph; for by this answer, as they say, one strikes one's own shins like Hercules in his madness. For Joseph and his brothers surely knew God by the name Jehovah, if that divine designation directly and properly signified God as an eternal being and the cause of all things, which is the commonplace opinion we are refuting. Moreover, through the whole of the first eight chapters of Daniel, God is mentioned again and again, yet never is he called Jehovah. Why is this? Clearly because Daniel's speeches are addressed to the Chaldeans, to whom God was not made known by the name Jehovah. Only in the ninth chapter is God called Jehovah, because there the matter concerns the God who was made known to his people, Jerusalem, the Prophets, the priests and the kings of Judah. But why note such a distinction? Surely the name Jehovah should not have been avoided when God was mentioned to the heathen, if that august designation of the godhead properly and directly signified God as an eternal being and the cause of all things; for in that sense God would have been made known to the nations. That the men of God refrained from that name when they spoke with the heathen is solid evidence that the name Jehovah properly and directly signifies something other than the eternal essence of the godhead, which was hidden from all the heathen.

units.la: Sextò. Si nomen יהוה proprie, & directe Deum significaret, quatenus essentia aeterna est, fons, & causa rerum omnium, utique Deus sub Euangelio, appellandus erat יהוה, vel magis, & potiori ratione, quam in veteri foedere, tribus comprimis de causis. 1°. Quia Deus semper est essentia aeterna, fons, & causa omnis entis. 2°. Quia Deus edixerat hoc esse nomen suum, & memoriale aeternum, seu, in generationem, & generationem, Exod. 3: 15. 3°. Quia sub Euangelio per novarum, & excellentissimarum creaturarum productionem, se modo illustriostriori revelavit, creatorem fontem, & causam cujus libet entis, ubi infinita potentia, Christum hominem produxit ex Virgine praeter & supra naturae finitae vires, & eum e mortuis excitavit, & fideles opus Dei creatos, in Jesu Christo produxit. Eph. 2: 10. Atqui Deus in Euangelio, vel in laudatis omnibus veteris Instrumenti locis ubi Deus יהוה audit, nunquam, nusquam à Christo, Euangelistis, & Apostolis censetur de nomine יהוה: sed constanter, vel Κυριος, vel ὁ Κυριος Dominus, vel, Θεος Deus, nominatur. Hinc in expedito concludere est nomen יהוה, non significare directè, & propriè Deum, ut est essentia aeterna, fons & causa existendi rebus omnibus.
units.tr: Sixthly. If the name Jehovah properly and directly signified God as eternal essence, the fount and cause of all things, then surely under the Gospel God ought to be called Jehovah, and even more and with greater reason than under the Old Covenant, for three chief reasons. First, because God is always the eternal essence, the fount and cause of every being. Second, because God declared this is my name and my eternal memorial, that is, for generation and generation. Exod. 3:15. Third, because under the Gospel he has revealed himself in a more illustrious way, as the creator, fount and cause of every being, through the production of new and most excellent creatures, when by infinite power, beyond and above the powers of finite nature, he produced Christ the man from the Virgin, raised him from the dead, and in Jesus Christ produced the faithful, who are created as God's workmanship. Eph. 2:10. But in the Gospel, and in all the passages of the Old Testament cited where God is called Jehovah, he is never, nowhere, called Jehovah by Christ, the Evangelists or the Apostles; rather he is constantly named either Kyrios [Κυριος], or ho Kyrios [ὁ Κυριος], Lord, or Theos [Θεος], God. Hence it is easy to conclude that the name Jehovah does not directly and properly signify God as the eternal essence, the fount and cause of existence for all things.

units.la: Respondere novum Instrumentum Graecè scriptum fuisse, & nomen aliquod Graecum, nempe Κυριον Dominum, vel Θεον Deum, vice nominis Hebraei יהוה, fuisse substituendum. Hoc inquam respondere nihili plane erit: nam in Graeco textu multa vocabula Hebraea, Syra, & Syro-Chaldaica Spiritus Sancti amanuenses retinuerunt, ut Amen, Maranata, Golgotha, Akeldama, Cepha, Hosanna, Alleluia, & quae non? Quod igitur Graecè scripserint, nihil utique causae fuit, quominus retinuerint Hebraicum יהוה nomen Dei proprium & memoriale aeternum in omnem generationem. Fullerus Miscellaneorum sacrorum lib. 2: c. 6. respondet, Hebraeum vocabulum יהוה non fuisse scriptum Graecè, quia Graeca lingua non patitur incorrupte atque integrè scribi aut proferri. Graecis enim non solum extra modum absona: sed etiam ineffabilis omnino est aspiratio ejusmodi in medio. Unde ἀνεκφώνητον illud veteres cognominarunt. Et lib. 4. c. 13. Profectò, inquit, ratio illa, quare primò ἀνεκφώνητον fit vocatum, quam attulimus, ab inextricabili pronunciationis Graecanicae difficultate sumptam, firma est & perspicua, & in promptu cuilibet, qui vel levissimum periculum facere dignetur. Ecquanam ratione augustissimum illud nomen Graece, b. e. Graecorum more enuntiari exactè queat? Ut omnes nervos contenderis, & quam accuratissimè eloqui coneris, certè ιεωουα vel saltem ιεωνα, ιεοῦα, omninò dicas oportet. At quanta hic prolationis inconcinnitas? Quantus hiatus? Quam nihil prorsus consonum? Censen volubiles Graecorum linguas ex hisce salebris sese expedire, aut teretes eorum aures, tam confusi & inconditi soni asperitatem perpeti posse? Verum enim vero Doctissimi Fulleri isthaec ratio plane futilis est, magno conatu ut nihil promoveat, quippe falso nititur fundamento, nomen scilicet, augustissimum יהוה legendum esse & pronuntiandum Jehova, quod & supra rationibus falsis utis arguimus, est enim novitia Marsilii Ficini & Galatini Monachi, chi, qui primi omnium lectionem illam in orbem terrarum invexere, quamque retinuere viri docti, vel invito ipso Galatino. Et Ethnici doctissimi Græci, quibus nomen augustissimum innotuerat, Diodorus Siculus, Apollo Clarius, aliique scripserunt, & omninò pronuntiarunt Ἰαώ. Et Porphyrius apud Eusebium lib. 1. Præparat. Euange. c. 5. asserit Judæorum Deum vocari Ἰευώ. Sed & Doctores antiqui Ecclesiæ id indigitamenti ex Samaritanis scripserunt, & pronuntiarunt Ἰαβὲ: vel ex propria sententia Ἰαὼ, vel Ἰαὲ; ut Clemens Alexandrinus, vel Αδωναὶ, ut Origenes in hexaplis. Usque adeo ut in antiquis editionibus Doctorum Ecclesiæ Græcorum, vel Latinorum, quæ lucem ante Galatinum viderunt, nusquam legas Jehova, quod & supra observavimus, ex veteri editione Hieronymi in Ps. 8. ubi legitur Jaho.
units.tr: It may be answered that the New Testament was written in Greek, and that some Greek name, namely Κύριος (Lord) or Θεός (God), was substituted for the Hebrew name יהוה. I say plainly that this answer will be worth nothing. In the Greek text the Holy Spirit's scribes kept many Hebrew, Syriac and Syro-Chaldaic words, such as Amen, Maranatha, Golgotha, Akeldama, Cephas, Hosanna, Alleluia, and many more. So the fact that they wrote in Greek was no reason at all why they should not have kept the Hebrew name יהוה, God's proper name and eternal memorial for all generations. Fuller, in the Miscellanea sacra, book 2, chapter 6, replies that the Hebrew word יהוה was not written in Greek, because the Greek language does not allow it to be written or pronounced correctly and in full. For to the Greeks such a sound is not only extremely harsh, but the aspiration in the middle of it is entirely unpronounceable. Hence the ancients called it ἀνεκφώνητον [unutterable]. And in book 4, chapter 13: Surely, he says, that reason why it was first called ἀνεκφώνητον, which we have given, taken from the inextricable difficulty of Greek pronunciation, is firm and clear, and obvious to anyone who will deign to make even the slightest trial. In what way could that most august name be pronounced exactly in Greek, that is, in the manner of the Greeks? However hard you strain every nerve and try to utter it as accurately as possible, you must certainly say ιεωουα, or at least ιεωνα, ιεοῦα. But what an awkwardness of pronunciation there is here! What a gap! How utterly discordant! Do you think the nimble tongues of the Greeks can extricate themselves from such rough places, or that their polished ears can bear the roughness of such a confused and disordered sound? But in truth this reasoning of the most learned Fuller is quite futile. It labours greatly to prove nothing, because it rests on a false foundation, namely that the most august name יהוה must be read and pronounced Jehovah. We have argued against this, using false reasons above, for it is a novelty of Marsilio Ficino and of the monk Galatinus, who first brought that reading into the world, and which learned men have kept, even against Galatinus' own wishes. And the most learned Greek pagans, to whom the august name had become known, Diodorus Siculus, Apollo of Claros and others, wrote and pronounced it entirely as Ἰαώ [Iaō]. Porphyry, in Eusebius, Praeparatio evangelica book 1, chapter 5, asserts that the God of the Jews is called Ἰευώ [Ieuō]. But the ancient teachers of the Church also wrote, from the Samaritans, that this designation was pronounced Ἰαβέ [Iabe], or in their own judgement Ἰαώ or Ἰαέ, as Clement of Alexandria did, or Αδωναί [Adōnai], as Origen did in the Hexapla. So much so that in the old editions of the Greek or Latin teachers of the Church, which saw the light before Galatinus, you will nowhere read Jehovah, as we also observed above, from the old edition of Jerome on Psalm 8, where it reads Jaho.

units.la: Respondent alii, noluisse Christum & Apostolos Judæis esse scandalo, restituendo pristino suo usui augustissimum Dei nomen, quod tunc legi & pronuntiari desierat: sed ejus loco uti maluisse nomine Κύριος, vel Θεὸς, quo conscessus Septuaginta-viralis nomen mm constanter reddiderant. Quæ hîc reponamus multa occurrunt. 1°. Sive superstitiosa veneratione Judæi, sive metu, ne tremendum Dei nomen crebra vulgi pronuntiatione vilesceret, vel à gentibus idololatris profanaretur, & in idola transferretur, sive alia de causa, ausu tamen nefario augustum nomen Deo proprium de medio sustulerant, (si obtineat sententia quam refellimus) utique Christus & Apostoli nomen augustissimum proprio suo usui, vel jure postliminii restituissent, nec sivissent Judæos impunè tulisse, quod Deo sapientiores videri vellent. 1°. Quia ut Christus & Apostoli in rebus levissimis, seu indifferentibus genio Judæorum se attemperarunt, in rebus summi momenti nihil Judæorum scandalum veriti, eorum traditiones traduxere. Matth. 5: 20. &c. Et 15: 7. 14. Qui obsecro inultam sivisset Christus illatam Dei mandato, de nomine suo memoriali æterno pronuntiando, injuriam, qui inultam non tulit illatam justitiæ & judicio legis? Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi, hypocritæ, qui decimatis mentam, & anetum, & cuminum, & omittitis, quæ graviora sunt legis, judicium, & misericordiam, & fidem. Mat. 23: 23. 2°. Quia Christus ubi agitur de observatione præceptorum secundæ tabulæ, generosè Pharisæis exprobrat, Vestris traditionibus præcepta Dei annihilastis. Mat. 15: 3. Quam potiori jure Christus & Apostoli Judæis exprobrassent, ausu eos nefario annihilasse præceptum, quod propriè, & per se, ad primam tabulam, & cultum Dei spespectabat? Nempe edixerat Numen ut sacerdotes populo benedicerent, non utique semel, sed vicibus ternis, in nomine suo יהוה, & ita nomen suum ponerent super populo suo. Num. 6: 23. &c. Atqui Sacerdotes tempore Christi praeceptum illud violaverant, & annihilaverant, illi enim non in nomine יהוה: sed in nomine אֲדֹנָי populo benedicebant. Maimon. More Nevochim. lib. 1 cap. 62. Hinc tam in proclivi quam imber dum pluit, concluditur Christum & Apostolos, non sese abstinuisse abs pronuntiatione nominis יהוה, ne scandalo forent Judaeis: Sed potius alto suo silentio super illo nomine, & constanti pronuntiatione אֲדֹנָי ipsius vicarii, aperte innuerunt Deum sub Euangelic, non esse appellandum יהוה. Nam contra Christus & Apostoli sapientissimi simulac pientissimi, nunquam attentassent amoliri pronuntiationem nominis יהוה, siquidem vivissent Deum id sibi non e a proprium vendicasse ad significandum proprie essentiam suam aeternam, ut causa est omnium. Sicut enim Deus semper est essentia aeterna, & fons existendi rebus omnibus, semper esset, juréque merito appellandus יהוה.
units.tr: Others reply that Christ and the Apostles did not want to give offence to the Jews by restoring to its former use the most august name of God, which had then ceased to be read and pronounced, but preferred to use in its place the name Κύριος or Θεός, which the Seventy had consistently rendered for the name יהוה. Many objections occur to us here. First, whether the Jews, from superstitious reverence, or from fear that the awesome name of God would become cheap through frequent pronunciation by the common people, or would be profaned by idolatrous nations and transferred to idols, or for some other reason, boldly removed the august name, proper to God, from use, (if the opinion we are refuting holds), then Christ and the Apostles would certainly have restored the august name to its proper use, or to its right of return, and would not have allowed the Jews to get away unpunished for wanting to seem wiser than God. Second, because Christ, when he was dealing with the observance of the precepts of the second table, did not hesitate to rebuke the Pharisees, saying, You have annulled the precepts of God by your traditions. Matt. 15: 3. With how much stronger right would Christ and the Apostles have rebuked the Jews for boldly annulling a precept that pertained directly and in itself to the first table and the worship of God? Indeed the Deity had ordained that the priests should bless the people, not once only, but three times, in his name יהוה, and so they should put his name upon his people. Num. 6: 23 ff. Yet the priests of Christ's time had violated and annulled that precept, for they did not bless the people in the name יהוה but in the name אֲדֹנָי. Maimonides, Guide of the Perplexed, book 1, chapter 62. Hence it follows as readily as rain falls when it is raining that Christ and the Apostles did not abstain from pronouncing the name יהוה lest they give offence to the Jews. Rather, by their deep silence about that name and their constant pronunciation of אֲדֹנָי, its substitute, they clearly indicated that God is not to be called יהוה under the Gospel. For on the contrary, Christ and the Apostles, being most wise and most pious, would never have attempted to remove the pronunciation of the name יהוה, if they had held that God had claimed it for himself as his proper name, to signify directly his eternal essence, as the cause of all things. For just as God is always the eternal essence and the source of existence for all things, he would always be, and would rightly be called, יהוה.

units.la: Septimo: Si nomen proprium יהוה, proprie & directe significaret Deum ut est essentia aeterna, & creator rerum omnium, utique Spiritus Sanctus Deum appellasset יהוה ubicumque Deum exhibet considerandum, sub notione entis aeterni & immutabilis, quod & aliquando usu venit ut Ps. 102: 13. Malach. 3: 6. Nec post nomen יהוה ejus aeternitatem & creationem attexere opus esset, quia utrumque proprie, per se, & directe supponitur significari nomine proprio יהוה. Atqui secus se rem habere constat pluribus ex Scripturae locis, ut Deut. 32: 27. ubi Moses dicit. Nubes sunt habitaculum אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם Dei qui est ante omnia, h. e. Dei aeterni. Illic enim dicendum erat nubes sunt habitaculum יהוה. Siquidem Deus nomen Tetragrammatum sibi vendicasset proprium ad significandum directe essentiam suam aeternam. Est & alter locus illustris Jes. 57: 15. Sic dixit excelsus & sublimis habitans, seu aeternum permanens, cujus nomen sanctum est. Utique hic loci dicendum erat cujus nomen est יהוה, si nomen Tetragrammatum ex Dei consilio proprie & per se essentiam Dei aeternam significaret. Nec aeternitas & creatio terrae attexenda esset nomini יהוה Dei aeternitatem per se sonanti, & creationem rerum omnium. Attexitur tamen nomini יהוה aeternitas & creatio terrae. Nonne nosti, nonne audivisti אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם יְהוָה בּוֹרֵא Deus seculi, seu aeternus יהוה, creans extremitates terrae, non fatigabitur. Utique quòd Propheta vehementer petit num Jacob audiverit יהוה esse Deum aeternum, & creatorem terra? Quaque interrogatione vehementi significat Jacobum id saepissime audivisse, argumento est nomen יהוה non significare proprie, & vi sua Deum esse ens aeternum & creatorem rerum omnium. Quod enim nomen ipsum per se & proprie significat, non est ab aliis fando audiendum, & discendum.
units.tr: Seventh: If the proper name יהוה signified God properly and directly as the eternal essence and creator of all things, then the Holy Spirit would certainly have called God יהוה wherever God is set forth for consideration under the notion of the eternal and unchangeable being. This sometimes happens in use, as in Psalm 102: 13 and Malachi 3: 6. Nor would it be necessary to add his eternity and creation after the name יהוה, since both are supposed to be properly, in themselves and directly signified by the proper name יהוה. But it is clear that the matter stands otherwise in several passages of Scripture, such as Deut. 32: 27, where Moses says, The clouds are the dwelling of the God who is before all things אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם, that is, of the eternal God. For there he ought to have said, the clouds are the dwelling of יהוה, if God had claimed the Tetragrammaton as his proper name to signify directly his eternal essence. There is also another famous place, Isaiah 57: 15: Thus says the high and lofty one who dwells, or who remains eternal, whose name is holy. Surely here it ought to say whose name is יהוה, if the name Tetragrammaton, by God's counsel, properly and in itself signified the eternal essence of God. Nor would eternity and the creation of the earth have to be added to the name יהוה, if it sounded of itself God's eternity and the creation of all things. Yet eternity and the creation of the earth are added to the name יהוה. Have you not known, have you not heard that אֱלֹהֵי עוֹלָם יְהוָה בּוֹרֵא, the God of eternity, that is, the eternal יהוה, who creates the ends of the earth, will not grow weary? Surely the prophet's vehement question, whether Jacob had heard that יהוה is the eternal God and creator of the earth, and the emphatic form of the question, signify that Jacob had very often heard this. This is proof that the name יהוה does not signify properly and by its own power that God is the eternal being and creator of all things. For what a name signifies in itself and properly is not something to be heard from others and learned by report.

units.la: Octavò. Deus ut est essentia aeterna, & creator rerum omnium, non est causa vitae aeternae & beatae peccatoribus. Ratio est 1°. Quia peccatum peccatores à Deo separat, & maledictionem ac mortem à creatore, & legislatore justo in caput eorum arcessit. Jef. 59: 2. Deuteron. 27:26. 2°. Quia si Deus ut est ens aeternum & creator, causa esset vitae aeternae peccatoribus, utique peccatores omnes vitam aeternam beatam viverent, nempe Deus, nec quicquam obstante peccato, semper & ubique est essentia aeterna, & creator, vel in habitudine ad quosuis peccatores. Atqui Deus quatenus est יהוה causa est vitae aeternum beatae peccatoribus. Ipse יהוה est vita tua, & longitudo dierum tuorum ad habitandum super terra, quam juravit יהוה patribus tuis Abraha-mo, Isaaco & Jacobo se daturum illis. Deut. 30: 19,20, Me יהוה reliquerunt scaturiginem aquarum viventium, ad excidendum sibi cisternas fractas, quae aquam non continent. Jerem. 2: 13. Et 17: 13. Hinc Paulus Christum vocat vitam nostram. Colos. 3: 4. Sicut Prophetae vocarunt יהוה vitam Israelis. Et Psaltes ex eo quod יהוה aeternum permaneat, concludit aeternam durationem posteritatis servorum ipsius. Ps. 102: 13, 29. Unde in promptu concluditur יהוה non significare proprie & directe Deum, quatenus est ens aeternum, creator, & causa rerum omnium.
units.tr: Eighthly. God, as he is the eternal essence and creator of all things, is not the cause of eternal and blessed life to sinners. The reason is: (1) because sin separates sinners from God, and brings curse and death upon them from the creator and just lawgiver. Isa. 59:2; Deut. 27:26. (2) Because if God as the eternal being and creator were the cause of eternal life for sinners, then surely all sinners would live an eternal and blessed life, since God, nothing standing in the way of sin, is always and everywhere the eternal essence and creator, or in relation to any sinners whatever. But God as יהוה is in fact the cause of eternal and blessed life for sinners. "He יהוה is your life, and the length of your days, to dwell upon the land which יהוה swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob that he would give them." Deut. 30:19-20. "They have forsaken me, יהוה, the fountain of living waters, to hew out for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water." Jer. 2:13; and 17:13. Hence Paul calls Christ "our life." Col. 3:4. Just as the prophets called יהוה "the life of Israel." And the Psalmist, because יהוה remains eternal, concludes the eternal duration of the posterity of his servants. Ps. 102:13, 29. Hence it is readily concluded that יהוה does not properly and directly signify God as he is the eternal being, creator, and cause of all things.

units.la: Nonò. Deus Israelitas sic alloquitur. Vos filii estis יהוה Dei vestri, non vos incidetis, neque ponetis calvitium inter oculos vestros, propter mortuum. Deut. 14: 1. Vetat igitur Numen ne populus suus Ethnicorum morem imitetur, qui resurrectionis ignari saeviebant in se ipsos, ob amissos desideratos, & unicè caros amicos. Mosi concinit Paulus. Nolim autem vos in ignorantia versari fratres, quod ad eos attinet, qui obdormierunt, ut ne tristitia afficiamini, sicut caeteri, qui spem non habent. 1 Thes. 4: 13. Eccur verò? Respondet Paulus verf. 16. Nam ipse Dominus cum hortationis clamore, & voce Archangeli, & cum tuba Dei descendet è coelo, & qui mortui fuerint in Christo resurgent primum. Iterum Mosi concinit, qui Israelitas deterret à luctu desperabundo Ethnicorum super mortuis.
units.tr: Ninthly. God addresses the Israelites thus: "You are the children of יהוה your God; you shall not cut yourselves, nor make baldness between your eyes for the dead." Deut. 14:1. The Deity therefore forbids his people to imitate the custom of the Gentiles, who, ignorant of the resurrection, raged against themselves over lost, longed-for and dearly loved friends. Paul agrees with Moses: "I would not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning those who have fallen asleep, that you sorrow not, as the rest who have no hope." 1 Thess. 4:13. Why so? Paul answers in verse 16: "For the Lord himself with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God, shall descend from heaven, and the dead in Christ shall rise first." Again he agrees with Moses, who restrains the Israelites from the despairing grief of the Gentiles over the dead.

units.la: hac una ratione, nempè quia sunt filii יהוה. Ut hinc perliquidum fiat nomen יהוה continere rationem & causam resurrectionis, vitæque futuræ, & immortalis. Nempe filii יהוה non debent in desperationem ruere: Sed in spem certam adduci futuræ resurrectionis, & vitæ æternæ, quia sunt filii יהוה. Unde nobis emergit hoc argumentum. Si nomen יהוה quatenus supponitur directè & proprie significare Deum, ut est ens æternum, & creator hominum, rerumque omnium, rationem & causam haberet futuræ resurrectionis, vitæque æternæ post mortem. Omnes homines vel nequissimi, & Deo inimicissimi, forent filii יהוה. Nam Deus ut est ens entium & creator fecit ex uno sanguine totam gentem hominum, jure ut possint cum Arato omnes gloriari &ν αὐτῷ γὰρ ἐσμεν: Nam hujus progenies etiam sumus. Act. 17: 26, 28. Et eo nomine in morte solari sese spe gloriosæ resurrectionis, vitæque æternæ. Atqui falsum est omnes homines esse filios יהוה, quatenus eo nomine gloriosò vitam æternam est collaturus: hæc enim est prærogativa fidelium, Deo per fidem fœderatorum, Abrahami, Isaaci, & Jacobi, quorum יהוה Deus est. Exod. 3: 6. Mat. 22: 32. Ergò Deus non sibi proprium vindicaverat nomen יהוה ut proprie & directè significaret se esse ens æternum, creatorem, & causam existendi rebus omnibus.
units.tr: For this one reason alone, namely because they are the sons of יהוה. So that it may become quite clear that the name יהוה contains the reason and cause of the resurrection, and of future and immortal life. Namely, the sons of יהוה ought not to fall into despair, but be brought to a certain hope of future resurrection and eternal life, because they are the sons of יהוה. From this there arises for us the following argument. If the name יהוה, supposing it directly and properly signified God as the eternal being and creator of men and of all things, contained the reason and cause of future resurrection and eternal life after death, then all men, even the most wicked and most hostile to God, would be sons of יהוה. For God, as the being of beings and creator, "made from one blood the whole race of men," so that all could rightly boast with Aratus, "For we are also his offspring" (ἐκ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν). Acts 17:26, 28. And by that name they could console themselves in death with the hope of glorious resurrection and eternal life. But it is false that all men are sons of יהוה, in the sense that by that glorious name he will bestow eternal life; for this is the prerogative of believers, of those bound to God by covenant through faith, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, whose God יהוה is. Exod. 3:6; Matt. 22:32. Therefore God did not claim for himself the name יהוה so that it would properly and directly signify that he is the eternal being, creator, and cause of the existence of all things.

units.la: Decimò. Deus ita loquitur. Ego sum יהוה, hoc est nomen meum, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo, & laudem meam sculptilibus. Jes. 42: 8. Hinc liquidò paret Deum sibi vindicasse proprium nomen יהוה se ab idolis ut separaret, & in illo nomine gloriam suam & laudem ita constituisse ut non daret nomen suum יהוה sculptilibus, quia sua laus & gloria est. Unde nobis emergit id argumenti. Si nomen Tetragrammatum sibi Deus fecisset proprium ut se directè & proprie significaret, quatenus est ens æternum, & fons existendi rebus omnibus, nulla potest legitima perhiberi ratio, cur Deus dixerit se nomen suum יהוה non daturum sculptilibus. Nam si per nomen quadriliterum Deum intelligas quatenus est ens æternum, & creator rerum omnium, nihil quicquam necesse erat Deum sanctè asserere se non daturum essentiam suam æternam, & gloriam creationis idolis. Nempe, impossibile est, plura esse entia æterna, infinita, plures Deos, pluresve creatores, sed enim vero si intelligas Deum non permissurum ut idola usurpent gloriam entis æterni, & fontis essendi rebus omnibus, nec hoc jure dici potest, quia Deus sivit ut Ethnicorum Dii haberentur pro entibus æternis, & causis rerum omnium, crediderunt enim ApolApollinem, & Jovem Deum esse æternum, immutabilem, patremque Deorum, & hominum, ut supra ratione quarta demonstravimus.
units.tr: Tenthly. God speaks thus: "I am יהוה; this is my name, and I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to graven images." Isa. 42:8. From this it clearly appears that God claimed for himself the proper name יהוה, in order to separate himself from idols, and so established his glory and praise in that name that he would not give his name יהוה to graven images, because it is his praise and glory. Hence there arises for us this argument. If God had made the four-letter name his own proper name, so that it signified him directly and properly as the eternal being and fountain of existence for all things, no legitimate reason could be offered why God said that he would not give his name יהוה to graven images. For if by the four-letter name you understand God as the eternal being and creator of all things, there was no need at all for God to solemnly declare that he would not give his eternal essence and the glory of creation to idols. Indeed, it is impossible that there should be several eternal, infinite beings, several gods or several creators. But if you understand it to mean that God would not permit idols to usurp the glory of the eternal being and fountain of existence for all things, this too cannot rightly be said, since God allowed the gods of the Gentiles to be held as eternal beings and causes of all things. For they believed that Apollo and Jupiter were eternal, immutable, and the father of gods and men, as we demonstrated above in the fourth reason.

units.la: Undecimò. Nomen quod directè & proprie significat ens æternum, creatorem, & causam rerum omnium, non est nomen gloriosum per excellentiam, & tremendum propter justitiam inexorabilem & vindictam, quia datur nomen magis excellens & gloriosum, nempe אל שדי Deus omnipotens, seu sibi & omnibus creaturis sufficiens. Genes. 17: 1. Et 35: 11. Exod. 6: 3. אל רחום וחנון Deus misericors & gratiosus. Exod. 34: 6. אבינו גאלנו pater noster, redemptor noster. Jes. 63: 16. Illa enim nomina præter æternam Dei existentiam, & creationem rerum omnium, quam consignificant, (quia conceptus omnipotentiæ, omni sufficientiæ, misericordiæ, & gratiæ, supponit necessario conceptum æternæ existentiæ, & creationis,) superaddunt illi significationi conceptum proprium omnipotentiæ, sufficientissimæ abundantiæ, misericordiæ, & gratiæ. Unde efflorescit gloria illustrior, illa quæ fulget in nomine, quod ens æternum, & creatorem duntaxat proprie significat. Præterea, nomen quod Deum directè duntaxat significat, quatenus est Ens æternum & creator omnium, utique non est tremendum ob justitiam inexorabilem & vindictam in idololatras, quia ens æternum & creator est ens optimum, ut ex inexhausta sua bonitate, omnes creaturas produxerit & conservet, nec judex est inexorabilis; & ad perdendum creaturas suas ex justitia sua vindicatrice pronum, nisi ex accidente peccati. Unde Deus ubi justitiam suam vindicatricem exercet, asserit, agere se opus suum extraordinarium, opus suum insolitum. Jes. 28: 21. Hinc scite Tertullianus, Deus de suo bonus est, de nostro justus. Atqui nomen יהוה est nomen gloriosum per excellentiam, & tremendum ob justitiam, & vindictam: Nam Moses ubi maledictiones tremendas, quas Deus in violatores suæ legis intonat, longo catalogo pertexuit, sic demum subsumit. Si non observaveritis ad faciendum omnia verba legis ipsius, scripta in libro isto ad timendum illud nomen gloriosum, & tremendum istud יהוה Deum tuum; miras faciet percussiones tuas, & percussiones seminis tui, percussiones magnas & stabiles, & infirmitates malas & stabiles. Deut. 28: 58, 59. Hinc evidentissime colligitur nomen יהוה non significare directè & proprie Deum quatenus est ens æternum, & creator rerum omnium.
units.tr: Eleventhly. A name which directly and properly signifies the eternal being, creator, and cause of all things is not a name glorious above all, and terrible on account of inexorable justice and vengeance, since there is given a more excellent and glorious name, namely אל שדי, "God Almighty," or "sufficient for himself and for all creatures." Gen. 17:1; 35:11; Exod. 6:3. אל רחום וחנון, "God merciful and gracious." Exod. 34:6. אבינו גאלנו, "our Father, our Redeemer." Isa. 63:16. For those names, besides the eternal existence of God and the creation of all things, which they consignify (since the concept of omnipotence, of all-sufficiency, of mercy and grace necessarily presupposes the concept of eternal existence and creation), add to that signification the proper concept of omnipotence, of most sufficient abundance, of mercy and grace. Hence there shines forth a more illustrious glory, that which shines in a name which properly signifies only the eternal being and creator. Moreover, a name which signifies God directly only as the eternal being and creator of all things is certainly not terrible on account of inexorable justice and vengeance against idolaters, since the eternal being and creator is the best of beings, who out of his inexhaustible goodness has produced and preserves all creatures, and is not an inexorable judge, nor prone to destroy his creatures by his avenging justice, except on account of sin as an accident. Hence when God exercises his avenging justice, he declares that he performs "his work, his strange work," Isa. 28:21. Hence Tertullian rightly said, "God is good in his own nature, just by reason of ours." Yet the name יהוה is a name glorious above all, and terrible on account of justice and vengeance. For Moses, when he had woven into a long catalogue the terrible curses which God thunders against the violators of his law, finally adds: "If you do not observe to do all the words of this law written in this book, to fear that glorious and terrible name, יהוה your God; then יהוה will make your plagues wonderful, and the plagues of your seed, great and lasting plagues, and evil and lasting sicknesses." Deut. 28:58-59. Hence it is most evidently gathered that the name יהוה does not directly and properly signify God as the eternal being and creator of all things.

units.la: Duodecimò. Sed & robur non contemnendum illi rationi accedit, ex hac singulari consideratione. Nempe etsi Deus multis se nominibus, bus in scriptura induerit, & singulari ratione nominibus illis, quae ejus æternitatem directè & per sese significeant, ut Elohe Kedem, Elohe Holam, Deus æternus, vel eum creatorem, ut Bore. Illa tamen nomina nunquam nusquam השם הנכבד והנורא nomen gloriosum & tremendum audiunt totâ Scriptura, nec augustissimum nomen, nec ineffabile, nec nomen separatum unquam à Rabbinis, vel Ecclesiæ Doctoribus appellantur. Ut quid verò? Quando id ipsum significant, quod nomen יהוה, quod Deum æternum, & conditorem rerum omnium, significat si vera sit, quam refellimus sententiam. Causam dicant discriminis etiam atque etiam rogamus? Eane est, quia Deus nomen יהוה sibi proprium fecerit? Anne etiam sibi proprium nomen fecit, quod sit Deus æternus, quem ante nullus alius Deus fuerit, quodque sit rerum omnium creator? Primus & ultimus, principium, & finis omnis creaturæ? Unde legitima consequutione colligitur nomen illud, יהוה gloriosum, tremendum, magnum, nomen καὶ' ἐξοχὴν, Deum sibi non fecisse proprium, ut significaret proprie & directè, se esse Deum æternum, & causam rerum omnium.
units.tr: Twelfthly. A further argument, and not a weak one, arises from the following particular consideration. Although God has clothed himself in many names in Scripture, and some of those names, such as Elohe Kedem, Elohe Holam, the eternal God, directly and in themselves signify his eternity, and others signify him as Creator, such as Bore, yet those names are never called, anywhere in the whole of Scripture, the glorious and tremendous name [השם הנכבד והנורא], nor are they ever called by the Rabbis or the Doctors of the Church the most august name, the ineffable name, or the separated name. But why not, since they signify the very thing that the name יהוה signifies, namely the eternal God and creator of all things, if the opinion we are refuting were true? Let them state the reason for this difference, we ask again and again. Is it because God made יהוה his own proper name? Did he not also make his own proper name the eternal God, whom no other god existed before, and the creator of all things, the first and the last, the beginning and the end of every creature? From which it follows by sound inference that the name יהוה, glorious, tremendous, great, the name pre-eminently [καὶ' ἐξοχήν], was not made God's own proper name so that it would signify, properly and directly, that he is the eternal God and the cause of all things.

units.la: Decimotertio. Deus nomen יהוה sibi proprium fecit, sese ut distingueret à falsis omnibus Diis Ægyptii cognoscent me esse יהוה in medio terra. Exod. 7: 5. & 8: 22. יהוה Deus noster est solus יהוה. Deut. 6: 4. Sed nunc יהוה Deus noster libera nos à manu ipsius, ut omnia terra regna sciant, te unum esse יהוה. Jesa. 37: 20. Si juraverint per nomen meum יהוה est vivens, sicut docuerunt populum meum jurare per Baalim. Jerem. 12: 16. Et dicent quia reliquerunt יהוה Deum suum, & adorarunt Deos alios, iisque servierunt. Jerem. 22: 9. Joël. 2: 27. Et ita passim. Hinc legitima consecutione colligitur, Deum nomen יהוה non sibi fecisse proprium, eo directè & proprie ut significaret se esse ens æternum, & creatorem rerum omnium. Nam etsi revera unus est ens æternum, & creator seclusis omnibus Diis, suo tamen illo nomine יהוה à falsis Diis se non separasset, quia gentes omnes credidere Deum suum esse ens æternum, & fontem existendi rebus omnibus, ut supra demonstravimus ratione quarta. Nec ulla erat controversia Ethnicos inter & Israelitas num Deus sit ens æternum, & causa rerum omnium, in eo enim omnes amicè consentiebant: Sed lis erat perpetua Israelitas inter & gentes, quisnam esset jure merito ens illud æternum, & fons essendi, num v. g. Baal? Num יהוה? Quando igitur ex locis Scripturæ laudatis nimis compertum est Deum Israelis, sibi nomen יהוה indidisse proprium, se à falsis gentium Diis ut discerdiscerneret & separaret. Unde fit ut Deus nomen יהוה, vocet nomen sanctitatis sua, hoc est, quo separatur per excellentiam suam comprimis à falsis Diis. Levit. 20: 3. & 22: 31: 32. Hinc evidentissime concluditur suo illo separationis nomine, Deum non significasse directè & proprie se esse ens aeternum, & causam rerum omnium. Ethnicis enim promptum fuisset respondere Israelitis. Ut quid Deum vestrum יהוה appellitare amatis, eum ut separetis, & secernatis à Deo nostro? Etiam Deus noster est יהוה. Eum enim credimus & adoramus ens aeternum & causam rerum omnium: Nam eum ubi salutamus ei dicimus. Ei. Tu es, nos vero non sumus essentia participes, & versamur in medio ortus & interitus. Sed & eum ubi invocamus his verbis compellare solemus. Σὺ πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε Θεῶν τε. Jupiter pater hominum atque Deorum.
units.tr: Thirteenthly. God made the name יהוה his own proper name so that he might distinguish himself from all false gods: The Egyptians shall know that I am יהוה in the midst of the land. Exod. 7:5; 8:22. יהוה our God is one יהוה. Deut. 6:4. Now therefore, יהוה our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are יהוה. Isa. 37:20. If they swear by my name, "As יהוה lives," as they taught my people to swear by Baal. Jer. 12:16. And they shall say, because they forsook יהוה their God and worshipped other gods and served them. Jer. 22:9; Joel 2:27; and so throughout. From this it follows by sound inference that God did not make the name יהוה his own proper name in such a way as to signify directly and properly that he is the eternal being and the creator of all things. For although he is in truth the one eternal being and creator, apart from all gods, yet he would not have separated himself from the false gods by that name יהוה, because all the nations believed that their god was the eternal being and the fountain of existence for all things, as we demonstrated above by the fourth reason. Nor was there any controversy between the Gentiles and the Israelites over whether God is the eternal being and the cause of all things, for in this all agreed amicably. The dispute was rather perpetual between the Israelites and the nations as to who was rightly and justly that eternal being and fountain of existence: was it, for instance, Baal? Or יהוה? Therefore, from the passages of Scripture cited, it is abundantly clear that the God of Israel gave himself the proper name יהוה so that he might distinguish and separate himself from the false gods of the nations. Hence God calls it the name of his holiness, that is, the name by which he is set apart, by his pre-eminent excellence, from false gods. Lev. 20:3; 22:31, 32. Hence it is most evident that by that name of separation God did not signify directly and properly that he is the eternal being and the cause of all things. For the Gentiles would readily have answered the Israelites: Why do you love to call your God יהוה, so that you set him apart and separate him from our God? Our God is also יהוה. For we believe and worship him as the eternal being and the cause of all things; when we greet him we say to him: You are, but we are not participants in essence, and we dwell in the midst of rising and perishing. But when we invoke him too, we are accustomed to address him in these words: Σὺ πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε Θεῶν τε [You are father of men and of gods]. Jupiter, father of men and of gods.

units.la: Decimoquartò.
units.tr: Fourteenthly.

units.la: Nomen quod proprie & directè Deum significat quatenus est ens aeternum & creator rerum omnium. Non significat directè & proprie Deum, quatenus vindictam, & tremendam justitiam exercet in falsos Deos abolendos, & in idololatras plectendos: Sed tantum ex consequenti, quia ens aeternum & creator etiam est legislator summusque vindex legum suarum, ut creaturam sontem & rebellem non ferat impunem. Atqui nomen יהוה, ex instituto & consilio numinis proprie & directè Deum significat quatenus vindictam se exerciturum recipit in falsos Deos gentium abolendos, & Idololatras plectendos, quod evidentissime paret, quia ubi ubi Deus recipit se exerciturum justa sua judicia in Deos alienos exterminandos, vel in idololatras, illicò passim attexit, & cognoscent, vel vos cognoscetis me esse יהוה, hoc est, quam verissime ac meritissime id nomen proprium mihi fecerim. Exod. 6: 6, 7. & 7: 4, 5. & 12: 12. & 14: 4. Jef. 19: 1. Jerem. 42: 10, 11, 12. Ezech. 5: 11, 13. & 6: 3, 7. & 11: 10. & 12: 15, 20. & 14: 8. & 15: 7. & 25: 17. & 28: 23. & 33: 29. & 39: 6, 7. Ergo nomen יהוה proprie & directè significat Deum, quatenus suo illo nomine recipiebat se exterminaturum falsos Deos, & tremendum in modum, in gentes Idololatras animadversurum. Secus enim nec gentes, nec Israelitæ per falsorum Deorum exterminationem, & severam in idololatras ultionem, haut cognovissent proprie, & directè, Deum Israelis esse יהוה.
units.tr: The name which signifies God properly and directly insofar as he is the eternal being and creator of all things does not signify God directly and properly insofar as he exercises vengeance and terrible justice in destroying false gods and punishing idolaters; rather, it signifies this only by consequence, because the eternal being and creator is also the lawgiver and supreme avenger of his laws, so that he does not allow a sinful and rebellious creature to go unpunished. But the name יהוה, by the institution and counsel of the deity, signifies God properly and directly insofar as he receives that he will exercise vengeance against the false gods of the nations to destroy them and punish idolaters. This is most clearly evident, because wherever God declares that he will exercise his just judgments to exterminate the strange gods or the idolaters, he immediately adds everywhere: And they shall know, or you shall know, that I am יהוה; that is, how truly and deservedly I have made that name my own. Exod. 6:6, 7; 7:4, 5; 12:12; 14:4. Isa. 19:1. Jer. 42:10, 11, 12. Ezek. 5:11, 13; 6:3, 7; 11:10; 12:15, 20; 14:8; 15:7; 25:17; 28:23; 33:29; 39:6, 7. Therefore the name יהוה properly and directly signifies God insofar as by that name he declared that he would destroy the false gods and would take vengeance upon the idolatrous nations in a terrible manner. For otherwise neither the nations nor the Israelites would have properly and directly come to know that the God of Israel is יהוה through the extermination of false gods and the severe vengeance upon idolaters.

units.la: Decimoquintò.
units.tr: Fifteenthly.

units.la: Si nomen יהוה proprie & directè significaret Deum quatenus est ens aeternum, & causa rerum omnium, qui cognosce-ret ret יהוה, non cognosceret יהוה sanctificare peccatores, nec Deus quatenus est יהוה, peccatores sanctificaret. Ratio est quia Deus non sanctificat, quatenus est ens æternum, & creator rerum omnium, sub ea enim notione, hominem creavit justum & sanctum, & quia certò certius est Deum in habitudine ad omnes peccatores esse ens æternum, creatorem & conservatorem ipsorum. Utique si Deus quatenus est ens æternum, & creator, peccatores sanctificaret, omnes omninò peccatores sanctitatis suæ faceret participes. Deus igitur peccatores sanctificat, quatenus est eorum redemptor, facta per seipsum peccatorum purgatione, & Spiritus Sancti efficaci collatione. Atqui Deus quatenus est יהוה, peccatores sanctificat. Ut ipsi cognoscant me esse יהוה, qui eos sanctificat. Levit. 20: 8, 24. & 22: 31, 32. Ezech. 20: 12, 20. Ergò Deus nomen יהוה non sibi fecit proprium, ut significaret directè & proprie, se esse ens æternum, & rerum omnium creatorem.
units.tr: If the name יהוה properly and directly signified God as he is an eternal being and the cause of all things, then whoever knew יהוה would not know that יהוה sanctifies sinners, nor would God, as he is יהוה, sanctify sinners. The reason is that God does not sanctify insofar as he is an eternal being and creator of all things; under that notion he created man just and holy, and it is more than certain that God, in his relation to all sinners, is an eternal being, their creator and preserver. Indeed, if God as eternal being and creator sanctified sinners, he would make all sinners partakers of his holiness. Therefore God sanctifies sinners insofar as he is their redeemer, by effecting the purging of sins through himself and by the efficacious bestowal of the Holy Spirit. But God, as יהוה, does sanctify sinners: that they may know that I am יהוה who sanctifies them (Lev. 20:8, 24; 22:31, 32; Ezek. 20:12, 20). Therefore God did not make the name יהוה his own proper name, so as to signify directly and properly that he is the eternal being and creator of all things.

units.la: Decimosexto: Cum Deus nomen יהוה sibi fecerit proprium ubi liberationem Israëlis è servitute Ægyptiaca Mosis ministerio moliretur, ut Mosi populoque persuaderet, se liberaturum Israëlem è servitute dirissima, & vindictam exerciturum in Ægyptios eorumque Deos. Exod. 6: 6. & 12: 12. Utique nomen ad fidem illam faciendam peroportunum sibi fecit proprium. Hæc verò nomen יהוה directè & proprie Deum significare, quatenus est ens æternum, creator, & causa rerum omnium. Nemo non videt id nominis non esse peroportunum & medium proximum & necessarium ad fidem illam ingenerandam. Nam liberatio Israëlis è servitute Ægyptiaca, & vindicta in Ægyptios, eorumque Deos, non fluit immediatè ex eo, quòd Deus sit ens æternum, & creator cœli & terræ, sed per remotas hasce consequentias. 1°. Quod creator summum jus habet in creaturas, & potentiam infinitam. 2°. Quòd velit aliquem populum liberare, sibique adoptare in populum peculiarem, alium vero populum pœnis afficere. 3°. Demum quòd tale sui beneplacitum declaraverit. Et promptum erat cum Mosi, tum Israëli respondere, novimus Deum esse ens æternum & creatorem, novimus nos esse creaturas ipsius, ipsosque etiam Ægyptios.
