Sed enim verò ut Deus sit ens æternum, & creator noster plura tamen secula sub dira servitute anhelavimus. Qui igitur in animum nostrum inducemus fore ut Deus ab oneribus Ægyptiorum nos eximat, quòd sit ens æternum, & creator noster, quandoquidem æquè est æternum ens & creator in habitudine ad ÆgypÆgyptios? Fac vero nomen יהוה directè & proprie significare illum qui Erit, nempe cum Mose Exod. 3: 12. Et Deus Israëlis ejus liberator potentissimus, & Εὐεργέτης munificentissimus, quòd Deus Mosem docuit, ubi se revelare recepit in nomine יהוה Erit. Extemplò enim attexuit, Adoptabo mihi vos in populum, ero vobis in Deum, & experiemini quòd ego יהוה Deus vester sum, eximens vos oneribus Ægypti, introducam quoque vos in terram, pro qua levavi manum meam me daturum illam, Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo, & dabo eam vobis in hereditatem, ego יהוה Exod. 6: 6, 7, 8. hoc est, experiemini quam verè voluerim appellari יהוה, Erit, quia ero vobis in Deum, liberatorem ab oneribus Ægyptiorum, & benefactorem munificum, quia vos adoptabo mihi in populum. Utique neminem latere potest nomen יהוה peroportunum & immediatum esse medium ad fidem simul Mosi, simul Israëli faciendam, de futura, certaque ipsius liberatione, è servitute Ægyptiaca.
units.tr: Sixteenthly: Sixteenthly: Since God made the name יהוה his own proper name when he was undertaking, through Moses' ministry, the liberation of Israel from Egyptian slavery, so that he might persuade Moses and the people that he would free Israel from the most cruel bondage and take vengeance on the Egyptians and their gods (Exod. 6:6; 12:12), he surely made the name his own for the purpose of producing that faith, and a most suitable name it was. But this name, it is said, signifies directly and properly God, as eternal being, creator and cause of all things. Everyone can see that this name is not suitable, nor a near and necessary means, for producing that faith. For Israel's liberation from Egyptian slavery, and vengeance on the Egyptians and their gods, does not follow immediately from God's being an eternal being and creator of heaven and earth, but only through these remote consequences: (1) that the creator has the highest right over his creatures and infinite power; (2) that he wishes to free one people and adopt them as his peculiar people, while punishing another people; (3) finally, that he has declared such his good pleasure. And it would have been easy to answer both Moses and Israel: we know that God is an eternal being and creator, we know that we are his creatures, and so are the Egyptians. But although God is an eternal being and our creator, we have nonetheless sighed for many ages under cruel servitude. Why then should we persuade ourselves that God will free us from the burdens of the Egyptians because he is our eternal being and creator, since he is equally an eternal being and creator in relation to the Egyptians? Suppose, however, that the name יהוה directly and properly signified him who Erit, namely with Moses (Exod. 3:12). And God, the most powerful deliverer of Israel and the most generous Benefactor [Εὐεργέτης], since God taught Moses, when he was pleased to reveal himself in the name יהוה Erit. For he immediately added: I will take you to be my people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am יהוה your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt. I will also bring you into the land concerning which I raised my hand that I would give it to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and I will give it to you for an inheritance: I am יהוה. Exod. 6:6, 7, 8. That is, you will experience how truly I wished to be called יהוה, Erit, because I will be your God, your liberator from the burdens of the Egyptians, and your generous benefactor, because I will adopt you to be my people. Surely no one can fail to see that the name יהוה is a suitable and immediate means of producing, at once for Moses and for Israel, faith in his future and certain liberation from Egyptian slavery.

units.la: QUÆSTIO XIX.
units.tr: QUÆSTIO XIX.

units.la: Vtrum Deus nomen יהוה proprium sibi fecerit, fidelitatem suam, hoc est, constantiam in exequendis promissionibus & minis, proprie, directè, & immediatè, ut significaret.
units.tr: Whether God made the name יהוה his own proper name in order to signify his faithfulness, that is, his constancy in carrying out his promises and threats, properly, directly and immediately.

units.la: Ita sentit Socinus ad Lublinum Epist. 3. Caterum, inquit, de nomine isto ut alibi scripsi, cum Vatablo, Brentio, aliisque doctissimis viris sentio, illo potissimum Deum appellari, quia existere & esse facit id, quod futurum promisit. Ita Crellius Socinianus lib. de Deo, & ejus attributis. cap. 11. Videndum nunc porrò est, cur id nominis sibi Deus imposuerit. Id vero nobis aperiet, alter Exodi locus quem cap. 6. vers. 2. & sequentibus extare diximus. In eo Deus sic in Hebræo alloquitur Mosem. Et laudato loco integre, pergit. Ex quibus verbis satis apparet, ideò Deum sese appellare Jehova, vel potius Jihueh, aut Jeheveh, id est Erit, quia id præstiturus sit Israëlitis, quod ipsorum patribus olim promiserit. Unde futurum sit, ut experimento ipso cognoscant, eum esse Jeheveh, seu Erit, ad quod patres ipsorum nondum dum, praesertim plene, fuerint experti. Fidem nempe suam ac constantiam in servandis promissis, eo nomine potissimum declarat Deus. Eadem mens & caeteris Socinianis. Ita Episcopius Arminianorum primipilus, Instit. Theologic. lib. 4. cap. 2. Quid interim nomine illo designari credamus, in praecedentibus fusè diximus, constantiam potius, si non dumtaxat, in promisso servando significat, quàm essentiam simpliciter, aut essentiam vi sua existentem. Ero enim, qui ero, sive in tertia persona, Erit, aliud significare non potest, quam servabo ac praestabo promissum meum. Et quia Abrahamo promissum id fecerat: sed effectum ejus nondum actu ipso, sive experimento sentire dederat, hinc se Abrahamo in nomine isto cognitum nondum fuisse ait: sed posteris Abrahami, tanquam unum cum Abrahamo, ut patre suo, corpus ac populum constituentibus, isto nomine יהוה Erit, sese cognoscendum dare voluit. Sed & Rabbi Schelomo Jarchi Gallus qui denatus est ineunte saeculo à Christo nato duodecimo. Suam Deum fidelitatem in implendis promissis suis, suo nomine יהוה in Exod. 6:3. significasse asserit, textum enim sic explicat. Promisi eis promissiones, & in omnibus iis dixi illis, Ego sum Deus omnipotens; At in nomine meo יהוה, non sum notus eis. Non scribitur hic, non notum feci eis: sed non notus sum, non cognitus sum illis proprietate veritatis mea propter quam vocatur nomen meum יהוה, id est, verax, seu fidelis propter veritatem verborum meorum, quoniam ecce, promisi eis, sed non praestiti. Hanc augustissimi nominis de Dei fidelitate in implendis promissis ac minis, significationem adoptavit doctissimus Camero, caeterique deinceps Orthodoxi Theologi, eam ut amicè sociaverint praecedenti, de aeterna Dei existentia, ut auctor & causa est rerum omnium, significationi, cui & Cardinalis Bellarminus mordicus adhaesit.
units.tr: Socinus holds this view in his letter to Lubinus, Epistle 3: Moreover, as I have written elsewhere, I agree with Vatablus, Brenz and other most learned men that God is called by this name chiefly because he brings into being and makes to be whatever he has promised to be future. Crellius the Socinian says the same in his book on God and his attributes, chapter 11: We must now consider why God gave himself this name. The other passage of Exodus, which we said is found in chapter 6, verse 2 and following, will reveal this to us. There God speaks to Moses in Hebrew in this way. After quoting the passage in full, he goes on: From these words it is quite clear that God called himself Jehovah, or rather Jihueh, or Jeheveh, that is, I Will Be, because he would do for the Israelites what he had long ago promised to their fathers. Hence they would come to know by experience itself that he is Jeheveh, or I Will Be, which their fathers had not yet fully experienced. God, that is, declares his faithfulness and constancy in keeping his promises chiefly by this name. The other Socinians think the same. Episcopius, the leader of the Arminians, likewise says in his Institutes of Theology, book 4, chapter 2: What we are to believe that name designates we have explained at length above: it signifies constancy, especially in keeping a promise, rather than essence simply, or an essence existing by its own power. For "I will be who I will be," or in the third person "He will be," can mean nothing other than "I will keep and perform my promise." And since he had made this promise to Abraham, but had not yet let him feel its effect in actual fact or experience, he says that he was not yet known to Abraham by this name; but he wished to be known by this name, I Will Be, to the descendants of Abraham, who form one body and people with Abraham as their father. Rabbi Solomon Jarchi, a Frenchman who died early in the twelfth century after Christ's birth, also asserts that by his name יהוה in Exodus 6:3 God signified his faithfulness in fulfilling his promises. He explains the text thus: I made promises to them, and in all of them I said to them, I am God Almighty; but in my name יהוה I am not known to them. It is not written here, I did not make myself known to them; but I was not known, I was not recognised by them in the true nature of my name, by which I am called יהוה, that is, true, or faithful, because of the truth of my words, since behold, I promised them but did not perform. The very learned Cameron adopted this meaning of the most august name, as faithfulness in fulfilling promises and threats, and later orthodox theologians have followed him. They have joined it amicably with the earlier meaning, which refers to the eternal existence of God as the author and cause of all things. Cardinal Bellarmine also clung to this meaning stubbornly.

units.la: Tros Rutulusve suat, nulli nos in illam pertrahere sententiam potuere. Quid causae dissensus nostri, aequo perpendant animo, etiam atque etiam rogitamus.
units.tr: Whether they are Trojans or Rutulians, nobody has been able to draw us into that opinion. We ask them again and again to weigh the causes of our disagreement with a fair mind.

units.la: Primum utique id ut adstruatur, non satis videtur momentosa ratio, quòd Deus id sui indigitamentum proprium sibi fecerit, dum promissam Abrahamo, posterorum è servitute Ægyptiaca liberationem, implendam aggrederetur, tunc enim pro summa sua sapientia, non nomine יהוה Erit, subintellige, fidelis, in implendo promisso, sese indigitasset: sed contrà nomine praesenti est, subintellige, fidelis, eo enim tempore praesenti effectum dabat, quod retrò quadringentis annis sese praestiturum Abrahamo, receperat. Sed & ubi plenè Deus illam suam fidem liberaverat, & promissionem illam de liberandis dis Abrahami posteris e servitute Ægyptiaca, deque danda illis hæreditaria possessione, terrâ Canaan, in totum impleverat, id sacri nominis ut deponeret, sicuti deinceps depositi, & nomine יהוה Erit appellari desiit, ubi reapse præstitit, quod nomine illo futurum pollicebatur, exquisita Dei sapientia efflagitabat, cessat enim mediorum usus, ubi ubi causa intelligens finem sibi præstitutum, obtinuit.
units.tr: First, the reason offered to support this view does not seem weighty enough: that God made this name his own proper designation when he set about fulfilling the promise to Abraham of liberating his descendants from Egyptian slavery. For then, in his great wisdom, he would have designated himself not by the name יהוה Ero, that is, faithful in fulfilling a promise, but rather by the present name, that is, faithful, since at that time he was giving present effect to what he had undertaken to perform for Abraham four hundred years before. Moreover, when God had fully shown that faithfulness and had completely fulfilled that promise to free Abraham's descendants from Egyptian slavery and to give them the land of Canaan as a hereditary possession, he laid aside that sacred name, and he ceased to be called by the name יהוה Erit, since he had actually performed what he had promised by that name. Divine wisdom required this, for the use of means ceases when an intelligent cause has attained the end it set for itself.

units.la: Fortean reposuerint Socinianorum, Arminianorumve sequaces, non ad hanc modò, sua fidelitate implendam promissionem, sed ad alias etiam respexisse summum numen, sacrum illud indigitamentum dum sibi proprium fecit. Quasnam? dicant rogito. Jamdiu præteritas, & sua fidelitate impletas? Inde sequitur Deum fuisse notum Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo, suo illo nomine יהוה Erit, si Dei fidelitatem & in implendis promissis constantiam, significet. Sed id Deus ipse præfractè negat. Apparui Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo nomine Dei fortis & omnipotentis, sed nomine meo יהוה non cognitus sum illis. Exod. 6: 3. Futurasne & sua fidelitate demum implendas, numen respexisse si dixerint? Regero, vel illæ spectabant carnales Abrahami posteros: vel posteros spirituales, & secundum promissionem & spiritum genitos sicut Isaacum. Si prius impletis sua fidelitate terrenis illis promissionibus Deus, utique desiisset appellari יהוה Erit, ob prius laudatam rationem, sed contrarium liquidò paret, ex ultimis Prophetis, Aggæo, Zacharia, Malachia, apud quos de nomine suo יהוה Erit, Deus passim censetur. Si posterius, vel omnes illas spirituales promissiones sua jamdiu fidelitate implevit Deus, vel nondum omnes implevit, implesse omnes nemo sanus dixerit, plenum enim earum complementum in futuro beati sæculi implemento expectandum est. Cur ergo sub Christi adventum appellari יהוה Erit, Deus desiit? Eo enim indigitamento Deus appellari amaret, ac deberet, pro summa sua sapientia, si ea mente, ut fidelitatem suam, & constantiam, in implendis minis ac promissis significandam augustum illud indigitamentum suscepisset.
units.tr: Perhaps the followers of the Socinians or Arminians will reply that God, when he made this sacred designation his own, had regard not only to the promise he would fulfil by his faithfulness, but also to other things. What things? Let them say, I ask. Things that were long past and already fulfilled by his faithfulness? It follows that God was known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob by his name יהוה Erit, if that name signifies God's faithfulness and constancy in fulfilling promises. But God himself flatly denies this: I appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob under the name of God Almighty, but by my name יהוה I was not made known to them. Exodus 6:3. If they say that God had regard to things still to be fulfilled by his faithfulness, I reply: either those things concerned the fleshly descendants of Abraham, or the spiritual descendants, born according to the promise and the Spirit, like Isaac. If God had already fulfilled by his faithfulness those earthly promises, he would certainly have ceased to be called יהוה Erit, for the reason given earlier. But the contrary is plainly evident from the last prophets, Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, among whom God is everywhere called by his name יהוה Erit. If the second alternative holds, then either God has already fulfilled by his faithfulness all those spiritual promises, or he has not yet fulfilled them all. No sane person would say that all have been fulfilled, since their full completion is to be awaited in the future fulfilment of the blessed age. Why then did God cease to be called יהוה Erit at the coming of Christ? For, in his great wisdom, God would have loved and ought to have been called by that name, if he had taken up that august designation with the intention of signifying his faithfulness and constancy in fulfilling threats and promises.

units.la: Secundò. Si Deus suam fidelitatem Moïsi & Israelitis, dura servitute pressis ac gementibus, directè & proprie oportuno nomine significare voluisset, non utique nomine יהוה Erit, sese insignivisset, sed nomine אמת Verax, vel נאמן Fidelis. Ut quid enim nomine in futurum prospiciente, & ex consequenti tantum fidelitatem significante, sese appellasset, quod sine illis ambagibus proprie ac perspicue nomine fidelitatem, vel fidelem sonante, significare potuisset?
units.tr: Second. If God had wished to signify his faithfulness directly and properly, by a suitable name, to Moses and the Israelites, who were oppressed by harsh slavery and groaning, he would surely not have distinguished himself by the name יהוה Erit, but by the name Verax, true, or נאמן Fidelis, faithful. For why would he have named himself by a name that looks to the future and signifies faithfulness only as a consequence, when he could have signified faithfulness properly and plainly, without such circumlocution, by a name that simply sounds of faithfulness or of one who is faithful?

units.la: Tertiò. Confessus septuagintaduumviralis linguæ Hebrææ callen-tissimus, Jesus præ cæteris omnibus, significationis nominis יהוה optimè conscius, & Apostoli, immediatè à Deo docti, nomen tetra-grammatum, semper per τὸν πιστὸν fidelem, reddidissent, si Deus eo consilio proprium id sibi fecisset indigitamentum, suam ut fidelitatem in implendis promissis, significare voluisset. Sed contrà nunquam ac nusquam, id nominis reddidere per τὸν πιστὸν: verùm fere semper per Κύριον Dominum, & nonnunquam per Θεὸν Deum. Nec quicquam Crellium juvat regerere, quia ad promissa præstanda opus est summa potentia, quæ non cadit nisi in summum rerum omnium Dominum. Nam ut sit opus summa potentia ad præstanda promissa perardua, nemo tamen dixit Dominum, ut constantem, & fidelem in promissis ser-vandis significaret. Nempè præter potentiam summam, opus est vo-luntate firma ad præstanda promissa, scilicet absque ea fuerit, vel summus rerum Dominus, summa illa sua potentia, id effectum non dabit, quod se facturum recepit, vel pœnitentia, vel infidelitate mutatus. Sed contra ὁ πιστὸς ubi Deo tribuitur, simul summam in Deo potentiam ut possit, simul firmam & constantem voluntatem, significat, ut velit effectum dare, quicquid promisit. Ideò fides ad-hibita promissionibus divinis, nititur modò potentia Dei, ut fides Abrahami, Rom. 4: 21. Hebr. 11: 19. modò fidelitate Dei, hoc est, firma ejus & constanti voluntate implendi promissa. 1 Cor. 10: 13, Hebr. 10: 23.
units.tr: Third. The seventy translators of the Septuagint were most skilled in the Hebrew language, and Jesus, above all others, knew very well the meaning of the name יהוה, and the Apostles, taught immediately by God, would have rendered the tetragrammaton always by τὸν πιστὸν, the faithful one, if God had made that name his own designation with the purpose of signifying his faithfulness in fulfilling promises. But on the contrary, they never and nowhere rendered that name by τὸν πιστὸν; they almost always rendered it by Κύριος, the Lord, and sometimes by Θεὸς, God. Nor does it help Crellius to reply that to perform great promises there is need of supreme power, which belongs only to the supreme Lord of all things. For although supreme power is needed to perform very difficult promises, nobody has said that the word Lord signifies constancy and faithfulness in keeping promises. Indeed, besides supreme power, a firm will is needed to perform promises; without it, even the supreme Lord of all things, with his supreme power, will not bring about what he undertook to do, but will be changed by repentance or by unfaithfulness. But when ὁ πιστὸς is attributed to God, it signifies at once supreme power in God, by which he is able, and a firm and constant will, by which he is willing to bring about whatever he has promised. Therefore faith placed in the divine promises rests sometimes on the power of God, as the faith of Abraham does (Romans 4:21; Hebrews 11:19), and sometimes on the faithfulness of God, that is, his firm and constant will to fulfil his promises (1 Corinthians 10:13; Hebrews 10:23).

units.la: Quartò. Deus ubi se Moïsi mittendo, ad liberandum Israelem è servitute Ægyptiaca, revelavit suo illo indigitamento יהוה Erit, asse-rit, se notum fuisse Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo, patribus ejus & Israë-litarum: sed non fuisse illis notum nomine suo יהוה, hoc est, re per illud nomen significata, utique noluit, suam illo nomine fidelitatem, significare, quia Dei fidelitas Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo abundè pridem innotuerat, in implendis suis illis adversus illos promissioni-bus, quibus se eis obstrinxerat. Abrahamo quidem è patria Ur Chal-dæorum exeunti, ubi receperat, se fore illi clypeum in protectionem, & mercedem magnam in remunerationem Genes. 15: 1. Fore eum magnum, ut efficeret, cumque magna benedictione mactaret: sed & id præclarè præstiterat Deus cumulatissima divitiarum omnium ter-renarum suppellectile, fœderum cum regibus vicinis confœderatis gloriâ, & reportata de regibus triumphantibus victoria, amplisque spoliis parva manu trecentorum & octodecim servorum, ut princeps Dei. Dei, hoc est, excellentissimus princeps, apud Cananæos audiret. Sed & Deus illi ut summè fidelis innotuerat in implenda difficillima promissione de Isaaco generando ab ipso viribus ad generandum profligatis, annis centum nato, & ex Sara sterilitatis deploratæ, & annum nonagesimum agente, Genes. 17: 17. Isaaco pariter Deus se fidelem abundè præstiterat, ut de ejus fidelitate nullum ei dubium subesse posset, ipsum enim benedictionibus suis, juxta promissiones, cumulaverat. Genes. 26: 3, 4, 12, 24, 28. Nec minus fidelem Deus se Jacobo addixerat, dum omnes illas promissiones impleverat, quibus se illi obstrinxerat, dum illum in somnio è scalæ fastigio alloqueretur, Genes. 28: 13, 14. Hinc liquidò paret Deum non significasse suam in implendis promissionibus fidelitatem, dum sibi indidit nomen proprium יהוה Erit, quia non potuisset verè dicere, se Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo non innotuisse suo illo nomine, si eo proprie suam fidelitatem indigitare voluisset.
units.tr: Fourthly. When God, sending Moses to free Israel from Egyptian slavery, revealed himself by his name יהוה, I will be, he asserts that he had been known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the fathers of him and of the Israelites: but he certainly did not wish to be known to them by his name יהוה, that is, by the reality signified through that name, because by that name he did not mean to signify his faithfulness. God's faithfulness had long since been abundantly made known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in the fulfilling of the promises he had bound himself to them by. To Abraham, when he left Ur of the Chaldeans, God had promised to be a shield to him and his great reward (Gen. 15:1), to make him great and to bless him with a great blessing. And God had clearly carried this out, heaping upon him an abundance of all earthly riches, the glory of covenants made with the neighbouring kings, the victory won over triumphant kings, and great spoils, with a small band of three hundred and eighteen servants, so that he was heard among the Canaanites as a prince of God, that is, an outstanding prince. God had also shown himself to Abraham as most faithful in fulfilling the most difficult promise, to beget Isaac from him when his powers of begetting were spent, when he was a hundred years old, and Sarah was barren beyond hope and ninety years old (Gen. 17:17). Likewise God had amply shown himself faithful to Isaac, so that no doubt about his faithfulness could remain, for he had heaped blessings upon him according to the promises (Gen. 26:3, 4, 12, 24, 28). And God had bound himself no less faithfully to Jacob, when he fulfilled all those promises by which he had bound himself to him, speaking to him in a dream from the top of the ladder (Gen. 28:13, 14). From this it is plain that God did not signify his faithfulness in fulfilling promises when he gave himself the proper name יהוה, I will be; for he could not truly say that he had not been known to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob by that name, if he had wished to designate his faithfulness properly by it.

units.la: Nec eos juvat, qui secus sentiunt, regerere, id à Deo dictum comparatè, quasi significaret, se non adeo clarè innotuisse fidelem Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo, atque imposterum fidelem se innotescere decreverit, posteris eorum Israëlitis, sicuti Paulus comparatè loquitur, dum asserit legem, non fuisse gloriosum ministerium, comparatè, scilicet, ad Evangelium. 2 Cor. 3: 10. Ἀντοσδοξ... sanè, καὶ ἐδὲν ἀτιμ... nam Apostolus loco laudato expressam instituit inter ministerium legis & ministerium Evangelii comparationem. Sed hic nec vola, nec vestigium comparationis in revelatione, vel nominis, vel rei significatæ per nomen יהוה cum ejus revelatione facta Abrahamo, Isaaco, & Jacobo: Sed præfracta negatio notitiæ Dei sub illo nomine Patriarchis, & præfracta affirmatio revelationis factæ de se, sub nomine El Schaddai. Sed & id solidissimè firmatur ex consideratione historiæ revelationis Dei factæ Moisi, illa enim quemlibet virum non ἐμφιλόνεικον contentiosum, rectà ducit in hanc mentem & sententiam, ut plenè persuadeatur, Deum hic loci, sibi imponere nomen hactenus inauditum, & incognitum Patriarchis. Moisi, enim, petenti cum venerim ad filios Israël, eisque dixerim, Deus patrum vestrorum misit me ad vos, si dixerint mihi, quod est nomen ejus? Quid dicam illis? Deus respondet, sic dicito filiis Israël יהוה Erit, Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abrahami, Deus Isaaci, & Deus Jacobi misit me ad vos: hoc est nomen meum in saeculum, & hoc memoriale meum in æternitatem. Exod. 3: 13, -15. Utique illo sui indigitamento perpetuo, &c. & memoriali æterno, Deus, nomen suum El Schaddai, & sui revelationem factam illis nominibus, perpetuo silentio obruit, ut novum illud suum indigitamentum יהוה perpetuò obtineat; ut sub illa nomenclatione in omnem ætatem innotescat populo suo Israëli. Fac verò illo nomine Deum significasse fidelitatem suam, nec perpetuo silentio pristinam sui revelationem factam nomine El Schaddai sepeliisset, nam Deus ubi fidelem se præstat in implendis promissis suis, se Deum fortem & sufficientem fidelibus suis sese exhibet, atque fidelem, qui enim non implet promissa sua, nec Deus fortis est, nec sufficiens fidelibus suis, quia deest sufficientiæ & fidelitati suæ, vel quod non possit, vel quod nolit implere promissa sua. Verum præterea Moysi in promptu erat Deo mittenti reponere, ut quid, mi Deus, asseris te non notum fuisse patribus meis, tuo isto indigitamento יהוה, quò fidelitatem tuam, & constantiam in implendis promissis tuis significas, quandoquidem Abrahamus, Isaacus, & Jacobus, plenè ac perspicuè, te Deum suum fidelem noverunt, præclara impletione tuarum adversus eos perarduarum, nec non gloriosarum promissionum.
units.tr: Nor do those who think otherwise help themselves by replying that God spoke comparatively, as if he meant that he had not yet been made clearly known as faithful to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and had decided that he would become known as faithful in the future to their descendants, the Israelites; just as Paul speaks comparatively when he says that the law was not a glorious ministry, comparatively, that is, to the Gospel (2 Cor. 3:10). [Ἀντοσδοξ... sanè, καὶ ἐδὲν ἀτιμ...] For the Apostle, in the passage cited, sets up an explicit comparison between the ministry of the law and the ministry of the Gospel. But here there is not so much as a hint or trace of a comparison, either in the revelation of the name יהוה or of the thing signified by that name, in its revelation made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Rather there is a flat denial that God was known to the patriarchs under that name, and a flat affirmation of the revelation made of himself under the name El Shaddai. This is also most firmly confirmed by considering the history of God's revelation to Moses. That history leads any man who is not contentious straight to this understanding and opinion, so that he is fully persuaded that God here gave himself a name hitherto unheard of and unknown to the patriarchs. For when Moses asked, When I come to the children of Israel and tell them, "The God of your fathers has sent me to you," if they ask me what his name is, what shall I say to them? God answers: Thus you shall say to the children of Israel, יהוה, "I will be," "The God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you." This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial for all eternity (Exod. 3:13–15). Clearly, by this perpetual designation, and by this eternal memorial, God buried his name El Shaddai and his revelation made under those names in perpetual silence, so that his new designation יהוה might hold good for ever, and that under this name he might be made known in every age to his people Israel. But suppose that by that name God had signified his faithfulness, and had not buried in perpetual silence his earlier revelation made under the name El Shaddai. For when God shows himself faithful in fulfilling his promises, he presents himself to his faithful people as a strong and sufficient God. But one who does not fulfil his promises is neither strong nor sufficient for his faithful people, since he lacks either power or faithfulness, either being unable or being unwilling to fulfil his promises. Moreover, Moses could readily have answered God who sent him: "Why, my God, do you say that you were not known to my fathers by this designation of yours, יהוה, by which you signify your faithfulness and constancy in fulfilling your promises, since Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob knew you fully and clearly as their faithful God, through the splendid fulfilling of your most difficult and glorious promises to them?"

units.la: Quintò. Si Deus nomen יהוה proprium sibi fecisset indigitamentum proprie ac directe, ut fidelitatem suam adversus populum suum significaret, utique id nominis ratione rei significatæ Ethnicis haud fuisset ignotum. Ratio est, quia Ethnici, plane erant persuasi, Deum, quem adorabant, diversum utique pro diversis gentibus, Deum esse fidelem, ea propter Jovem celebrabant optimum & maximum: optimum, sua bonitate & fidelitate, ut vellet promissa præstare cultoribus suis: maximum, ut posset. Sed enim verò, res nomine יהוה significata plane erat ignota gentibus, hinc Pharao, Moysi edicenti, ut liberum faceret populum Israël, reponit. Quis est יהוה ut ejus voci auscultem dimittendo Israelem? Non novi יהוה, ideo etiam Israelem non dimittam. Exod. 5:2. Hinc factum, ut sancti Dei viri ubi Ethnicos alloquuntur, indigitamento illo proprio יהוה Deum suum non insigniunt, sed Deum nomine communi appellitant. Ita Joseph ad uxorem Potipharis, quomodo facerem malum hoc maximum, & peccarem in Deum? Genes. 39:9. Et ad aulicos Pharaonis post somnium in carcere mœstos, Annon Deo sunt interpretationes? Genes. 40:8. Et ad Pharaonem ipsum, Deus respondendo enuntiabit prosperitatem Pharaonis. Quod autem iteratum est somnium, ideo est quia stata est hæc res à Deo ipso, & festinanter facturus est illam Deus. Genes. 41:16,32. Ita Daniel: niel: Est Deus in coelo, revelans arcana, Deus coeli, regnum, potentiam, firmitatemque, & gloriam det tibi. Dan. 2: 28,37. Nempe, Josephus, & Daniel Ethnicos alloquuntur, quibus res significata nomine tetragrammato ignota erat penitus. Unde abunde liquet illo nomine non fuisse significatam aeternam Dei essentiam, ut causa est rerum omnium, vel ipsius in implendis promissis fidelitatem, id enim de Deo, quem colebant Ethnici, ipsis ad persuasionem plane innotuerat.
units.tr: Fifthly. If God had made the name יהוה a proper designation of himself, properly and directly, so as to signify his faithfulness towards his people, then, given the reality signified by that name, it would certainly not have been unknown to the Gentiles. The reason is that the Gentiles were fully persuaded that the God they worshipped, whom they thought of as different for different nations, was faithful; therefore they celebrated Jupiter as best and greatest: best in his goodness and faithfulness, in that he would wish to perform his promises to his worshippers; greatest in that he was able to do so. But the reality signified by the name יהוה was entirely unknown to the nations. Hence Pharaoh, when Moses commanded him to let the people of Israel go free, replied: Who is יהוה, that I should obey his voice by letting Israel go? I do not know יהוה, so I will not let Israel go either (Exod. 5:2). Hence it came about that when the holy men of God addressed the Gentiles, they did not name their God by that proper designation יהוה, but called him by a common name. So Joseph to the wife of Potiphar: How could I do this great evil and sin against God? (Gen. 39:9). And to Pharaoh's courtiers, who were sad after their dream in prison: Do not interpretations belong to God? (Gen. 40:8). And to Pharaoh himself: God will answer and declare the welfare of Pharaoh. As for the dream being repeated, it is because the matter has been established by God himself, and God will shortly bring it about (Gen. 41:16, 32). Likewise Daniel: There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets; may the God of heaven give you kingdom, power, strength, and glory (Dan. 2:28, 37). Clearly Joseph and Daniel were speaking to Gentiles, for whom the reality signified by the Tetragrammaton was entirely unknown. From this it is abundantly clear that by that name was not signified the eternal essence of God as the cause of all things, nor his faithfulness in fulfilling promises; for these things about the God whom the Gentiles worshipped were plainly well known to them and were persuasive.

units.la: Sexto. Si Deus ubi moliretur populi Israel e servitute Aegyptiaca liberationem, ejus in terram Canaan introductionem, ad fidem suam liberandam, & fidelitatem in implendis promissis illis, factis pridem Abrahamo, significandam, nomen יהוה eo consilio sibi proprium fecisset, illo ipso nomine, utique erat appellandus, ubi missione Christi Moise longe excellentioris, promissiones spirituales Abrahamo factas, de nascituro semine benedicto Messiâ, de liberatione per ipsum spirituali generis humani e servitute lamentabili, e potestate principis tenebrarum, sanguine Christi agni incontaminati, ejusque gloriosa translatione, manu extensa, in regnum admirabilis suae lucis, in Canaan spiritualem, & coelestem Jerusalem, quo enim gloriosiores sunt illae, quibus se obstrinxerat promissiones, de Messiâ ex virgine nascituro, de eo Immanuele, Θεάνθρωπω, Deo simul & homine, de diabolo tenebrarum principe, cum ejus imperio destruendo, de gentibus daemoni idolisque mancipatis, toto orbe ad cognitionem cultumque veri Dei vocandis, de Judaeis incredulis, atque rejectis, post gentium plenitudinem, convertendis, de revocandis universali resurrectione ad vitam mortuis, de innovandis coelo ac terra, solutis igne, fusisque elementis, de novo coelo, novaque terra creandis, de immutandis in vitam coelestem & immortalem superstitibus in terra mortalibus, de ultimo judicio, vivis ac mortuis judicandis, de addicendis poenis aeternis ad finem, impiis & incredulis, de evehendis pompa triumphali splendidis nubium curribus ad occursum Domini fidelibus, iisque plaudentibus Angelorum myriadibus, coelo, throno, vitaeque corona gloriosa donandis. Deus utique stupendum opus, sua fidelitate moliturus, novo Euangelii saeculo, augustissimo illo nomine יהוה pro sua sapientia erat insigniendus, siquidem ad fidelitatem suam significandam eo se insignire voluisset. Verum nunquam ac nusquam eo fuit indigitamento notatus, sed mutato nomine, perpetuo Κύριος, vel cum articulo ὁ Κύριος. Dominus, vel ὁ Θεὸς Deus fuit appellatus, vel dum versione septuaginta duumvirali, in Græcum sermonem, viam sibi muniret ad vocationem gentium, vel dum Messias Christus, ejusque Apostoli Judæis convertendis, vel gentibus, incumberent, & apud homines in terris versarentur.
units.tr: Sixthly. If God, when he was undertaking the liberation of the people of Israel from Egyptian slavery and their introduction into the land of Canaan, had made the name יהוה his own for the purpose of vindicating his faithfulness and signifying his fidelity in fulfilling those promises made long before to Abraham, then surely he would have been called by that very name when, through the sending of Christ, who far surpasses Moses, the spiritual promises made to Abraham were fulfilled. These were the promises of the blessed Messiah to be born of his seed, of the spiritual liberation of the human race through him from wretched servitude, from the power of the prince of darkness, by the blood of Christ the unspotted Lamb, and of their glorious transfer, with his hand outstretched, into the kingdom of his marvellous light, into the spiritual Canaan and the heavenly Jerusalem. For how much more glorious are the promises he bound himself by: of the Messiah to be born of a virgin, of that Immanuel, God-man [Θεάνθρωπω], God and man at once; of the destruction of the devil, the prince of darkness, and of his dominion; of the nations given over to demons and idols, to be called throughout the whole world to the knowledge and worship of the true God; of the unbelieving and rejected Jews, to be converted after the fullness of the Gentiles; of the dead, to be raised to life at the universal resurrection; of the renewal of heaven and earth, when the elements are dissolved by fire and melted; of the new heaven and new earth to be created; of the living on earth, mortal, to be changed into heavenly and immortal life; of the last judgment, when the living and the dead are judged; of eternal punishments to be inflicted on the wicked and unbelieving to the end; of the faithful to be carried up in triumphal procession on shining chariots of clouds to meet the Lord, with myriads of angels applauding, and to be given heaven, a throne, and the glorious crown of life. Surely God, about to accomplish by his faithfulness such a stupendous work in the new age of the Gospel, would have been designated, in his wisdom, by that most august name יהוה, if he had wished to mark his faithfulness by it. But he was never and nowhere named by that designation; instead, under a changed name, he was always called [Κύριος], or with the article [ὁ Κύριος], Lord, or [ὁ Θεὸς], God. He was so called either in the Septuagint version, when the two-fold translation into Greek opened a way for him to the calling of the Gentiles, or when the Messiah Christ and his Apostles were engaged in converting the Jews or the Gentiles and were living among men on earth.

units.la: Nec quicquam juvant desumptæ à Socinianis, vel Remonstrantibus, ex superstitione, vel metu Judæorum, vel vitando scandalo, & si quæ sint ejusdem farinæ exceptiunculæ illæ, quæ supra futilitatis suæ pœnas nobis dederunt.
units.tr: Nor do the objections taken from the Socinians or the Remonstrants help at all, whether they arise from superstition, from fear of the Jews, or from avoiding offence. And whatever small exceptions of this kind there are have already paid the penalty for their futility above.

units.la: Septimò. Si Dei fidelitas à mundi conditu in exequendis minis, & implendis promissis, penitus perspecta erat Adamo, morti addicto, & maledictioni, paradiso Eden, vitæque arbore exterminato, terribilem juxta Dei comminationem, simul ac universo generi humano antediluviano, & post diluvium, tremendam juxta comminationem annis centum & viginti prædictam, novaeque genti, oriundæ ex Noacho, in arcu cœlesti, in signum fidelitatis Dei, de non amplius perdendo genere humano, aquis cataclysmi generalis, constituto in nubibus, ut Dei fidelitas perseveret de generatione in generationem. Psalm. 100: 5. & 117: 2. Ut omnes semitæ Dei sint fidelitas. Psalm. 25: 10. Hoc est, omnes Dei revelationes, quibus Deus velut exiens luce gloriæ suæ, inaccessa omnibus creaturis, sese hominibus manifestat, vel stupendis operibus suis, vel verbo minarum, aut promissionum suarum. Utique nihil quicquam opus erat suam illam fidelitatem ut significaret, novo illo sui indigitamento יהוה, Patriarchis ignoto, sese insigniret. Sed prius est verum, ex historia lapsus Adami, & diluvii, & Psalmis illis bene multis, ubi Dei fidelitas ad cœlos, & nubes pertingere dicitur, ubi Deus, ad arcum Dei fidelitatis signum, in nubibus constitutum respicit. Psalm. 36: 6. & 57: 11. & 89: 3, 6, 9, 15, 25, 34, 50. & 108: 5. & 119: 89, 90.
units.tr: Seventh. If God's faithfulness was thoroughly known from the foundation of the world, it was known to Adam, condemned to death and the curse, and banished from Paradise of Eden and the tree of life, in accordance with God's dreadful threat. It was known also to the whole human race before the flood, and after the flood to the new people descended from Noah, in accordance with the terrible threat of a hundred and twenty years. It was known to them through the rainbow in the clouds, set as a sign of God's faithfulness that he would no longer destroy the human race with the waters of a universal deluge, so that God's faithfulness might endure from generation to generation. Ps. 100:5 and 117:2. So that all the paths of God might be faithfulness. Ps. 25:10. That is, all of God's revelations, by which God, as if breaking forth in the light of his glory, inaccessible to all creatures, makes himself known to men, either by his wonderful works or by the word of his threats and promises. Surely there was no need for him to signify his faithfulness by that new designation of himself, יהוה [Jehovah], unknown to the patriarchs. Rather the truth is the reverse: it is shown from the history of Adam's fall and the flood, and from the many Psalms where God's faithfulness is said to reach the heavens and the clouds, and where God looks upon the rainbow, the sign of his faithfulness, set in the clouds. Ps. 36:6; 57:11; 89:3, 6, 9, 15, 25, 34, 50; 108:5; 119:89, 90.

units.la: Octavò. Quandoquidem omnibus compertum est, Deum passim, innumerisque ferè in locis Scripturæ, prædicere, fore, ut Pharao & Ægyptii idololatræ, cæteraque gentes latè per terrarum orbem, nec non populus suus, ad castra idololatrarum transfuga, vel ab idololatris oppressus, cognoscant eum esse יהוה, argumentum est omni exceptione majus, quod Deus eo nomine de se significare constituerat, nondum fuisse ab omnibus plenè perspectum, sed Deum esse in explendis minis, promissisque suis implendis, fidelem, tot erat tunc temporis demonstratum argumentis, quot extabant historiæ de ejus minis præstitis, & impletis promissionibus pretiosis, ut ejus fidelitas, omnibus conspicua mortalibus, ad nubes cœli pertingeret.
units.tr: Eighth. Since it is known to everyone that God, in almost countless places of Scripture, foretells that Pharaoh and the idolatrous Egyptians, and the other nations throughout the world, and likewise his own people, when they desert to the camps of idolaters or are oppressed by idolaters, will come to know that he is יהוה [Jehovah], it is an argument greater than any objection that God had resolved to signify himself by that name, and that it had not yet been fully perceived by all. God was faithful in carrying out his threats and fulfilling his promises, and at that time this was demonstrated by as many proofs as there were histories of his threats carried out and his precious promises fulfilled, so that his faithfulness, visible to all mortals, reached to the clouds of heaven.

units.la: Nonò. Pro summa sapientia sua Deus nomen יהוה, proprium sibi fecit indigitamentum, se ab idolis, falsisque gentium numinibus, gloriosè ut distingueret, quod & fusius infra demonstrabimus, ut ratione augustissimi nominis sanctus passim, hoc est, gloriosè separatus, audiat, & habeatur, & sanctè protestetur, id nominis perpetuum esse sui monumentum, gloriamque intemeratam, seque eam sculptilibus non daturum, ego sum יהוה, illud nomen meum est, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo, & laudem meam sculptilibus. Jesai. 42:8. Hinc liquet, eo nomine, Deum sese gloriosè secernere ab idolis, cæterisque gentium Diis. Sed ubi negat, se daturum gloriam, & laudem suam illo nomine significatam, sculptilibus, nec de essentia sua æterna, nec de fidelitate sua infinita sermonem habet, id enim omninò impossibile est, meris nempè creaturis, futilibusve hominum figmentis, collatum ire Deum, naturam suam, suamve perfectissimam fidelitatem. Superest igitur, ut Deus neget, se permissurum, falsa ut gentium numina sibi tribuant divinitatis, & fidelitatis suæ gloriam, sed & id verum non comperitur, id enim permisit, hoc est, nullus impedivit. Ecquid igitur? Superest Deus ut neget, se non permissurum ut gloriam & laudem suam illo sui indigitamento יהוה significatam, Deorum alter, quisquis demum fuerit Chaldæorum, Assyriorum, Syrorum, Ægyptiorum, Græcorum, Romanorum, sibi tribuat, quod sequenti quæstione demonstratum imus.
units.tr: Ninth. In his supreme wisdom God made the name יהוה [Jehovah] his own proper designation, so that he might gloriously distinguish himself from idols and the false divinities of the nations, which we shall also demonstrate more fully below. Thus by reason of that most august name he is everywhere heard and regarded as holy, that is, gloriously set apart, and he solemnly declares that this name is his perpetual memorial and his unimpaired glory, and that he will not give that glory to carved images: I am יהוה; that is my name; my glory I will not give to another, nor my praise to graven images. Isa. 42:8. From this it is clear that by that name God gloriously separates himself from idols and the other gods of the nations. But when he says that he will not give to graven images the glory and praise signified by that name, he is speaking neither of his eternal essence nor of his infinite faithfulness. For it is utterly impossible that God, his nature, or his most perfect faithfulness should be set alongside mere creatures or the futile fictions of men. It remains, then, that God denies he would permit the false gods of the nations to claim for themselves the divinity and the glory of his faithfulness. But this too is not found to be true, for he did permit it, that is, no one prevented it. What then? It remains that God denies he would allow the glory and praise signified by that designation יהוה [Jehovah] to be claimed by another of the gods, whoever they might be, of the Chaldeans, Assyrians, Syrians, Egyptians, Greeks or Romans. This we shall show in the following question.

units.la: QUAESTIO XX.
units.tr: QUESTION XX.

units.la: Quid Deus ignotum antea Patriarchis, vel à mundi conditu, suo illo proprio indigitamento יהוה Mosi, populoque Israëli suo, proprie, ac directè, significare voluerit?
units.tr: What did God, who was unknown to the Patriarchs before the creation of the world, intend to signify, properly and directly, by that peculiar name יהוה given to Moses and to his people Israel?

units.la: Magnum pietatis & redemptionis mysterium, magno isthoc nomine praenuntiatum ac promissum, in clara Scripturarum luce, demonstraturis, tria haec argumenti momentosa capita simul demonstranda incumbunt. 1°. Gloriosum istud numinis indigitamentum quantum quantum est prospexisse in futurum, ut significet Erit. 2°. Cur sapientissimum numen, nomen Erit in futurum prospiciens indere sibi voluerit, cum primùm Mosis ministerio populi sui Israël è dura servitute Ægyptiaca, gloriosam redemptionem moliretur. 3°. Quid Israëlitarum Deus suo illo proprio terribilique indigitamento יהיה Erit, proprie, per se, directè, & immediate, significare voluerit?
units.tr: To set out in the clear light of the Scriptures the great mystery of piety and redemption, which was foretold and promised under this great name, three weighty points must be demonstrated together. (1) That this glorious name of the Deity, in whatever way it is understood, looks forward to the future and signifies Will be. (2) Why the most wise Deity, looking forward to the future in the name Will be, chose to give itself this name at the very time when, through Moses' ministry, it was undertaking the glorious redemption of its people Israel from harsh Egyptian servitude. (3) What the God of Israel meant to signify properly, per se, directly and immediately, by that peculiar and terrible name יהיה Will be.

units.la: Primum causae momentum quod attinet, Mosi percontanti quid respondebo filiis Israël dicentibus mihi, quod est nomen ejus? Deus dixit Mosi אהיה אשר אהיה quod proprie sonat Ero, qui Ero, quibus exemplò addidit, sic dices filiis Israël אהיה Ero, misit me ad vos, Exod. 3: 13,14. Ita sentiunt Onkelos, ille enim Hebraea verba retinet, & paraphrastes Hierosolymitanus, & Jonathan BenUziel [illegible, ~6 letters], Ego sum, qui fui & futurus sum. Ita Maimonides Hebraeorum doctissimus vertente Joanne Buxtorfio filio, Ehieh asher Ehieh, h.e. ero qui ero. More Nevoc. lib. 1. cap. 62. & cap. 63. Et positum est nomen primum, quod subjecti vicem sustinet Ehieh Ero. & nomen secundum, quod attributum ejus est & idem vocatur Ehieh Ero. Ita R. Salomon qui sic explicat, Ero cum eis in hac afflictione, qui Ero cum eis in servitute alienorum regnorum. Et AbenEzra dum ait: Ascher Ehieh, qui Ero, expositionem esse primi Ehieh Ero. Ita Hiskuni ex recentioribus Hebraeorum Rabbinis referente Fagio, nempe ut primum Ehieh, id est Ero, sit nomen Dei, alterum vero Ascher Ehieh, id est qui ero, sit ejus exposipositio. Ita ipse Buxtorfius: Etymologiam ejus quod attinet, habet simpliciter formam futuri à verbo היה fuit, unde אהיה אשר אהיה de verbo ad verbum est, Ero qui Ero: vel ero quia ero. Differt. 5. de Nom. Dei Hebraic. Ita Vatablus, & Mercerus Lutetiæ professores Regii. Ita Scindlerus in nomen Tetragrammatum. Nec rectius factum, ut existimat Buxtorfius, ubi septuaginta verterunt Ego sum qui sum. Nempe quivis homulus vere asserere potest dum existit, Ego sum qui sum. Verissima enim est propositio identica: sed nemo Angelorum, nedum hominum vere asserere potest, Ero qui Ero. Ubi enim dixit, Ego sum qui sum, illico potest desinere esse, vel annihilatione, vel naturali corruptione, ut unus Deus meritissimo jure asserere valeat, Ero, qui Ero.
units.tr: As to the first point, when Moses asked, What shall I answer the sons of Israel, who say to me, what is his name? God said to Moses [אהיה אשר אהיה] I will be who I will be, which properly means I will be, who I will be. He at once added, Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel [אהיה] I will be has sent me to you (Exod. 3:13, 14). So understand Onkelos, for he keeps the Hebrew words, and the Jerusalem paraphrast, and Jonathan Ben Uziel: I am who was and who will be. So Maimonides, the most learned of the Hebrews, as rendered by the younger Johannes Buxtorf: Ehieh asher Ehieh, that is, I will be who I will be. (More Nevochim, bk. 1, chs. 62 and 63.) The first name, which stands in the place of the subject, is Ehieh, I will be, and the second name, which is its attribute, is also called Ehieh, I will be. So R. Solomon, who explains it thus: I will be with them in this affliction, who will be with them in servitude under foreign kingdoms. And Abenezra, when he says: Asher Ehieh, who will be, is an explanation of the first Ehieh, I will be. So Hiskuni, among the more recent Hebrew rabbis, as reported by Fagius: namely, that the first Ehieh, that is I will be, is the name of God, while the second, Asher Ehieh, that is who will be, is its explanation. So Buxtorf himself: As to its etymology, it simply has the form of the future from the verb היה was, whence אהיה אשר אהיה word for word is, I will be who I will be, or I will be because I will be. (Dissertation 5, on the Hebrew names of God.) So Vatablus, and Mercerus, royal professors at Paris; so Scindler on the Tetragrammaton. Nor was it rightly done, as Buxtorf thinks, when the Seventy translated I am who I am [ἐγὼ εἰμὶ ὁ ὤν]. For any mere man can truly say while he exists, I am who I am. That is a most true identical proposition. But no angel, let alone any man, can truly say I will be who I will be. For when he has said I am who I am, he can at once cease to be, either by annihilation or by natural corruption, whereas the one God can with the most just right say I will be who I will be.

units.la: Robur summum explicationi, sapientissimum numen addidit ubi Mosi imperat de se in tertia persona ut loquatur, extemplò attexuit יהוה misit me ad vos, Exod. 3: 15, 16. Neminem vero fugit יהוה tertiam esse personam futuri verbi היה fuit, quod & fatetur doctissimus Buxtorfius dissertatione laudata, dum ait nomen illud derivatur à radice היה vel היה Jod ab initio est formativum nominum propriorum, ut in יעקב & aliis, desumptum ex tertia persona futuri. Fatetur ergò nomen יהוה esse tertiam personam futuri היה. Unde colligere in promtu est, sicut Isichac, significat, ridebit, & Jaacob, supplantabit, ita יהוה futurum verbi היה Esse, significare Erit. Ita Mercerus in Genef. 2: 4. Si legendum sit, (Tetragrammatum) malim legere per tria Segol יְהוָה, id est, Erit Ita Grotius in Exod. 3: 15. Erit. Ita Oleaster, Flacus Illiricus, Arias Montanus, Capellus, ita Paraphrastæ Onkelosus, Jonathan, Jerosolymitanus ut supra. Ita Clemens Alexandrinus libro quinto Stromat. pag. 562. Λέγεται ὁ Ι′αὼ ὁ μεσηεμψάμενος ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐσόμενος. Dicitur autem Iaou, quod vertitur, qui est & qui erit. Idem ultrò fatetur Menasse Ben Israel in Conciliatore suo Quæst. 3. in Exod. Igitur, inquit, ex opinione omnium Philosophorum, quos supra citavi, dicimus, & nomen Tetragrammatum denotare substantiam divinitatis, & vocem אהיה nisi quod hæc est prima persona singularis futuri, היה autem tertia. Sed ad calcem quæstionis novissimus Conciliator lectorem monet se reverentia divinitatis pro ה primo, quod est in Tetragrammato scripsisse י. Eadem futili reverentia Tiberiensium Masoretarum factum existimamus ut ת in א commutaverint Ecclesiastæ 11: 3. Et si arbor ceciderit versus meridiem, vel versus septentrionem, ubi ceciderit, ibi יהוא Erit. Ubi Mercerus notavit, א esse pro ת tertiæ personæ futuri היה verbi. Quid vetat igitur quo minus dicamus nomen quadriliterum lectum & pronuntiatum fuisse Jeheve, quod & docuit Drusius in Exod. 3: 15. Sed enim Jeheve, vel Jeve, proprie significat erit. Septuaginta seniores etsi in Exodum verterint ἐγὼ εἰμὶ ὁ ὤν, Ego sum qui sum, ipsi tamen nomen illud legerunt & pronuntiarunt Jeheve, nempe verba ista יהוה וכרו verterunt ἔσται, μνημόσυνον αὐτοῦ. Erit, est memoriale ejus. Hos. 12: 5.
units.tr: The sovereign strength of the explanation lies in this: when the most wise Deity commanded Moses to speak of himself in the third person, it immediately added יהוה has sent me to you (Exod. 3:15, 16). No one fails to see that יהוה is the third person of the future of the verb היה was, which the most learned Buxtorf also admits in the dissertation cited, when he says: That name is derived from the root היה or היה. The Jod at the beginning is the formative letter of proper names, as in יעקב and others, taken from the third person of the future. He therefore admits that the name יהוה is the third person of the future היה. Hence it is easy to infer that, just as Isaac means he will laugh, and Jacob means he will supplant, so יהוה, the future of the verb היה to be, means He will be. So Mercerus on Gen. 2:4: If the Tetragrammaton is to be read, I would rather read it with three segols יְהוָה, that is, Will be. So Grotius on Exod. 3:15: Will be. So Oleaster, Flacius Illyricus, Arias Montanus, Capellus, and so the paraphrasts Onkelos and Jonathan and the Jerusalem paraphrast, as above. So Clement of Alexandria, in the fifth book of the Stromata, p. 562: Λέγεται ὁ Ἰαὼ ὁ μεσηεμψάμενος ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐσόμενος. Iaou is called, which is rendered, he who is and who will be. Menasseh Ben Israel himself gladly admits the same in his Conciliator, question 3 on Exodus: Therefore, he says, by the opinion of all the philosophers I have cited above, we say that the Tetragrammaton denotes the substance of the Deity, and the word אהיה, except that this is the first person singular of the future, היה, but the latter is the third. But at the end of the question the most recent Conciliator warns the reader that, out of reverence for the Deity, he wrote י for the first ה that stands in the Tetragrammaton. By the same empty reverence, we think, the Tiberian Masoretes changed ת into א in Eccles. 11:3: And if a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, wherever it falls there יהוא it will be. There Mercerus noted that א stands for ת, the third person of the future of the verb היה. What then forbids us from saying that the four-letter name was read and pronounced Jehovah, as Drusius also taught on Exod. 3:15? For Jehovah or Jeve properly means he will be. Although the Seventy elders translated I am who I am [ἐγὼ εἰμὶ ὁ ὤν] in Exodus, Ego sum qui sum, they nevertheless read and pronounced that name Jehovah, for they translated the words יהוה וכרו as ἔσται μνημόσυνον αὐτοῦ, Erit, est memoriale ejus [ἔσται, μνημόσυνον αὐτοῦ]: He will be, his memorial (Hos. 12:5).

units.la: Magnum & gloriosum illud Dei indigitamentum יהוה in futurum prospicere, & significare, Erit, ut Moses & Israelitarum animum in spem & exspectationem futuri erigeret, evidentissime numen sapientissimum significavit, dum suo illi indigitamento ubivis fere verba in futurum prospicientia attexuit, sive promittat, sive minetur. Pauca ex millenis loca selegisse & notasse sufficiat, exorsis abs locis illis ubi Deus proprium sibi fecit id nominis indigitamentum. Vade & congrega seniores Israel, & dic eis. יהוה Deus patrum vestrorum apparuit mihi, & dixit אעלה אתכם מעני מצרים, ἀναξιῶσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κακώσεως τ Αἰγυπτίων. Educam vos ex afflictione Ægyptiorum. Exod. 3: 16, 17. Idcirco dic filiis Israel, ego יהוה, והוצאתי ἐξάξω, & Educam vos ab oneribus Ægyptiorum והצלתי ῥύσομαι, & eruam vos a servitute eorum וגאלתי λυτρώσομαι, & redimam vos bracchio extenso, & judiciis magnis ולקחתי λήψομαι, & accipiam vos mihi in populum. והייתי ἔσομαι, & ero vobis in Deum. Exod. 6: 6, 7. Et dixit Moses ad Aaron. Hoc est quod dixit יהוה in iis, qui accedunt ad me אקרש ἁγιασθήσομαι sanctificabor, & in conspectu totius populi אכבד δοξασθήσομαι glorificabor. Levit. 10: 3. Benedicet tibi יהוה & custodiet te; lucere faciet יהיה faciem suam super te, & miseribitur tui. Attollet יהוה faciem suam ad te, & ponet tibi pacem, & ponent nomen meum super filios Israelis. ואני אברכם ἐγὼ εὐλογήσω αὐτοῖς, & ego benedicam eis. Numer. 6: 23, 24, 25, 26, 27. Nisi custodieris ut facias omnia verba legis istius, qua scripta sunt in libro isto, ut timeas nomen gloriosum, & terribile istud את יהוה Deum tuum והפלא יהוה ἐνδοξάσει, augebit mirum in modum Dominus plagas tuas &c. והשיב ἀποστρέψει, & convertet in te omnem infirmitatem Ægypti &c. Deut. 28: 58, 59, 60. Dixitque Josue ad filios Israel, accedite huc, & audite verba יהוה Dei vestri. Dixit praterea Josue in hoc cognoscetis quod Deus vivens est in medio vestri והורש ὁλοθρεύων ἐξολοθρεῦσαι, & quod perdendo disperdet a facie vestra Chananaum &c. Jos. 3: 9. 3: 9, 10. Quæ respondit ibo quidem tecum, verum in hoc non erit gloria tua, quia in manum mulieris יהוה וימכר vendet Dominus Sisera. Jud. 4: 9. Tum dixit ad eum יהוה, והיה כי אהיה עמך והכיתּ, καὶ ἔσται μετ᾽ σῦ, καὶ πατάξεις, quia ero tecum percutiesque Midian. Jud. 6: 16. Benedictus יהוה qui non permisit ut deesset tibi cognatus hodie ויקרא & vocabitur nomen ejus in Israël והיה לך καὶ ἔσται σοι, & erit tibi animum tuum recreatu- rum &c. Ruth. 4: 14, 15. In die illa אקים ἐπεγερῶ suscitabo contra Heli omnia, quæ locutus sum adversus domum ejus והכל הבית ἀξιομα, καὶ πληρώσω, incipiam & perficiam. 1 Sam. 3: 12. Tu enim יהוה exercituum Deus Israëlis revelasti aurem servi tui dicendo בית אבנה־לך οἶκον οἰκοδομήσω σοι, Domum ædificabo tibi. Nunc itaque יהוה Deus, tu enim es Deus והיו ודבריך אמת καὶ οἱ λόγοί σε ἔσονται ἀληθινοί, Et verba tua erunt vera. 2 Sam. 7: 27, 28. Et dixit יהוה ad eum, vade revertere in viam tuam &c. והיה καὶ ἔσται, Et erit, quicumque fugerit gladium Hazael, occidet eum Jehu, & quicumque fugerit gladium Jehu interficiet eum Elizæus והשארתי καὶ καταλείψω, & reservabo in Israële septem millia &c. 1 Reg. 19: 15, 17, 18. Accesserat verò vir Dei & dixerat Regi Israëlis his verbis. Sic dixit יהוה, propterea quod dixerunt Aramæi, Deus montium, est יהוה, & non Deus vallium est ונתתי καὶ δώσω dabo universam multitudinem magnam in manum tuam: ut sciatis quod ego sum יהוה. 1 Reg. 20: 18. Idcirco sic dicit יהוה de lecto super quem ascendisti, לא־תרד תמות תמות כי טות מטה καταβήση ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῇ θανατῷ ἀποθανῇ. Non descendes, sed morte morieris. 2 Reg. 1: 4. Sic enim dixit יהוה: לא־תראו רוח ולא־תראו גשם οὐκ ὄψεσθε πνεῦμα, ἐπὶ μὴ ἴδετε ὑετόν, non videbitis ventum, neque plu- viam, & alveus iste replebitur aquis, & bibetis vos, & familia vestra & jumenta vestra. Leve autem est hoc in oculis יהוה, ונתן, καὶ δώσει, insuper dabit Moab in manum vestram, & percutietis omnem civitatem munitam, & omnem urbem electam, & universam arborem fructiferam succidetis, cun- ctosque fontes aquarum obturabitis, & omnem agrum egregium operietis, la- pidibus. 2 Reg. 3: 17, 18, 19. Nunc fili mi, עמך והצלחה ובנית בית יהוה, ἡ πνεῦμα μετὰ σε, καὶ κατευοδωθῇς, καὶ οἰκοδομήσεις οἶκον κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σε. Erit יהוה tecum, & prosperè ages & ædificabis domum יהוה Dei tui. 1 Chron. 22: 11. Apparuit autem יהוה ipsi Salomoni, & dixit. &c. ואני אשמע מן השמים ואסלח לחטאתם וארפא Καὶ ἐγὼ εἰσακούσομαι ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἱλεως ἔσομαι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῶν, καὶ ἰάσομαι τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν, Et ego quoque exaudiam de cœlo, & parcam peccato eorum, & sanabo terram eorum. 2 Chron. 7: 12: 14. Ac dixi, qua-so יהוה Deus coeli. &c. memento quaefo verbi, quod praecepisti Moysi servo tuo, dicendo, אִתָּם־חֲמַעֲלוּ אֲנִי אֹפִיךְ אִתְּכֶם בָּעַמִּים εάν απστρέψητε υμεις, εγώ απσοστρεφω υμας εν τοις λαοις, vos prævaricabimi, ego dispergam vos in populos. אֲקַבְּצֵם וְהֵבִיאֹתִים אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם συναξω αυτους, και εισαξω αυτους εις τον τόπον, congregabo eos, & adducam eos ad hunc locum &c. Nehem. 1: 5, 8, 9.
units.tr: That great and glorious designation of God, יהוה, which looks to the future and means It will be, clearly showed the most wise Deity wishing to raise the spirit of Moses and the Israelites to hope and expectation of what is to come. He wove words looking to the future into that designation almost everywhere, whether he was promising or threatening. It is enough to select and note a few places out of thousands, beginning with those where God made that designation his own. Go and gather the elders of Israel, and say to them: Jehovah, the God of your fathers, appeared to me and said, I will bring you up [אעלה אתכם] out of the affliction of the Egyptians [ἀναξιῶσω ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κακώσεως τῶν Αἰγυπτίων]. Exod. 3: 16, 17. Therefore say to the sons of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I will bring you out [והוצאתי, ἐξάξω] from the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you [והצלתי, ῥύσομαι] from their servitude, and I will redeem you [וגאלתי, λυτρώσομαι] with an outstretched arm and great judgments, and I will take you [ולקחתי, λήψομαι] to me as a people, and I will be [והייתי, ἔσομαι] your God. Exod. 6: 6, 7. Then Moses said to Aaron, This is what Jehovah said: among those who come near me I will be sanctified [אקרש, ἁγιασθήσομαι], and before all the people I will be glorified [אכבד, δοξασθήσομαι]. Lev. 10: 3. Jehovah bless you and keep you; Jehovah make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you. Jehovah lift up his face upon you and give you peace, and they shall put my name upon the sons of Israel, and I will bless them. Num. 6: 23–27. If you do not keep all the words of this law, written in this book, so that you fear this glorious and terrible name, Jehovah your God, Jehovah will wondrously increase your plagues [והפלא, ἐνδοξάσει] and will turn upon you every sickness of Egypt [והשיב, ἀποστρέψει]. Deut. 28: 58–60. Joshua said to the sons of Israel, Come here and hear the words of Jehovah your God. Joshua said further, By this you shall know that the living God is in your midst, and that he will utterly destroy [והורש, ὁλοθρεύων ἐξολοθρεῦσαι] before your face the Canaanites. Josh. 3: 9, 10. Deborah answered: I will indeed go with you, but your glory will not be in this, because Jehovah will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman [וימכר]. Judg. 4: 9. Then Jehovah said to him, I will be with you [והיה, καὶ ἔσται μετ᾽ σοῦ], and you will strike [καὶ πατάξεις] Midian. Judg. 6: 16. Blessed be Jehovah, who has not allowed you to lack a kinsman today, and his name shall be called in Israel [ויקרא], and it shall be to you [והיה לך, καὶ ἔσται σοι] a restorer of your soul. Ruth 4: 14, 15. On that day I will raise up [אקים, ἐπεγερῶ] against Eli all that I have spoken against his house [והכל, ἀξιομα, καὶ πληρώσω], I will begin and complete it. 1 Sam. 3: 12. For you, Jehovah of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed to the ear of your servant, saying, I will build you a house [οἶκον οἰκοδομήσω σοι]. Now therefore, Jehovah God, you are God, and your words will be true [καὶ οἱ λόγοί σου ἔσονται ἀληθινοί]. 2 Sam. 7: 27, 28. Jehovah said to him, Go, return on your way, etc. And it shall be [והיה, καὶ ἔσται] that whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will slay him, and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will slay him; and I will leave [והשארתי, καὶ καταλείψω] seven thousand in Israel, etc. 1 Kings 19: 15, 17, 18. Moreover a man of God came near and spoke to the king of Israel in these words: Thus says Jehovah, because the Arameans said, Jehovah is a God of the mountains, and not a God of the valleys, I will give [ונתתי, καὶ δώσω] all this great multitude into your hand, so that you may know that I am Jehovah. 1 Kings 20: 18. Therefore thus says Jehovah concerning the bed on which you have gone up: You shall not come down, but you shall surely die [καταβήση ... ἀποθανῇ]. 2 Kings 1: 4. For thus said Jehovah: You shall not see wind, nor shall you see rain [οὐκ ὄψεσθε πνεῦμα, οὐδὲ ἴδετε ὑετόν]; you shall not see wind or rain, yet this valley shall be filled with water, and you shall drink, you and your household and your animals. And this is a light thing in the eyes of Jehovah: he will also [ונתן, καὶ δώσει] give Moab into your hand, and you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and you shall cut down every fruitful tree, stop up all the springs of water, and cover every good field with stones. 2 Kings 3: 17, 18, 19. Now, my son, Jehovah will be with you, and you will prosper and build the house of Jehovah your God [ἔσται κύριος μετὰ σοῦ, καὶ κατευοδωθῇς, καὶ οἰκοδομήσεις οἶκον κυρίῳ τῷ Θεῷ σου]. 1 Chron. 22: 11. Jehovah appeared to Solomon himself and said, etc. And I will hear from heaven, and will be gracious to their sins, and will heal their land [καὶ ἐγὼ εἰσακούσομαι ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἱλεως ἔσομαι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῶν, καὶ ἰάσομαι τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν]. 2 Chron. 7: 12, 14. And I said, I beseech you, Jehovah, God of heaven, etc. Remember, I beg you, the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying: If you transgress, I will scatter you among the peoples [ἐὰν ἀποστρέψητε ὑμεῖς, ἐγὼ ἀποστρέψω ὑμᾶς ἐν τοῖς λαοῖς]; I will gather them and bring them to the place [συναξω αὐτούς, καὶ εἰσαξω αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον]. Neh. 1: 5, 8, 9.

units.la: Pervenimus ad Jobi historiam, ubi Deus de nomine יהוה censetur dumtaxat dum sermones serit cum Satana tentatore, & iterum ad calcem historiae, ubi infinitam majestatem oftensurus Jobum alloquitur è turbine. Sed & ibi gloriofo indigitamento verbum in futuro attexitur. Accinge nunc, sicut vir lumbos tuos אֶשְׁאָלְךָ ερωτήσω σε, interrogabo te. &c. Et ego etiam כִּי־תוֹשִׁיעַ εγώ ομολογήσω, fatebor tibi, quod dextra tua servabit te. Job. 40: 2, 9. Dixit יהוה ad Eliphas Themanitem Job servus meus, יִתְפַּלָּל, orabit pro vobis, faciem enim ejus, אֶשָּׂא και ποιήσω καρπωσιν, προσωπον αυτου λήψομαι, suscipiam, Job. 42: 7, 8.
units.tr: We come to the history of Job, where God is named Jehovah only while he speaks with Satan the tempter, and again at the end of the history, where, about to show his infinite majesty, he addresses Job out of the whirlwind. But there too the word in the future is joined to that glorious designation. Gird up now your loins like a man, and I will question you [אשאלך, ἐρωτήσω σε]. And I too [כי־תושיע, ἐγὼ ὁμολογήσω] will confess to you that your right hand will save you. Job 40: 2, 9. Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My servant Job shall pray for you; for I will accept his prayer [יתפלל, ... אשא, καὶ ποιήσω ..., προσωπον αὐτου λήψομαι] and not deal with you according to your folly. Job 42: 7, 8.

units.la: Psalmorum liber innumera fere phraseos exempla suppeditat, nonnulla è multis laudasse sufficiet. ויהי יהוה, & erit יהוה exaltatio pauperi. Psalm. 9: 10. Quia sol & scutum nobis יהוה Deus, gratiam, & gloriam, יִתֵּן יְהוָה לֹא־יִמְנַע טוֹב ώ θεός χάριν και δόξαν δώσει Kύριος σχρήστη &c. dabit יהוה, nec prohibebit bonum. &c. Psalm. 84: 12. Etiam צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ και γάρ ο Kύριος δώσει, Dominus dabit bonum. יְהוָה יִתֵּן הַטּוֹב δικαιοσύνη ενώπιον αυτου περιπατήσει, justitiam ante se ambulare faciet. Psalm. 85: 13, 14. Regnabit Dominus in secula. Psalm. 146: 10. יְמְלֹךְ יְהוָה לְעוֹלָם Вασιλεύσει Kύριος εις τον αιώνα, Regnabit Dominum in secula. כִּי־יְהוָה יְהוָה בִּכְסִלְךָ וְשָׁטַר O' γάρ Kύριος εσται επι πασων οδών σου, και ερεισθει &c. Quia יהוה erit fiducia tua, & custodiet pedem tuum. Prov. 3: 26. לֹא־יַרְעִיב יְהוָה נֶפֶשׁ צַדִּיק και λιμοχονήσει Kύριος ψυχην δικαιου, non sinet esurire יהוה animam justi. הַוַּת רְשָׁעִים יְהַדֹּף Zωλω η δικαιων ανατςειψει, propter pravitatem impios expellet. Prov. 10: 3.
units.tr: The book of Psalms supplies almost countless examples of this phrase; it will suffice to praise a few out of many. And Jehovah will be a refuge for the poor [ויהי יהוה]. Ps. 9: 10. For Jehovah God is a sun and shield to us; the Lord will give grace and glory; he will not withhold good [יתן יהוה, לא־ימנע טוב; ὁ θεὸς χάριν καὶ δόξαν δώσει, Κύριος ..., δώσει, οὐχ ὑστερήσει]. Ps. 84: 12. Yes, the Lord will give what is good [יהוה יתן הטוב; καὶ γὰρ ὁ Κύριος δώσει]. Righteousness will go before him and make his path [צדק לפניו יהלך; δικαιοσύνη ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πορεύσεται]. Ps. 85: 13, 14. Jehovah will reign forever. Ps. 146: 10 [ימלך יהוה לעולם; Βασιλεύσει Κύριος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα]. For Jehovah will be your confidence, and will keep your foot. Prov. 3: 26 [כי־יהוה יהיה בכסלך; ὁ γὰρ Κύριος ἔσται ἐπὶ πασῶν ὁδῶν σου]. Jehovah will not let the soul of the righteous hunger [לא־ירעיב יהוה נפש צדיק; λιμοκτονήσει Κύριος ψυχὴν δικαίου], but he will thrust away the craving of the wicked. Prov. 10: 3 [הות רשעים יהדף; ζωὴν δικαίων ἀνατρέψει].

units.la: Jesaias plenam messem exhibet, spicas aliquot in specimen colligemus, Oculi elati hominis humiliabuntur, & incuruabitur altitudo hominum, לָבֹא וְנִשְׂגַּב יְהוָה לְבַדּוֹ και ύψωθήσεται Kύριος μόνος, exaltabitur יהוה solus in die illa. Jesa. 2: 11. Dies enim יהוה exercituum super omnes cedros Libani, & super omnes quercus Bassan &c. לְכָל־גֵּאֶה וָשָׁפָל και ύψωθήσεται Kύριος Κύριος μόνος. Et exaltabitur יהוה solus in die illa. Jef. 2: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. יהוה צבאות וינבה יהוה ויגא ὑψωθήσεται Κύριος σαβαωθ, Et exaltabitur יהוה exercituum והאל הקדוש בקדש ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἅγιος δοξασθήσεται, & Deus sanctus sanctificabitur in justitia. Jef. 5: 16. יהוה enim judex noster : יהוה legislator noster : יהוה rex noster, יהושענו הוא Κύριος αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς σώσει, ipse salvabit vos. Jef. 33: 22. Ecce dies veniunt dixit יהוה, והקמתי לדוד צמח צדיק, ἀναστήσω τῷ Δαυὶδ ἀνατέλλω δικαίαν, Et suscitabo Davidi germen justum. Jerem. 23: 5. Sic dixit יהוה Deus Israël ושמתי בן אביר, Sic agnoscam transmigrationem Juda. והשבתים, עיני עליהם, ἀποκαταστήσω, ponam oculum meum super eos, & reducam eos in terram hanc. ולא אהרס, οὐ μὴ καθελῶ, Et non destruam אתוש ולא ונטעתים, καταφυτεύσω αὐτας, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκπλύω. Et plantabo eos, & non evellam. Jerem. 24: 6. אתה יהוה לעולם חשב σὺ δὲ κύριε εἰς τῶν αἰῶνα καθηκῆσαι, Tu autem יהוה aeternum permanebis. Lament. 5: 19. Et dic, montes Israël audite verbum Domini יהוה : sic dixit Dominus יהיה montibus & collibus, torrentibus, & vallibus, ecce ego adduco super vos gladium, ואביאתי ἐξολοθρεύσω τὴν, Et perdam excelsa vestra, והפלחי καταβαλῶ, & cadere faciam interfectos vestros coram idolis vestris. ונתתי δώσω, & dabo cadavera filiorum Israël והריתי ἀλασκορπῶ, & dispergam ossa vestra circum aras vestras. Ezech. 6, 3, 4, 5. Propterea sic dicit Dominus יהוה gladium metuistis ורב אביא ῥομφαίαν ἐπάξω, & gladium inducam super vos, dixit Dominus יהוה, והוצאתי ἐξάξω, & educam vos de medio ejus. ונתתי ועשיתי ποιήσω tradam vos in manum alienorum. & faciam in vobis judicia. Propterea dic, sic dixit Dominus יהוה, Etiam si procul ejecerim eos in gentes, & disperserim eos per terras מעט למקדש ואהי להם, ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς εἰς ἁγίασμα μικρὸν. Ero eis in sanctuarium parvum Ezech. 11: 8, 9, 16. Et dic terra Israël, sic dixit יהוה, ecce ego ad te והוצאתי והכרתי ἐκσπάσω, & educam gladium meum è vagina sua ἐξολοθρεύσω, & occidam ex te justum & impium. Ezech. 21: 3.
units.tr: Isaiah offers a full harvest; let us gather a few ears as a sample. The lofty looks of man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, [Heb. לָבֹא וְנִשְׂגַּב יְהוָה לְבַדּוֹ] [Gk. και ύψωθήσεται Kύριος μόνος] and the LORD alone shall be exalted [Heb. יהוה] in that day. Isa. 2:11. For the day of the LORD of hosts shall come upon all that is proud and lofty, [Heb. לְכָל־גֵּאֶה וָשָׁפָל] [Gk. και ύψωθήσεται Kύριος] upon all the cedars of Lebanon and all the oaks of Bashan, and so on. The LORD alone shall be exalted in that day. Isa. 2:12–17. [Heb. יהוה צבאות וינבה יהוה ויגא] [Gk. ὑψωθήσεται Κύριος σαβαωθ] And the LORD of hosts shall be exalted, [Heb. והאל הקדוש בקדש] [Gk. ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ἅγιος δοξασθήσεται] and the holy God shall be sanctified in righteousness. Isa. 5:16. For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; [Heb. יהושענו הוא] [Gk. Κύριος αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς σώσει] he himself will save us. Isa. 33:22. Behold, the days come, says the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous branch [Heb. והקמתי לדוד צמח צדיק] [Gk. ἀναστήσω τῷ Δαυὶδ ἀνατέλλω δικαίαν], and I will raise up for David a righteous offshoot. Jer. 23:5. Thus says the LORD God of Israel: [Heb. ושמתי בן אביר] "Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge the exiles of Judah"; [Heb. והשבתים, עיני עליהם] [Gk. ἀποκαταστήσω, ponam oculum meum super eos], I will set my eyes upon them for good, and bring them back to this land; [Heb. ולא אהרס] [Gk. οὐ μὴ καθελῶ] I will build them and not pull them down; [Heb. ונטעתים] [Gk. καταφυτεύσω αὐτας, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐκπλύω] I will plant them and not uproot them. Jer. 24:6. [Heb. אתה יהוה לעולם חשב] [Gk. σὺ δὲ κύριε εἰς τῶν αἰῶνα καθηκῆσαι] But you, O LORD, remain for ever. Lam. 5:19. Say also: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD; thus says the Lord GOD to the mountains and hills, to the watercourses and valleys: Behold, I bring a sword upon you, [Heb. ואביאתי] [Gk. ἐξολοθρεύσω τὴν] and I will destroy your high places, [Heb. והפלחי] [Gk. καταβαλῶ] and I will make your slain fall before your idols. [Heb. ונתתי] [Gk. δώσω] I will lay the dead bodies of the children of Israel [Heb. והריתי] [Gk. ἀλασκορπῶ] and scatter your bones around your altars. Ezek. 6:3–5. Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: You feared the sword, [Heb. ורב אביא] [Gk. ῥομφαίαν ἐπάξω] and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord GOD; [Heb. והוצאתי] [Gk. ἐξάξω] I will bring you out from the midst of it; [Heb. ונתתי ועשיתי] [Gk. ποιήσω] I will deliver you into the hands of strangers, and execute judgments upon you. Therefore say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Although I have removed them far away among the nations and scattered them through the lands, [Heb. מעט למקדש ואהי להם] [Gk. ἔσομαι αὐτοῖς εἰς ἁγίασμα μικρὸν] yet I will be to them a little sanctuary. Ezek. 11:8, 9, 16. And say to the land of Israel, thus says the LORD: Behold, I am against you, [Heb. והוצאתי והכרתי] [Gk. ἐκσπάσω] and I will draw my sword from its sheath, [Gk. ἐξολοθρεύσω] and I will cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked. Ezek. 21:3.

units.la: Posteriores Prophetæ verba in futurum prospicientia nomini יהוה non secus atque priores attexere solent. ארחם והושעתים ביהוה אלהיהם τὰς δὲ υἱὰς Ἰουδὰ ἐλεήσω, καὶ σώσω αὐτὰς ἐν κυρίῳ Θεῷ αὐτῶν. Et domus Jehuda miserebor, & salvabo eos in יהוה Deo suo. ואני לא־אהיה לכם Et ego non ero vester. Hos. 1: 7, 9. אושיבך באהלים, ἐπ’ κατοικιῶ σε ἐν σκηναῖς. γωῆς. Ego autem יהוה Deus tuus ex terra Ægypti adhuc habitare faciam te in tabernaculis. Hos. 12: 9. ארפת משובתם אהבם ברכה Ἰάσομαι τὰς κατοικίας αὐτῶν, ἀγαπήσω αὐτούς. Sanabo rebellionem eorum, diligam eos spontanee אהיה כאל לישראל ἐσομαι ὡς δρόσος τῷ Ισραὴλ, Ero tanquam ros Israël. Hos. 14: 5, 6. ויהוה מציון ישאג ὁ δὲ κύριος ἐκ Σιὼν ἀναφωνήσει. Et יהוה de Sion rugiet. ומירושלים יתן קולו ἐκ Ἱερουσαλὴμ δώσει φωνὴν αὐτοῦ, Et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam. Joël. 3. 16. Audite verbum hoc, quod locutus est יהוה contra vos, filii Israël, על־כן אפקד עליכם ταῦτα ἐκδικήσω ἐφ' ὑμᾶς. Idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras. Amos 3: 1. 2. ויהיר־כן יהוה אלהי צבאות, ἢ ἔσται μεθ' ὑμῶν κύριος. Sic enim erit יהוה Deus exercituum vobiscum. Amos. 5: 14. Et erit in illa dixit Dominus יהוה והבאתי השמש בצהרים והחשכתי לארץ, δύσεται ὁ ἥλιος μεσημβρίας, καὶ συσκοτάσει. Occumbere faciam solem in ipso meridie, & tenebras obruam terram. והפכתי חגיכם לאבל μεταστρέψω τὰς ἑορτὰς ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος. Et convertam festivitates vestras in luctum. Ecce dies veniunt dixit Dominus יהוה והשלחתי רעב בארץ ἐξαποστελῶ λιμὸν τῷ γῇ. Et mittam famem in terram. Amos 8: 9, 10, 11. Annon in die illa dixit יהוה והאבדתי חכמים מאדום, perdam sapientes ex Edom. והיתה ליהוה המלוכה ἡ βασιλεία. Eritque ipsi יהוה regnum. Abdi. 8: 21. In die illa dixit יהוה, אספה, συνάξω, Congregabo claudicantem, & ejectam, אקבצה, εἰσδέξομαι, colligam. וישמתי, ἀπωσομαι, & ponam claudicantem. &c. ומלך יהוה βασιλεύσει κύριος, & regnabit יהוה Mich. 4: 6, 7. Ecce ego ad te, dixit יהוה exercituum והראיתי, ἀποκαλύψω, & revelabo fimbrias tuas in facie tua. והשלכתי, ἐπιρρίψω & projiciam super te abominationes. ונבלתיך ושמתיך, ἀνομαί σε εἰς δέγμα. Et contumelis te afficiam, & ponam te tanquam inquinamentum. Nahum. 3: 5, 6. Nonne fuisti ab initio יהוה Deus meus, sancte meus? לא נמות יהוה, οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνωμεν, non moriemur יהוה. Habac. 1: 12. ואנו ביהוה אגילה באלהי ישעי, Ἐγὼ δὲ ἐν τῷ κυρίῳ ἀγαλλιάσομαι, ἀγαλλιάσομαι τῷ Θεῷ τῷ σωτῆρί μου. Ego autem in יהוה exultabo, & laetabor in Deo salvatore meo. Habac. 3: 18. Rex Israël יהוה in medio tui. לא־תראי רע עוד, οὐκ ὄψε, κακὰ ἔτι, non videbis malum ultra. יהוה Deus tuus in medio tui, potens יהיש עליך יגיל עליך, ישועה ישיש עליך. σώσει σε ἐπάξει ἐπὶ σε ἀφροσύνῳ, ἢ καινιεῖ σε ἐν τῇ ἀγαπήσει αὐτοῦ, ἢ ἀφεγν-
units.tr: The later prophets, too, when they look forward to the future, are accustomed to join the name of the LORD just as the earlier ones did. [Heb. ארחם והושעתים ביהוה אלהיהם] [Gk. τὰς δὲ υἱὰς Ἰουδὰ ἐλεήσω, καὶ σώσω αὐτὰς ἐν κυρίῳ Θεῷ αὐτῶν] "I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God"; [Heb. ואני לא־אהיה לכם] "and I will not be your God." Hos. 1:7, 9. [Heb. אושיבך באהלים] [Gk. ἐπ’ κατοικιῶ σε ἐν σκηναῖς] "But I, the LORD your God from the land of Egypt, will yet make you dwell in tents." Hos. 12:9. [Heb. ארפת משובתם אהבם ברכה] [Gk. Ἰάσομαι τὰς κατοικίας αὐτῶν, ἀγαπήσω αὐτούς] "I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely; [Heb. אהיה כאל לישראל] [Gk. ἐσομαι ὡς δρόσος τῷ Ισραὴλ] I will be as the dew to Israel." Hos. 14:5, 6. [Heb. ויהוה מציון ישאג] [Gk. ὁ δὲ κύριος ἐκ Σιὼν ἀναφωνήσει] "The LORD will roar from Zion, [Heb. ומירושלים יתן קולו] [Gk. ἐκ Ἱερουσαλὴμ δώσει φωνὴν αὐτοῦ] and utter his voice from Jerusalem." Joel 3:16. "Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel; [Heb. על־כן אפקד עליכם] [Gk. ταῦτα ἐκδικήσω ἐφ' ὑμᾶς] therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities."
